英文原文

Hey everyone!

A toner probe is a tool used to identify and trace cables when you do not know where they go.

It is extremely common to open a wiring closet,look at a patch panel full of unlabeled cables and need to figure out which cable corresponds to a specific wall jack or room.

A toner kit is usually two parts,a tone generator that connects to one end of the cable and sends a signal and a probe wand that detects that signal at the other end.

For A plus troubleshooting,this tool shows up in scenarios like find the cable for Office 205,identify which patch panel port belongs to this wall jack or trace which cable in this bundle is the correct run.

The tone generator connects to a cable using an RJ45 jack,alligator clips or other adapters and it injects a tone signal into the cable.

The probe is a handheld wand with a speaker and it detects the tone through the cable jacket using inductive pickup,meaning you do not need to strip wires or touch bare copper.

As you move the probe near the correct cable,the tone becomes louder or clearer.

This is why you can scan across a bundle and identify the one cable that screams the loudest.The exam takeaway is that toning is a tracing method,not a data test.

So it is for identification and mapping,not performance validation.

The workflow is straightforward.

You connect the tone generator to the known end like a wall jack in an office and turn it on.

Then you go to the wiring closet and use the probe across the patch panel and cable bundles until you find the strongest tone.

Once you identify the matching cable,you label it immediately,ideally on both ends,so you do not have to repeat the tracing later.

This is also a key professional habit because labeling saves hours over time.

After identification,a best practice is to verify the cable with a cable tester because a cable can be correctly identified and still be faulty.

Basic toner kits are inexpensive and usually good enough for occasional tracing.

Mid-range kits add useful options like adjustable probe volume,different tone patterns so you can distinguish multiple cables and better sensitivity in dense bundles.

Higher end tools may include additional testing functions like continuity checks,wire map hints or stronger signal generation for more challenging environments.

For the exam,the important point is not the brand but the capability.

Tone generator sends,probe detects and it helps you identify unknown cables quickly.

Toners are not perfect for every situation.

They cannot trace fiber optic cable because fiber does not carry electrical tone signals.

So fiber requires optical tools instead.

Very long runs can weaken the tone,and heavily shielded cable can reduce how easily the probe detects the signal,because shielding blocks some electromagnetic leakage.

Areas with high electrical noise can also make tone detection harder.

A technician workaround is using a more sensitive probe,lowering probe volume to reduce overload,or tracing in smaller sections of the bundle rather than sweeping across everything at once.

Label as soon as you find a cable because the whole point is saving future time.

Keep spare batteries because weak batteries are a common reason a toner seems to not work.

If tracing multiple cables,do them one at a time or use different tone patterns if your kit supports it.

Otherwise,you can confuse yourself in a busy closet.

If you identify a cable,test it after,because a correct trace does not guarantee correct wiring or continuity.

Also,be careful around active circuits because some tone generators are not designed to be used on live network links.

So,in professional environments,you usually tone disconnected cable runs.

Toner probes help you trace and identify cables by sending a tone on one end and detecting it with a probe wand on the other end.

This is essential when cables are unlabeled or when you need to map a wall jack to a patch panel port.

The probe detects the signal through the cable jacket,making it quick and safe to scan bundles and panels.

Toners are for identification and tracing,not for certifying cable quality,so it is best practice to test the cable after you find it.

Fiber cannot be toned the same way because it is not electrical,so that is a key limitation to remember.

106. 打线刀

大家好！

打线工具是您用于将网络线缆端接到配线架、拱心石墙壁插座和打线块上的工具。

与将R J四十五插头压接到线缆末端不同，打线端接是将每根单独的导体压入带有金属齿的槽中。

这些金属齿会刺破绝缘层并抓住铜线，从而形成牢固的电气连接，旨在保持多年可靠。

这就是为什么打线端接是结构化布线的标准，因为它们具有一致性、安全性且专业。

打线工具看起来像一把粗大的螺丝刀，当您按下时，它会在一个动作中将导线就位并剪掉多余的导线。

存在多种打线标准，该工具通常支持针对不同线块的不同刀片。

对于网络而言，最常见的是一一零型，这是您在大多数配线架和墙壁插座背面看到的类型。

您可能还听说过克罗内块，它采用不同的机械设计，在某些电信环境中更为常见。

另一种较旧的样式是六十六块，它主要与电话系统相关，而非以太网。

就A Plus考试而言，高收益点是以太网结构化布线最常见的是端接在一一零型线块上，而打线工具通常配备一一零型和克罗内型刀片。

要打线一根线缆，首先使用剥线器从末端剥去约一到两英寸的外皮。

然后分开四对双绞线，并按照插座或配线架上的颜色代码，遵循T五六八A或T五六八B标准。

目标是尽可能让双绞线靠近端接点，因为解开过多会降低性能。

将每根导体放入正确的槽中，并在槽外留出少量多余导线。

然后保持打线工具垂直于线块并笔直向下用力按压。

当您按下时，工具会将导体强制压入槽中。

金属触点刺破绝缘层以接触铜线，而切割刃则会干净地剪掉多余的导体。

许多人记得这个工具，因为当端接正确就位时，您可以感觉到并听到一声独特的咔哒声。

一旦导线就位，它应完全坐落在槽中，且切割端应干净，无毛刺。

这就是为什么当操作正确时，打线端接被视为“设置后即忘”的连接。

恰当的技术是防止难以发现的间歇性问题的关键。

尽可能保持线对的绞合状态，仅解开到达每个槽所需的最小长度。

将线缆外皮固定在靠近端接点的位置，以便线缆获得应力释放，导体不会承受机械应力。

垂直向下按压而不是倾斜按压，以确保导体完全落入槽中。

针对线块类型使用正确的刀片，因为不匹配可能会损坏端接点并导致接触不可靠。

端接后，目视检查所有八根导体，然后测试线路，因为不良的打线端接可能在几天后表现为随机的网络问题。

打线工具有冲击式和非冲击式两种风格。

冲击式工具内部有一个弹簧，可积蓄张力然后突然释放，以一致的力将刀片向下驱动。

这种一致的力就是冲击式工具成为专业安装首选的原因，因为它们能可靠地将导体就位并干净地切割。

非冲击式工具依赖稳定的手部压力，虽然也能工作，但更依赖用户，如果您疲劳或匆忙，可能会导致就位不一致。

在成本预期方面，非冲击式工具的价格通常在十五到三十美元之间，而冲击式工具的价格通常在三十到一百美元左右，具体取决于制造质量和包含的刀片。

打线错误是可以预见的。

如果您遵循了错误的颜色代码，或不一致地混合了T五六八A和T五六八B，连接将会失败或表现异常。

如果您解开过多，线缆可能仍然能链路连通，但性能不佳，特别是在您期望千兆速度时。

如果导线未完全就位，您经常会遇到间歇性掉线，这很难诊断，因为它们时有时无。

如果您使用了错误的刀片，可能会损坏线块，最终导致端接不可靠，即使线序是正确的。

如果外皮留得太靠后，导体随着时间的推移可能会被拉扯或承受压力。

考试要点是，干净的端接技术可以预防那些最浪费故障排除时间的间歇性问题。

打线工具用于通过将每根导体座入绝缘位移槽中，将以太网线缆端接到配线架和墙壁插座上。

一一零型线块在网络布线中最为常见，冲击式打线工具通常是首选，因为它们能创建一致且可靠的端接。

良好的技术侧重于让双绞线靠近端接点、使用正确的刀片垂直向下按压、将外皮靠近以实现应力释放，并在完成后测试线路。

接下来，我们将转向线缆测试仪，它用于验证您压接或打线的线缆是否实际上接线正确且工作正常。

英文原文

Hey everyone!

A punch down tool is what you use to terminate network cables onto patch panels,keystone wall jacks and punch down blocks.

Instead of crimping an RJ forty-five plug onto the end of the cable,punch down termination presses each individual conductor into a slot that has metal teeth.

Those teeth cut through the insulation and grab the copper,creating a solid electrical connection that is designed to stay reliable for years.

This is why punchdowns are the standard in structured cabling because they are consistent,secure and professional.

The punch down tool looks like a chunky screwdriver and when you press down it seats the wire and trims the extra wire in one motion.

There are multiple punch down standards and the tool often supports different blades for different blocks.

For networking the most common is the one one zero style which is what you see on the back of most patch panels and wall jacks.

You may also hear about crony blocks which use a different mechanical design and are more common in some telecom environments.

Another older style is the 66 block which is mostly associated with phone systems rather than Ethernet.

For A plus exam purposes the high yield point is that Ethernet structured cabling is most commonly terminated on 110 style blocks and punch down tools often come with one one zero and crony blades.

To punch down a cable you start by stripping about one to two inches of jacket off the end using a cable stripper.

Then you separate the four twisted pairs and follow the color code on the jack or patch panel using either T568A or T568B.

The goal is to keep the twists as close to the termination as possible because untwisting too far can reduce performance.

Place each conductor into the correct slot leaving a small amount of extra wire beyond the slot.

Then hold the punch down tool straight and perpendicular to the block and press down firmly.

When you press down the tool forces the conductor into the slot.

The metal contacts pierce the insulation to touch copper and the cutting edge trims off the excess conductor cleanly.

Many people remember this tool because you can feel and hear a distinct click when the termination seats properly.

Once a wire is seated,it should sit fully down in the slot and the cut end should be clean,not frayed.

This is why punch downs are considered set it and forget it connections when done correctly.

Proper technique is what prevents hard to find intermittent issues.

Keep pair twists intact as long as possible and only untwist the minimum needed to reach each slot.

Seat the cable jacket close to the termination point so the cable has strain relief and the conductors are not carrying mechanical stress.

Press straight down rather than at an angle,so the conductor lands fully in the slot.

Use the correct blade for the block type because a mismatch can damage the termination point and create unreliable contact.

After termination,visually inspect all eight conductors and then test the run because a bad punch down can look like a random network problem days later.

Punch down tools come in impact and non-impact styles.

Impact tools have an internal spring that builds tension and then snaps,driving the blade down with a consistent force.

That consistent force is why impact tools are preferred for professional installations because they seat conductors reliably and cut cleanly.

Non-impact tools rely on steady hand pressure which can work but is more dependent on the user and can lead to inconsistent seating if you're tired or rushing.

In terms of cost expectations,non-impact tools often fall around$15 to$30 while impact tools are commonly around$30 to$100 depending on build quality and included blades.

Punch down mistakes are predictable.

If you follow the wrong color code or mix T five six eight A and T five six eight B inconsistently,the connection will fail or behave strangely.

If you untwist too far,the cable may still link up but perform poorly,especially when you expect gigabit speeds.

If wires are not fully seated,you often get intermittent drops that are painful to diagnose because they come and go.

If you use the wrong blade,you can damage the block and end up with an unreliable termination even if the wire order is correct.

And if the jacket is left too far back,the conductors can get pulled or stressed over time.

The exam takeaway is that clean termination technique prevents intermittent problems that waste the most troubleshooting time.

Punch down tools are used to terminate Ethernet cable onto patch panels and wall jacks by seating each conductor into an insulation displacement slot.

One one zero blocks are the most common for network cabling and impact punch down tools are generally preferred because they create consistent reliable terminations.

Good technique focuses on keeping twists close to the termination,pressing straight down with the right blade,keeping the jacket close for strain relief and testing the run after completion.

Next we move to cable testers which verify whether your crimped or punched down cable is actually wired correctly and working.

107. 网线测试仪

大家好！

线缆测试仪是您用来证明网络线缆接线正确且电气性能良好的工具。

您无法仅通过观察来可靠地判断线缆状况，因为导体可能顺序错误、开路、短路或在连接器内部仅部分连接。

在您自行压接线缆或端接永久性线路后，线缆测试仪必不可少，它们也非常适用于故障排除，因为线缆会因弯曲、门夹、连接器应力和日常磨损而损坏。

基础测试仪的价格通常在十五到五十美元之间，而验证完整类别性能的专业认证仪可能耗资数千美元。

但对于A Plus故障排除，您主要需要了解基础测试仪检查的内容以及如何解读结果。

在基础层面上，测试仪检查连通性和线序图，这意味着一端的每个引脚都应连接到另一端正确的引脚。

它们可以识别开路，即导体断裂或未接触，以及短路，即不应接触的导体相互接触。

许多测试仪还能指示线对交叉或导体互换，这通常源于压接或打线时的线序错误。

一个关键的考试概念是分裂线对，这种情况下线缆看似能进行基本连接，但性能不佳，因为双绞线关系未保持正确，这会增加串扰并降低高速可靠性。

大多数基础线缆测试仪都有一个主机和一个远端机。

您将线缆的一端插入主机，另一端插入远端机，然后开始测试。测试仪向每根导体发送信号，并以编号指示灯或小显示屏的形式显示结果。

接线正确的线缆通常在两端都显示干净的一到八序列，这表明导体已连接且映射正确。

整个测试仅需几秒钟，这使得它成为您在归咎于交换机、驱动程序或网络设置之前所能执行的最快故障排除步骤之一。

如果数字显示顺序错乱，表明导线被互换或交叉，这通常指向端接线序不正确。

如果某个数字完全缺失，则该导体开路，意味着它在连接器或打线点内部断裂或未接触。

如果多个数字同时亮起或表现异常，这可能表明存在短路，通常由绝缘层损坏或连接器问题引起。

如果线缆通过测试但用户在更高速度下仍性能不佳，分裂线对或端接点附近过度解开可能是隐蔽原因，特别是在理应支持千兆连接的线路上。

专业认证工具超越了简单的连通性检查，它们测量线缆是否符合类别性能要求。

它们可以测量长度、衰减和串扰特性，并确定该线路是否真正符合预期速度的五类增强版、六类或六类增强版标准。

这些工具价格昂贵，因为它们测试高频下的信号行为并生成文档报告。

对于A Plus考试，您主要需要理解基础测试仪检查接线正确性，而认证仪验证性能合规性，后者通常是专业结构化布线工作所要求的。

线缆测试仪适用于跳线、永久性安装线路以及排查神秘的掉线问题。

一个明智的工作流程是在安装前测试线缆，在端接后测试，并在用户报告问题时再次测试，因为排除线缆故障比追踪软件原因要快得多。

对于长距离线路，在将线缆穿过墙壁或天花板前后进行测试也很有用，因为如果弯曲过急或拉扯过猛，拉线过程可能会损坏线缆。

考试思维是尽早排除最简单的物理原因，因为糟糕的布线可能模仿更高级别的网络问题。

线缆测试仪通过检查连通性、线序图、开路、短路以及在许多情况下的分裂线对问题，来验证网络线缆是否接线正确。

基础测试仪价格低廉且快速，非常适合验证压接跳线、打线线路以及排查故障。

专业认证仪价格较高，用于证明线缆符合类别标准和性能要求。

如果您先进行测试，就可以避免浪费时间去排查看似是网络配置问题而实则是端接不良或线缆损坏的情况。

接下来，我们将转向环回插头，它通过让设备向自身发送数据来帮助您测试网络端口。

英文原文

Hey everyone!

A cable tester is how you prove a network cable is wired correctly and electrically sound.

You cannot reliably judge a cable by looking at it because a conductor can be out of order,open,shorted or only partially connected inside a connector.

Cable testers are essential after you crimp your own cables or punch down a permanent run and they are also great for troubleshooting because cables get damaged by bends,door pinches,connector stress and general wear.

Basic testers are commonly in the$15 to$50 range while professional certifiers that validate full category performance can cost thousands.

But for A plus troubleshooting,you mainly need to understand what basic testers check and how to interpret results.

At a basic level,testers check continuity and wire map,meaning each pin on one end should connect to the correct pin on the other end.

They can identify opens where a conductor is broken or not making contact and shots where conductors touch when they should not.

Many testers can also indicate crossed pairs or swapped conductors,which commonly comes from a wiring order mistake at a crimp or punch down.

A key exam concept is split pairs,where the cable might appear to work for basic connectivity but performs poorly because the twisted pair relationships were not kept correct,which can increase crosstalk and reduce high speed reliability.

Most basic cable testers have a main unit and a remote unit.

You plug one end of the cable into the main unit and the other end into the remote,then start the test.The tester sends signals down each conductor and displays the results as numbered lights or a small display.

A correctly wired cable typically shows a clean 1 through 8 sequence on both ends which tells you the conductors are connected and mapped correctly.

The whole test takes only a few seconds which makes it one of the fastest troubleshooting steps you can do before you start blaming switches,drivers or network settings.

If the numbers show out of order that indicates wires are swapped or crossed which usually points back to an incorrect termination order.

If a number is missing entirely that conductor is open meaning it is broken or not making contact inside the connector or punch down.

If multiple numbers light at the same time or behave strangely that can indicate a shot often caused by damaged insulation or a connector problem.

If the cable passes but users still have poor performance at higher speeds split pairs or excessive untwisting near terminations can be the hidden cause especially on runs that are supposed to support gigabit connections.

Professional certification tools go beyond simple continuity by measuring whether the cable meets category performance requirements.

They can measure length,attenuation and crosstalk characteristics and determine whether the run truly qualifies as CAT5E,CAT6 or CAT6A for the intended speed.

These tools are expensive because they test signal behavior at high frequencies and generate reports for documentation.

For A,you mainly need to understand that a basic tester checks wiring correctness while a certifier validates performance compliance which is often required for professional structured cabling jobs.

Cable testers are useful for patch cables,for permanent involved runs and for troubleshooting mysterious drops.

A smart workflow is to test a cable before you install it,test after you terminate it and test again if a user reports issues because it's faster to rule out the cable than to chase software causes.

For long runs it is also useful to test before and after pulling cable through walls or ceilings because the pulling process can damage cable if it is bent too sharply or pulled too aggressively.

The exam mindset is to eliminate the simplest physical causes early because bad cabling can mimic higher level network problems.

Cable testers verify that network cables are correctly wired by checking continuity,wire mapping,opens,shorts and in many cases split pair issues.

Basic testers are inexpensive and fast making them perfect for validating crimped patch cables,punched down runs and troubleshooting failures.

Professional certifiers are more expensive and are used to prove a cable meets category standards and performance requirements.

If you test first you can avoid wasting time troubleshooting what looks like a network configuration issue when the real problem is simply a bad termination or a damaged cable.

Next we move to loop pack plugs which help you test network ports by making a device send data to itself.

108. 环回插头

大家好！

环回插头是一种简单的诊断工具，它通过将发送路径环回到接收路径来帮助您测试网络端口。

简单来说，它让设备与自己对话。

这非常有用，因为故障排除的关键在于隔离，而环回测试能帮助您确定网络接口是否能够正常发送和接收信号。

如果环回测试成功，端口硬件可能工作正常，您就需要查看其他地方，比如线缆、交换机或网络配置。

如果环回测试失败，端口或适配器可能存在故障。

网络接口拥有发送和接收路径。

通常情况下，一台设备的发送端通过线缆和交换机连接到另一台设备的接收端。

环回插头在插头内部将发送端连接回接收端。

当设备发送测试信号时，它会立即接收到相同的信号，设备从而可以确认发送和接收功能正常。

这就是为什么环回是一种强有力的硬件测试，因为它排除了网络其余部分的干扰，专注于端口本身。

环回插头适用于不同的连接类型。

R J四十五环回插头用于以太网端口。

光纤环回设备通过短的内部光纤路径将发送光纤连接到接收光纤。

在某些环境中，还存在用于传统串行故障排除的串行环回插头。

您还可以看到专为交换机上的小型可插拔端口设计的环回模块。

对于A Plus考试，关键概念不是死记硬背每种变体，而是理解只要有发送和接收路径的地方就存在环回测试，其目标是验证端口的发送和接收能力。

要使用环回插头，您将其连接到待测端口，然后运行设备的诊断程序或环回测试功能（如果可用）。

在许多设备上，您可能会看到链路指示灯亮起，这可以快速表明端口检测到了连接。

关键的故障排除决策基于测试结果。

如果环回成功但设备无法在网络中通信，问题很可能在设备外部，例如线缆、连接的交换机端口或配置。

如果环回持续失败，您应怀疑网络接口硬件、端口或支持该接口的驱动程序及固件层。

制作一个简单的以太网环回插头是可能的，理解这一概念有助于您推理考试题目。

对于旧式的十兆和一百兆以太网，其理念是将发送引脚连接回接收引脚，从而使流量环回。

对于千兆以太网，涉及更多的线对，因此适当的环回需考虑额外的导体。

在实践中，许多技术人员购买廉价成品环回插头，因为目标是可靠的诊断，而非完美的DIY项目。

但考试技能在于理解该插头是将发送线路接回接收线路，以验证端口功能。

当您需要将硬件故障与外部原因区分开来时，环回测试非常有用。

如果用户无法连接且您怀疑计算机上的网络插座已损坏，环回测试有助于确认端口是否存活。

如果交换机端口看似有问题，环回测试可以帮助检验该端口是否能建立链路并通过本地测试。环回测试还适用于在部署前验证设备，因为在实验台上发现坏端口比在安装后才发现要容易得多。

在间歇性故障的情况下，重复进行环回测试有助于揭示不稳定的硬件行为。

环回插头通过将发送路径环回到接收路径来测试网络端口，使设备能够验证其是否能正确发送和接收信号。

如果环回成功，端口可能功能正常，接下来您应排查线缆、交换机或配置。

如果环回失败，您应怀疑端口、适配器或支持的驱动程序及固件。

环回插头适用于以太网、光纤和其他接口，它们是一种无需在线缆另一端使用第二台设备即可快速隔离问题的方法。

英文原文

Hey everyone!

A loopback plug is a simple diagnostic tool that helps you test a network port by looping the transmit path back into the receive path.

In plain terms,it makes a device talk to itself.

This is useful because troubleshooting is about isolation and a loopback test helps you determine whether the network interface is capable of sending and receiving signals properly.

If a loopback test succeeds,the port hardware is likely working and you look elsewhere,like the cable,the switch or network configuration.

If a loopback test fails,the port or adapter may be faulty.

Network interfaces have transmit and receive paths.

Normally,transmit on one device connects to receive on the other device through a cable and switch.

A loopback plug connects transmit back to receive inside the plug itself.

When the device sends out a test signal,it immediately receives that same signal back and the device can confirm that sending and receiving are functioning.

This is why loopback is a strong hardware test because it removes the rest of the network from the equation and focuses on the port itself.

Loopback plugs exist for different connection types.

RJ45 loopback plugs are used for Ethernet ports.

Fiber loopback devices connect transmit fiber to receive fiber with a short internal fiber path.

Serial loopbacks exist for legacy serial troubleshooting in some environments.

You can also see loopback modules designed for SFP ports on switches.

For A Plus,the key concept is not memorizing every variant but understanding that loopbacks exist wherever there is a transmit and receive path and the goal is to validate the port's ability to send and receive.

To use a loopback plug,you connect it to the port under test and then run the device's diagnostics or a loopback test function if available.

On many devices you may see link lights come on which can be a quick indicator that the port detects a connection.

The key troubleshooting decision is based on results.

If loopback succeeds but the device cannot communicate on the network,the issue is likely outside the device such as cabling,the connected switch port or configuration.

If loopback fails consistently,you suspect the network interface hardware,the port or the driver and firmware layer supporting that interface.

It is possible to make a simple Ethernet loopback plug and understanding the concept helps you reason about exam questions.

For older 10 and 100 megabit Ethernet,the idea is connecting transmit pins back to receive pins so traffic loops.

For gigabit,more pairs are involved so a proper loopback accounts for additional conductors.

In practice,many technicians purchase inexpensive pre-made loop back plugs because the goal is reliable diagnostics,not a perfect DIY project.

But the exam skill is understanding that the plug is wiring transmit back into receive to validate port functionality.

Loopback testing is useful when you need to separate hardware failure from external causes.

If a user cannot connect and you suspect a dead network jack on the computer,loopback helps confirm whether the port is alive.

If a switch port seems bad,loopback can help test whether the port can link and pass a local test.Loopback is also useful for validating equipment before deployment,because discovering a bad port on the bench is much easier than discovering it after installation.

In intermittent cases,repeating loopback tests can help reveal flaky hardware behavior.

Loopback plugs test network ports by looping transmit back into receive so the device can verify it can send and receive signals correctly.

If loopback succeeds,the port is likely functional and you troubleshoot the cable,switch or configuration next.

If loopback fails,you suspect the port,the adapter or supporting driver and firmware.

Loopback plugs exist for Ethernet,fiber and other interfaces and they are a fast way to isolate problems without needing a second device on the other end of the cable.

109. LCD 技术与背光

大家好，欢迎进入这个新章节，我们将深入探讨显示技术。

今天我们从液晶显示器开始讲起，它的全称是液晶显示屏。

几十年来，这一直是计算机显示器和笔记本电脑屏幕背后的主力技术。

核心理念是液晶显示器自身不发光，因此显示屏必须控制来自其他光源的光线。

一旦您理解了背光这一概念，无论是在A Plus考试还是实际支持工作中，您都能更快地排除屏幕过暗等常见问题。

那么液晶究竟是什么？

可以把它们想象成微小的快门，当电流通过时会发生扭转。

在一种状态下，它们阻挡光线；当施加电压时，它们旋转并允许光线通过。

现在将这一原理扩展到数百万个像素，每个像素控制透过的光量，您就获得了形成图像的能力。

重要的故障排除要点是，液晶层是在控制光线，而非产生光线。

因此，如果光源发生故障，图像在技术上仍然存在，但会太暗而无法正常看到。

液晶面板是由多层协同工作的堆叠结构。

其中包括偏振滤光片、液晶层、用于生成颜色的红绿蓝彩色滤光片，以及管理每个像素的薄膜晶体管控制器。

所有这些都像一个高度受控的光墙系统，但它们都不产生光线。

这就是为什么每个液晶显示器都需要面板后方的背光。

如果背光缺失或发生故障，像素仍然可以变化，但您无法获得可用的图像亮度。

较旧的液晶显示器使用冷阴极荧光灯背光。

这些是安装在屏幕后方的细荧光灯管，其概念类似于旧式的办公室荧光照明。

冷阴极荧光灯背光往往消耗更多电力，产生更多热量，并且需要一点时间才能达到全亮度。

它们还含有汞，这对安全处置很重要。

从故障排除的角度来看，基于冷阴极荧光灯的笔记本电脑屏幕还与逆变器问题相关，因为逆变器提供驱动灯管所需的电压。

现代液晶显示器主要使用发光二极管背光。

发光二极管更节能，运行温度更低，瞬间开启，并且通常比冷阴极荧光灯寿命更长。

一个考试陷阱是营销术语，因为当人们说发光二极管显示器时，他们通常指的是使用发光二极管背光的液晶面板。

显示屏的核心仍然是液晶，只是背光技术发生了变化。

即使在发光二极管背光中，布局也很重要。

侧入式设计将发光二极管放置在边缘，并使用扩散板将光线散布到整个屏幕，这有助于制造更薄的显示器，但可能导致亮度不均匀。

直入式设计将发光二极管布置在整个背板上，以实现更均匀的照明。

带有局部调光的全阵列是高端方案，其中背光被划分为可独立调光的区域，从而改善对比度，使黑暗场景看起来更暗，而明亮区域保持明亮。

例如在推理题中，这有助于解释为什么两个发光二极管背光显示器在对比度和均匀性上看起来可能截然不同。

背光知识对于故障排除非常实用。

如果笔记本电脑屏幕极暗，但您能隐约看到图像，液晶面板通常仍在工作，问题很可能出在背光系统上。

一个经典的测试是用手电筒以一定角度照射屏幕。

因为如果您能隐约看到桌面或登录屏幕，说明图像生成正常，故障在于光源。

这在带有冷阴极荧光灯背光的旧系统上尤为常见，逆变器或灯管本身可能会发生故障，使屏幕看似损坏，实则不然。

以上就是液晶显示技术的概要。

液晶控制透光量，但它们需要背光才能使图像可见。

冷阴极荧光灯是较旧的背光方法。

发光二极管是现代方法，而发光二极管的排列方式（如侧入式、直入式或全阵列）会改变质量和对比度。如果您记住手电筒测试的概念，就可以快速区分背光问题与真正的面板故障。

接下来，我们将转向面板类型，首先从平面转换技术开始。

英文原文

Hey there,welcome to the new section where we are diving into display technology.

Today we are starting with LCD,which stands for liquid crystal display.

And this has been the workhorse technology behind computer monitors and laptop screens for decades.

The key idea is that LCDs do not create light on their own,so the display has to control light coming from another source.

Once you understand that one concept,backlighting,you can troubleshoot common screen is dim problems a lot faster on both the A exam and in real support work.

So what exactly are liquid crystals?

Think of them as tiny shutters that can twist when electricity flows through them.

In one state,they block light and when voltage is applied,they rotate and allow light to pass.

Now scale that up to millions of pixels,each one controlling how much light comes through and you get the ability to form an image.

The important troubleshooting takeaway is that the liquid crystal layer is controlling light,not generating it.

So if the light source fails,you can still have an image that is technically there but it is too dark to see normally.

An L C D panel is a stack of layers working together.

You have polarizing filters,the liquid crystal layer,red,green and blue color filters to create color and thin film transistor controls that manage each pixel.

All of that acts like a highly controlled light wall system but none of it produces light.

That is why every L C D needs a bat light behind the panel.

If the bat light is missing or failing the pixels can still change but you will not get a usable image brightness.

Older L C D displays used CCFL backlighting which stands for cold cathode fluorescent lamp.

These are thin fluorescent tubes mounted behind the screen similar in concept to older office fluorescent lighting.

CCFL backlights tend to use more power,generate more heat and they can take a moment to reach full brightness.

They also contain mercury which matters for safe disposal.

From a troubleshooting perspective,CCFL based laptop screens are also associated with inverter issues because the inverter provides the voltage needed to drive the lamp.

Modern L C D's primarily use LED backlighting where LED stands for light emitting diode.

LEDs are more energy efficient,run cooler,turn on instantly and generally last longer than CCFL.

One exam trap is marketing language because when someone says LED monitor they usually mean an L C D panel that uses LED backlighting.

The display is still an L C D at its core but the batlight technology changed.

Even within LED backlighting the layout matters.

Edge lit designs put LEDs along the edges and use a diffuser to spread light across the screen,which helps create thinner displays but can cause uneven brightness.

Direct lit puts LEDs across the back panel for more even illumination.

Full array with local dimming is the premium approach where the backlight is divided into zones that can dim independently,improving contrast so dark scenes look darker while bright areas stay bright.

For example reasoning,this helps explain why two LED backlit displays can look very different in contrast and uniformity.

Backlight knowledge is extremely practical for troubleshooting.

If a laptop screen is extremely dim but you can faintly see an image,the L C D panel is usually still working and the problem is likely the backlight system.

A classic test is shining a flashlight at an angle on the screen.

Because if you can see the desktop or login screen faintly,the image generation is fine and the light source is the failure.

This is especially common on older systems with CCFL backlights where the inverter or the lamp itself can fail and make the screen appear dead even though it is not.

So that's L C D technology in a nutshell.

Liquid crystals control how much light passes through but they need a backlight to make the image visible.

CCFL was the older backlight approach.

LED is the modern approach and the LED arrangement like edge lit,direct lit or full array can change quality and contrast.If you remember the flashlight test concept you can quickly separate a backlight problem from a true panel failure.

Next up we'll move into panel types starting with IPS technology.

110. IPS 面板

大家好！

既然我们已经了解了液晶显示器背光的工作原理，接下来聊聊不同的液晶面板类型。

今天我们将重点关注平面转换技术，它被广泛视为许多显示器和移动设备中的高端液晶面板选项。

当您听到平面转换时，请想到两大优势：色彩准确性和可视角度。

这两个特性在购买决策和用户抱怨“从侧面看屏幕效果很差”时经常出现。

平面转换得名于液晶在面板内的旋转方式。

在平面转换面板中，晶体在平面内旋转，意味着平行于屏幕表面旋转，而不是以那种随视角变化而剧烈扭转的方式旋转。

这种设计提高了光线穿过面板时的一致性。

实际上，平面转换能让您在移动头部或多个人同时观看同一屏幕时，保持图像更加稳定。

平面转换面板以色彩还原更一致而闻名，这就是为什么它们深受摄影师、设计师和视频编辑者的喜爱，因为他们关心屏幕上颜色的准确性。

即使对于普通办公用户，更好的色彩一致性也让显示屏看起来更清晰，减少泛白感。

在考试中，请将其视为一种推荐技能。

当用户优先考虑图像质量和色彩时，平面转换通常是比廉价面板类型更安全的选择。

可视角度是平面转换的突出之处。

平面转换面板能在极端角度下保持可用的图像质量，通常描述为水平和垂直方向均可达约一百七十八度。

重点不是将这个数字作为承诺死记硬背，而是理解用户体验。

色彩偏移较少，亮度保持一致，对比度也不像廉价面板类型那样迅速反转。

这就是为什么平面转换非常适合会议中的笔记本电脑、共享观看场景以及屏幕不断倾斜的移动设备。

当多人需要查看同一屏幕时，例如同事在演示期间观看笔记本电脑，平面转换便成为轻松的选择。

当您以奇怪的角度使用设备时，它也很有帮助，比如躺着时在平板电脑上看视频。

在智能手机上，平面转换式的表现非常有价值，因为您会不断移动设备并改变视角，同时仍希望画面看起来一致。

平面转换并非完美，而A Plus考试喜欢考察权衡取舍。

平面转换面板通常价格更高，且响应时间可能比扭曲向列型面板慢。

您常听到的平面转换响应时间范围约为四到八毫秒，这在竞争性游戏中很重要，因为那里存在运动模糊和重影的担忧。

平面转换还可能出现平面转换光晕，这是一种在黑暗场景中看到的与背光相关的光晕，特别是在从角度观看时。

这些缺点有助于您解释为什么电竞玩家可能会选择不同类型的面板，即使平面转换看起来更好看。

另一个权衡是对比度。与垂直排列面板相比，平面转换面板的对比度通常中等。

您常听到的平面转换大致数值约为一千比一，这意味着在黑暗房间中，黑色看起来可能更像灰色，而对比度更强的面板则不会这样。

考试要点是，没有哪种面板类型在所有方面都是最好的，平面转换通常是色彩和角度的最佳平衡，但不一定是深邃黑色的最佳选择。

当用户重视一致的图像质量、准确的色彩和宽广的可视角度时，平面转换是一个强有力的推荐。

它适合内容创作、一般办公工作以及任何需要共享屏幕或从不同位置观看的场景。

平面转换已成为中高端显示器的常见默认选择，特别是当目标是高质量体验而非最低成本或绝对最快的像素响应时。

以上就是平面转换技术的概要。

强大的色彩准确性、卓越的可视角度以及通常较高的图像质量。

同时也要记住权衡取舍，包括更高的成本、出现平面转换光晕的可能性，以及通常在四到八毫秒左右的响应时间。

接下来，我们将看看扭曲向列型面板，它采取了相反的策略，优先考虑速度和affordability而非图像质量。

英文原文

Hey everyone!

Now that we understand how L C D backlighting works,let's talk about different L C D panel types.

Today we are focusing on IPS which stands for In Plane Switching and it is widely viewed as a premium L C D panel option in many monitors and mobile devices.

When you hear IPS,think of two big strengths,color accuracy and viewing angles.

Those two traits show up constantly in buying decisions and in user complaints about this screen looks bad from the side.

IPS gets its name from how the liquid crystals rotate within the panel.

In IPS,the crystals rotate in plane,meaning parallel to the screen surface,rather than twisting in a way that changes drastically depending on viewing angle.

This design improves consistency when light passes through the panel.

In practical terms,IPS keeps the image more stable when you move your head or when multiple people are looking at the same screen.

IPS panels are known for more consistent color reproduction,which is why they are popular with photographers,designers and video editors who care about how accurate colors look on screen.

Even for normal office users,better color consistency makes the display feel more clean and less washed out.

On the exam,remember this as a recommendation skill.

When a user prioritizes image quality and color,IPS is usually the safer choice than a budget panel type.

Viewing angles are where IPS stands out.

IPS panels can maintain usable image quality from extreme angles,often described as up to about 178 degrees horizontally and vertically.

The point is not memorizing the number as a promise,but understanding the user experience.

Colors shift less,brightness stays more consistent,and contrast does not invert nearly as quickly as it does on cheaper panel types.

This is why IPS works well for laptops in meetings,shared viewing and mobile devices where the screen is constantly being tilted.

IPS becomes an easy choice when multiple people need to see the same screen,like co-workers looking at a laptop during a presentation.

It also helps when you use a device at odd angles,like watching a video on a tablet while lying down.

On smartphones,IPS style behavior is valuable because you are constantly moving the device and changing viewing angle and you still want the picture to look consistent.

IPS is not perfect and the A-plus exam likes trade-offs.

IPS panels are often more expensive and response times can be slower than TN panels.

A common range you'll hear for IPS response time is about 4 to 8 milliseconds,which can matter for competitive gaming where motion blur and ghosting are concerns.

IPS can also show IPS glow,which is a backlight related glow seen in dark scenes,especially when viewing from an angle.

These drawbacks help you explain why an esports gamer might choose a different panel type even if IPS looks nicer.

Another trade-off is contrast.IPS panels often have moderate contrast ratios compared to VA panels.

A common ballpark number you'll hear for IPS is around 1000 to 1,which means blacks can look more grey in a dark room compared to a panel with stronger contrast.

The exam point is that no panel type is best at everything,and IPS is usually the best balance for color and angles,not necessarily the best for deep blacks.

IPS is a strong recommendation when the user values consistent image quality,accurate colors and wide viewing angles.

It fits content creation,general office work and any scenario where the screen is shared or viewed from different positions.

IPS has become a common default choice for mid-range to high end displays,especially when the goal is a high quality experience rather than the lowest cost or the absolute fastest pixel response.

That's IPS in-plane switching in a nutshell.

Strong color accuracy,excellent viewing angles,and generally high image quality.

Remember the trade-offs as well,including higher cost,the possibility of IPS glow,and response times often around 4 to 8 milliseconds.

Next,we'll look at TN panels,which take the opposite strategy by prioritizing speed and affordability over image quality.

111. TN 面板

大家好，讲完平面转换技术后，我们来聊聊扭曲向列型面板。

扭曲向列型是最古老且最简单的液晶面板类型之一，因其速度快且成本低廉，至今仍被广泛使用。

扭曲向列型面板是经典的预算选项，也常见于高刷新率游戏显示器中，因为在这些场景中速度比完美的色彩更重要。

扭曲向列型面板得名于其液晶自然呈螺旋状扭转的方式。

当施加电压时，它们会解开扭转，从而改变光线穿过面板的方式。

这种设计比平面转换更简单，这也解释了为什么扭曲向列型面板生产成本更低且能更快地切换状态。

考试要点是，扭曲向列型专为速度和成本效益而构建，而非高端图像质量。

扭曲向列型最大的优势是响应时间，即像素从一种状态切换到另一种状态的速度。

扭曲向列型面板宣传的响应时间通常低至一毫秒，这对竞争性游戏极具吸引力，因为它有助于减少运动模糊和重影。

即使您不是游戏玩家，了解扭曲向列型速度快也有助于您回答考试中的选择题，特别是当场景优先考虑响应速度而非观看体验时。

扭曲向列型面板常见于专为高刷新率设计的显示器中。

标准显示器的刷新率为六十赫兹，但游戏显示器的目标可能是一百四十四、二百四十甚至三百六十赫兹。

高刷新率能使运动画面看起来更流畅，但也要求面板能够足够快地切换以跟上节奏。

在这些产品中常选择扭曲向列型，因为它能以较低成本很好地处理快速切换。速度的代价是图像质量。

扭曲向列型面板通常色彩还原较弱，意味着与平面转换相比色彩可能显得泛白，且它们通常覆盖的色域较窄。

这就是为什么扭曲向列型不被视为摄影、设计或视频编辑等需要色彩准确性任务的理想选择。

对于考试题目，这是需要记住的关键权衡。

扭曲向列型速度快且便宜，但牺牲了图像质量。

扭曲向列型的可视角度通常较差，这是用户能立即注意到的症状。

当您从侧面、上方或下方观看扭曲向列型屏幕时，色彩可能会发生剧烈偏移，对比度也可能反转，导致图像在极端角度下看起来失真甚至无法阅读。

这在旧款预算笔记本电脑上尤为明显，倾斜屏幕会极大地改变外观。

如果用户抱怨屏幕正面看还可以但从侧面看就很糟糕，扭曲向列型往往是原因所在。

扭曲向列型仍然适用于预算系统、电子表格和电子邮件等基本办公任务，以及响应时间比色彩准确性更重要的竞争性游戏设置。

如果用户的优先级是低成本或最高速度，扭曲向列型可能是合适的选择。

如果用户的优先级是图像质量、共享观看或色彩工作，平面转换通常是更好的推荐。

以上就是扭曲向列型面板的概要，这是一种优先考虑速度和实惠性的面板类型。

其主要优势是非常快的响应时间（有时宣传约为一毫秒）以及与高刷新率显示器的兼容性。

其主要劣势是可视角度差以及色彩不够准确、不够鲜艳。

接下来，我们将转向垂直排列面板，与平面转换和扭曲向列型相比，它旨在提供更好的对比度和更深邃的黑色。

英文原文

Hey everyone,after IPS,let's talk about TN,which stands for Twisted Pneumatic.

TN is one of the oldest and simplest LCD panel types and it is still widely used because it is fast and inexpensive.

TN panels are the classic budget option and they are also common in high refresh rate gaming displays where speed matters more than perfect color.

TN panels are named for how the liquid crystals naturally twist in a spiral pattern.

When voltage is applied,they untwist and change how light passes through the panel.

The design is simpler than IPS,which helps explain why TN panels are cheaper to produce and can switch states quickly.

The exam takeaway is that TN is built for speed and cost efficiency,not premium image quality.

The biggest advantage of TN is response time,meaning how quickly pixels change from one state to another.

TN panels often advertise response times as low as 1 millisecond,which is especially attractive for competitive gaming because it helps reduce motion blur and ghosting.

Even if you are not a gamer,understanding that TN is fast helps you answer selection questions on the exam,especially when the scenario prioritizes responsiveness over viewing experience.

TN panels commonly appear in displays designed for high refresh rates.

Standard displays refresh at 60 Hz,but gaming displays may target 144240 or even 360 Hz.

High refresh rates can make motion look smoother,but they also demand a panel that can switch quickly enough to keep up.

TN is often chosen in these products because it handles fast switching well at lower cost.The trade-off for speed and cost is image quality.

TN panels usually have weaker color reproduction,meaning colors can look washed out compared to IPS and they generally cover a narrower color gamut.

This is why TN is not considered ideal for tasks where color accuracy matters like photography,design or video editing.

For exam questions,this is the key trade-off to remember.

TN is fast and cheap but it sacrifices image quality.

TN viewing angles are typically poor and this is a symptom users notice immediately.

When you look at a TN screen from the side,from above or from below,colors can shift dramatically and contrast can invert,making the image look wrong or even unreadable at extreme angles.

This is especially noticeable on older budget laptops where tilting the screen changes the appearance a lot.

If a user complains that the screen looks fine straight on but terrible from the side,TN is often the reason.

TN still makes sense for budget systems,basic office tasks like spreadsheets and email,and competitive gaming set ups where fast response time matters more than color accuracy.

If the user's priority is low cost or maximum speed,TN can be the right fit.

If the user's priority is image quality,shared viewing or color work,IPS is typically a better recommendation.

That's TN twisted pneumatic,a panel type that prioritizes speed and affordability.

The key strengths are very fast response times,sometimes advertised around 1 millisecond,and compatibility with high refresh rate displays.

The key weaknesses are poor viewing angles and less accurate,less vibrant colors.

Next,we'll move to VA panels,which aim for better contrast and deeper blacks compared to IPS and TN.

112. VA 面板

大家好，既然我们已经了解了平面转换和扭曲向列型面板，接下来聊聊垂直排列面板。

垂直排列的全称是垂直取向，它是您在显示器和电视中会看到的另一种主要液晶面板类型。

垂直排列面板以最显著的一个优势而闻名，那就是对比度。如果说平面转换是色彩和可视角度的面板，扭曲向列型是速度和成本的面板，那么垂直排列通常是深邃黑色和强对比度的面板。

对于A Plus考试，目标是理解权衡取舍，以便您能将面板类型与用户需求相匹配，并识别常见的投诉。

垂直排列得名于液晶在默认状态下的排列方式。

在垂直排列面板中，晶体的排列方式使其在应该显示黑色时能更有效地阻挡光线。

当施加电压时，晶体发生偏移以允许光线通过，从而生成更明亮的色彩。

实际的要点是，垂直排列面板往往比许多其他液晶类型更好地控制漏光，这是它们能够产生更深邃的黑色和更强对比度的主要原因。垂直排列面板之所以受欢迎，是因为它们通常能提供比典型平面转换面板高得多的对比度。

对比度是最亮白色与最暗黑色之间的差异，它直接影响屏幕在黑暗场景中的表现优劣。

平面转换的典型对比度大致约为一千比一，而垂直排列面板通常能达到三千比一或更高，具体取决于特定型号和背光设计。

适合考试的结论很简单。

如果有人想要为电影、媒体和一般流行内容获得更深邃的黑色，垂直排列往往是能最好地提供这种体验的液晶面板类型。在现实生活中，对比度是让显示屏看起来丰富的关键，特别是在昏暗的房间中。

在低对比度面板上，电影和游戏中的黑暗场景可能看起来泛白，因为黑色变成了灰色。

垂直排列面板往往能更好地处理这个问题，因此它们常用于旨在满足媒体消费和游戏需求的显示器中，因为在这些场景中视觉深度至关重要。

如果用户描述的主要抱怨是“黑色看起来像灰色”，那么垂直排列往往是专门为此改善体验而选择的面板类型，而无需转向完全不同的技术类别。

垂直排列面板的可视角度通常优于扭曲向列型，但并不总是像平面转换那样一致，特别是从侧面观看时的色彩和亮度。

根据面板和场景的不同，您在较宽的角度下可能会注意到一些偏移或亮度损失。

对于故障排除和用户支持而言，这一点很重要，因为用户可能非常喜欢正面的对比度，但抱怨在房间另一侧从侧面观看时图像看起来不同。

这不一定是缺陷，它可能是该面板类型的正常行为。

垂直排列面板的像素转换速度也可能比扭曲向列型慢，有时甚至比平面转换还慢，特别是在暗到暗的转换中。

这可能表现为快速移动场景中的运动模糊或涂抹，游戏玩家可能会将其描述为重影。

许多现代垂直排列游戏显示器通过更高的刷新率和过驱动设置改善了这一点，但这种权衡对考试而言仍然重要。

垂直排列在对比度方面可能看起来很棒，但对于最具竞争性、要求最快响应的游戏而言，它可能不是最佳选择，而在这些方面扭曲向列型往往胜出。

一个实际的支持说明是，激进的过驱动可以减少模糊，但可能会产生过冲伪影，因此设置会改变用户的体验。

当用户优先考虑电影、游戏和一般观看的对比度及深邃黑色时，特别是在较暗的房间中，垂直排列是一个极佳的推荐。

如果用户更看重视觉舒适度和对比度，而非极端角度下的完美色彩准确性，它也可以是通用生产力任务的强力选择。

如果用户需要最准确的色彩工作或供群体观看的最广可视角度，平面转换通常更合适。

如果用户需要绝对最快的响应速度和最低的成本，扭曲向列型仍然合理。

垂直排列处于中间位置，是一种专注于对比度的选项，为许多人提供了平衡的性能。

以上就是垂直排列技术的概要。

垂直排列面板是液晶显示器，以强对比度和更深邃的黑色而闻名，其对比度通常在三千比一或更高，而许多人认为平面转换的范围大约是一千比一。

其权衡可能包括不如平面转换一致的可视角度，以及相比最快的扭曲向列型游戏面板可能出现的运动涂抹。

对于A Plus考试，请记住决策逻辑：垂直排列是对比度的选择，平面转换是色彩和角度的选择，而扭曲向列型是速度和预算的选择。

Hey everyone,now that we have covered IPS and TN,let's talk about VA panels.

VA stands for Vertical Alignment and it's another major LCD panel type you'll see in monitors and TVs.

VA is best known for one big strength,contrast.If IPS is a colors and viewing angles panel and TN is the speed and cost panel,VA is often the deep blacks and strong contrast panel.

For the A-plus exam,the goal is understanding trade-offs so you can match the panel type to the user's needs and recognize common complaints.

VA gets its name from how the liquid crystals sit in their default state.

In a VA panel,the crystals are aligned in a way that blocks light more effectively when they are supposed to show black.

When voltage is applied,the crystals shift to allow light to pass and create brighter colors.

The practical takeaway is that VA panels tend to control light leakage better than many other L C D types,which is a big reason they can produce darker looking blacks and stronger contrast.VA panels are popular because they often deliver much higher contrast than typical IPS panels.

Contrast ratio is the difference between the brightest whites and the darkest blacks,and it directly impacts how good a screen looks in dark scenes.

A common IPS contrast ballpark is around 1000 to 1,while VA panels often land around 3000 to 1 or higher depending on the specific model and backlight design.

The exam-friendly takeaway is simple.

If someone wants darker blacks for movies,media and general pop,VA is often the L C D panel type that delivers that experience best.In real life,contrast is what makes a display look rich,especially in a dim room.

Dark scenes in movies and games can look washed out on low contrast panels because blacks turn into grey.

VA panels tend to handle this better,so they are commonly used in displays aimed at media consumption and gaming where visual depth matters.

If a user describes the blacks look grey as their main complaint,VA is the panel type that's often chosen specifically to improve that experience without moving to a completely different technology category.

VA panels usually have viewing angles that are better than TN,but not always as consistent as IPS,especially for color and brightness when viewed from the sides.

Depending on the panel and the scene,you may notice some shift or loss of brightness at wider angles.

For troubleshooting and user support,this matters because a user might love the contrast straight on but complain that the image looks different when viewed from the side across a room.

That is not necessarily a defect,it can be normal behavior for the panel type.

V A panels can also have slower pixel transitions than T N and sometimes even than IPS,especially in dark to dark transitions.

This can show up as motion blur or smearing in fast-moving scenes,which gamers may describe as ghosting.

Many modern VA gaming monitors improve this with higher refresh rates and overdrive settings,but the trade-off still matters for the exam.

VA can look great for contrast,but it may not be the best choice for the most competitive fastest response gaming where TN often wins.

A practical support note is that aggressive overdrive can reduce blur but may create overshoot artifacts,so settings can change what the user experiences.

VA is a great recommendation when the user prioritizes contrast and deep blacks for movies,games,and general viewing,especially in dimmer rooms.

It can also be a strong choice for general productivity if the user values visual comfort and contrast more than perfect color accuracy from extreme angles.

If the user needs the most accurate color work or the widest viewing angles for group viewing,IPS is often a better fit.

If the user needs the absolute fastest response and lowest cost,TN can still make sense.

VA sits in the middle as a contrast-focused option with balanced performance for many people.

That's VA technology in a nutshell.

VA panels are L C D's that are known for strong contrast and darker blacks,often around 3000 to 1 or higher,compared to the roughly 1000 to 1 range many people associate with IPS.

The trade-offs can include less consistent viewing angles than IPS and potential motion smearing compared to the fastest TN gaming panels.

For the A-plus exam,remember the decision logic:VA is the contrast choice,IPS is the color and angles choice,and TN is the speed and budget choice.

113. OLED 显示屏

大家好，现在我们将完全超越传统的液晶显示技术。

有机发光二极管是一种fundamentally不同的显示方法。

液晶显示器依赖液晶来控制来自背光的光线，而有机发光二极管像素则自行发光。

这单一的差异解释了有机发光二极管的大部分优势和大部分劣势，也是为什么当您亲眼看到它时，会感觉它是一种高端的飞跃。

有机发光二极管显示器使用有机的碳基化合物，当电流通过时会发光。

每个像素实际上都是其自身的微小光源，因此没有单独的背光层。

这意味着显示器可以在像素级别控制亮度，而不仅仅是在面板或区域级别。

当屏幕需要显示黑色时，像素可以完全关闭，这与液晶显示器截然不同，后者的背光通常在面板后方仍然亮着。

有机发光二极管的标志性特征是完美的黑色和实际上无限的对比度。当像素关闭时，它不发射任何光线，因此黑色区域是真正的黑色，而不是您在背光液晶面板上经常看到的深灰色，即使是好的面板也是如此。

这就是为什么有机发光二极管在黑暗房间中看起来特别令人印象深刻，以及为什么黑暗的电影场景感觉更深邃、更真实。

从考试角度来看，这是一个简单的记忆钩子。

有机发光二极管等于自发光像素，自发光像素等于真正的黑色。

有机发光二极管也往往能产生非常鲜艳饱和的色彩，因为每个像素都在创造自己的光线，而不是过滤来自背光的光线。

这有助于减少背光泄漏的外观，并能改善感知到的色彩冲击力。

许多有机发光二极管面板支持现代媒体内容中使用的宽色域目标，这就是为什么您在作为卖点的高端手机、笔记本电脑和电视中看到有机发光二极管的原因。

有机发光二极管的响应速度极快，因为不涉及液晶旋转。

液晶显示器的响应时间通常以毫秒讨论，但有机发光二极管的切换速度非常快，通常以微秒描述。

实际结果是减少了运动模糊和重影，这对游戏和快速运动视频有帮助。

这是有机发光二极管游戏显示器变得越来越受欢迎的原因之一，尽管有机发光二极管最初首先在手机和电视领域占据主导地位。有机发光二极管的可视角度极佳，因为每个像素直接发光，而不是依赖背光穿过多个层。

实际上，这意味着与许多液晶面板类型相比，从侧面观看时色彩偏移更少，对比度损失也更少。

对于A Plus思维，如果用户抱怨显示器从偏离轴线的角度观看时看起来截然不同，有机发光二极管通常不是罪魁祸首，而扭曲向列型面板往往是。

由于有机发光二极管不需要背光组件，它可以制造得非常薄。

有机发光二极管还可以在柔性基板上制造，这就是曲面屏幕和折叠手机变得实用的原因。

当您看到具有非常薄的显示组件或折叠设计的设备时，有机发光二极管是实现这种外形因素的常见底层技术。

您需要知道的用于故障排除的最大有机发光二极管缺点是烧屏，有时被描述为永久性图像残留。

如果静态元素长时间停留在屏幕上，如任务栏、程序坞、记分牌或频道标志，用于该内容的像素可能会与周围像素磨损程度不同。

随着时间的推移，这种不均匀的磨损可能会留下微弱的永久鬼影。

这就是为什么历史上有机发光二极管在生产率显示器中不太常见，因为在这些显示器上，静态用户界面元素每天会在同一位置停留数小时。

有机发光二极管材料会随着使用而退化，不同颜色的老化速度可能不同，其中蓝色通常最具挑战性。

这可能导致长期内色彩平衡逐渐偏移。

有机发光二极管也可能无法达到最亮的高端液晶方法相同的峰值亮度，特别是当您在非常明亮的房间中或使用强烈的高动态范围高光进行比较时。

对于支持和推荐，实际的观点是，有机发光二极管非常适合对比度和暗室观看，但高亮度液晶技术在明亮环境中仍然可以胜出。

有机发光二极管的制造成本通常更高，特别是在大尺寸上，这就是为什么有机发光二极管在成为预算产品的常见配置之前，先常见于旗舰手机和高端笔记本电脑的原因。

功耗表现也与液晶显示器不同。

对于有机发光二极管，较暗的内容可以使用更少的电力，因为黑色像素是关闭的，而大面积明亮区域可以使用更多电力，因为许多像素完全点亮。

这就是为什么深色模式在有机发光二极管设备上（特别是在手机上）可以更省电。

有机发光二极管广泛用于旗舰智能手机、高端笔记本电脑和高端电视，并且在显示器中也变得越来越常见。

模式是一致的。

有机发光二极管出现在显示质量是关键卖点且买家愿意支付更多费用的地方。

在故障排除中，如果用户拥有有机发光二极管设备，图像问题更可能与烧屏或像素级缺陷有关，而非背光故障，因为没有背光。

有机发光二极管使用自发光像素，从而实现完美的黑色、卓越的对比度、鲜艳的色彩、快速的响应和强大的可视角度。

其权衡包括烧屏风险、长期材料磨损和更高的成本，以及在非常明亮的高动态范围场景中与某些高端液晶方法相比的亮度限制。

接下来，我们将看看迷你发光二极管，这是液晶显示器的高科技回应，试图捕捉类似有机发光二极管的对比度，同时避免烧屏。

Hey everyone,now we are moving beyond traditional LCD technology entirely.

OLED,which stands for Organic Light Emitting Diode,is a fundamentally different display approach.

L C D's rely on liquid crystals to control light from a backlight,but OLED pixels generate their own light.

That single difference explains most of OLED's strengths and most of its weaknesses,and it's also why OLED feels like a premium leap when you see it in person.

OLED displays use organic carbon-based compounds that emit light when electricity flows through them.

Each pixel is effectively its own tiny light source,so there is no separate backlight layer.

This means the display can control brightness at the pixel level,not just at the panel or zone level.

When the screen needs to display black,the pixel can simply turn off completely,which is very different from L C D where the backlight is usually still on behind the panel.

OLED's signature feature is perfect blacks and effectively infinite contrast.When a pixel is off,it emits zero light,so black areas are truly black rather than the dark grey you often see on backlit L C D panels,even good ones.

This is why OLED looks especially impressive in a dark room and why dark movie scenes feel deeper and more realistic.

From an exam perspective,this is the easy memory hook.

OLED equals self-emissive pixels and self-emissive pixels equal true black.

OLED also tends to produce very vibrant saturated colors because each pixel is creating its own light rather than filtering light from a backlight.

That helps reduce the look of backlight bleed and can improve perceived color pop.

Many OLED panels support wide color gamma targets used in modern media content,which is why you see OLED in premium phones,laptops and televisions where image quality is a selling point.

OLED response time is extremely fast because there is no liquid crystal rotation involved.

L C D response times are often discussed in milliseconds but O LED switching can be so fast it is often described in microseconds.

The practical result is reduced motion blur and ghosting which helps for gaming and fast motion video.

This is one reason OLED gaming monitors have become more popular even though OLED originally dominated phones and TVs first.OLED viewing angles are excellent because each pixel emits light directly rather than relying on a backlight shining through multiple layers.

In practice,this means less color shifting and less contrast loss when viewing from the side compared to many L C D panel types.

For A-plus thinking,if a user complains that a display looks dramatically different when viewed off axis,O LED is typically not the culprit,while TN panels often are.

Because OLED does not need a backlight assembly,it can be manufactured very thin.

OLED can also be made on flexible substrates,which is how curved screens and foldable phones became practical.

When you see a device with a very thin display assembly or a folding design,OLED is a common underlying technology enabling that form factor.

The biggest OLED downside you need to know for troubleshooting is burn-in,sometimes described as permanent image retention.

If static elements stay on screen for long periods,like a taskbar,a dock,a scoreboard,or a channel logo,the pixels used for that content can wear differently than surrounding pixels.

Over time,that uneven wear can leave a faint permanent ghost image.

This is why OLED historically has been less common on productivity monitors,where static UI elements can sit in the same place for hours every day.

OLED materials degrade with use,and different colors can age at different rates,with blue often being the most challenging.

This can lead to gradual shifts in color balance over long periods.

OLED also may not reach the same peak brightness as the brightest premium L C D approaches,especially when you compare them in very bright rooms or with intense HDR highlights.

For support and recommendations,the practical point is that OLED is excellent for contrast and dark room viewing,but high brightness L C D technologies can still win in bright environments.

OLED is generally more expensive to manufacture,especially at larger sizes,which is why OLED is common in flagship phones and premium laptops before it becomes common in budget products.

Power usage also behaves differently than L C D.

With O LED,darker content can use less power because black pixels are off,while large bright areas can use more power because many pixels are fully lit.

This is why dark mode can be more power friendly on OLED devices,especially on phones.

OLED is widely used in flagship smartphones,premium laptops and high-end TVs,and it's becoming more common in monitors as well.

The pattern is consistent.

OLED shows up where display quality is a key selling point and the buyer is willing to pay more.

In troubleshooting,if a user has an OLED device,image issues are more likely to relate to burn-in or pixel-level defects,not backlight failure,because there is no backlight.

OLED uses self-emissive pixels which enables perfect blacks,excellent contrast,vibrant color,fast response,and strong viewing angles.

the trade offs are burn in risk,long term material wear,and higher cost,plus brightness limitations compared to some high end L C D approaches in very bright H T R scenarios.

Next,we'll look at mini LED,which is L C D's high tech response that tries to capture O L E D like contrast while avoiding burn in.

114. Mini-LED 技术

大家好，我们刚刚介绍了O L E D，它能实现像素级发光并提供惊人的对比度，但可能存在烧屏风险且成本较高。迷你发光二极管则是液晶显示器领域对此的回应。

它仍然是带有液晶的液晶面板，但背光得到了显著升级。

迷你发光二极管不再使用面板后方相对少量的发光二极管，而是使用了数量巨大且尺寸更小的发光二极管，从而提高了显示器精确控制屏幕不同区域亮度的能力。

迷你发光二极管指的是背光发光二极管的尺寸。

这些发光二极管比旧的背光设计小得多，这使得制造商可以在屏幕后方封装更多的发光二极管。

迷你发光二极管设计可以使用数千甚至数万个发光二极管，而不是几十个或几百个。

液晶层仍然控制图像，但背光变得更加精细，这直接提升了对比度和高动态范围性能。

真正的功能是局部调光区域。

全阵列局部调光在迷你发光二极管出现之前就已经存在，但迷你发光二极管通过允许数百到数千个独立控制的区域，将其提升到了更高的水平。

每个区域可以根据该区域图像的需求变亮或变暗。

你拥有的区域越多，背光的表现就越接近像素级控制，尽管它在液晶层后方仍然是分区域管理的。

拥有许多调光区域后，迷你发光二极管可以产生比传统液晶背光更深的黑色，因为黑暗区域后方的区域可以显著变暗。

这使得高动态范围场景看起来更令人信服，例如深色背景上的明亮高光。

虽然它无法达到O L E D真正的像素级关闭状态，但它足以缩小差距，让许多用户将其视为高端液晶体验。

迷你发光二极管相对于O L E D的主要优势之一是峰值亮度。

迷你发光二极管显示器通常可以推送非常明亮的高动态范围高光，这在明亮的房间中很有帮助，并使高动态范围效果更加引人注目。

实际上，阳光反射、爆炸场面和明亮的用户界面高光看起来会极其强烈和清晰。

这是迷你发光二极管在用于明亮环境的高端笔记本电脑和显示器中广受欢迎的主要原因。

迷你发光二极管有一种常见的伪影称为光晕效应，也称为光环效应。

由于每个调光区域控制着许多像素，黑暗背景上的一个小亮物体可能会导致其背后的整个区域变亮，从而在亮物体周围产生光晕。

一个典型的例子是黑色背景上的白色文字，字母周围显示出微弱的光环。

与O L E D相比，这是一个关键的权衡，因为O L E D的每个像素都能自我控制，通常不会出现光晕效应问题。

一个主要优势是，迷你发光二极管没有O L E D那样的烧屏风险profile，因为图像仍然由液晶层和背光系统形成，而不是自发光有机像素。

这使得迷你发光二极管对台式机和生产力设置具有吸引力，因为在这些设置中，任务栏、菜单栏和应用程序面板等静态元素可能会长时间显示在屏幕上。

这是迷你发光二极管成为重度办公使用更安全推荐的最重要原因之一。

迷你发光二极管是一项高端技术，成本高于基本的发光二极管背光液晶显示器，因为制造密集的背光阵列并控制许多调光区域需要先进的硬件和处理能力。

你往往会在高端显示器、高端笔记本电脑和高端平板电脑中看到迷你发光二极管。

对于A Plus考试，关键概念是迷你发光二极管仍然是液晶显示器，但拥有更先进的背光，从而改善了对比度和高动态范围亮度。

如果直接比较它们，O L E D在完美黑色、像素级对比度和消除光晕效应方面胜出，而且其响应时间也极快。

迷你发光二极管则在极高的峰值亮度和避免O L E D烧屏风险方面胜出，使其非常适合明亮的房间和重度静态生产力工作。

对于故障排查，O L E D问题可能包括烧屏和像素磨损，而迷你发光二极管问题更可能类似于液晶显示器问题，如背光均匀性、调光伪影或区域行为异常。

迷你发光二极管是一种高端液晶方法，它使用数千个微型发光二极管和许多局部调光区域，以显著提高对比度和高动态范围性能。

它可以变得非常明亮，并且不像O L E D那样存在烧屏风险，但由于区域控制不同于像素级控制，它可能会出现光晕效应。

接下来，我们将转向触摸屏和显示器逆变器，这将显示硬件与用户输入以及经典的背光故障排查联系起来。

英文原文

Hey everyone,we just covered OLED which produces light per pixel and delivers amazing contrast,but it can have burn-in risk and higher cost.Mini LED is the L C D world's response to that.

It is still an L C D panel with liquid crystals,but the backlight is dramatically upgraded.

Instead of a relatively small number of LEDs behind the panel,Mini LED uses a huge number of much smaller LEDs,which improves how precisely the display can control brightness across different parts of the screen.

Mini LED refers to the size of the backlight LEDs.

The LEDs are far smaller than older backlight designs,which allows manufacturers to pack many more of them behind the screen.

Instead of dozens or a few hundred LEDs,mini LED designs can use thousands or even tens of thousands.

The L C D layer still controls the image,but the backlight becomes much more granular,which directly improves contrast and HDR performance.

The real feature is local dimming zones.

Full array local dimming already existed before Mini LED,but Mini LED takes it much further by allowing hundreds to thousands of independently controlled zones.

Each zone can brighten or dim depending on what the image needs in that region.

The more zones you have,the more the backlight can behave like almost per pixel,even though it's still grouped into zones behind the L C D layer.

With many dimming zones,Mini LED can create much deeper blacks than traditional L C D backlights,because zones behind dark regions can dim significantly.

This makes HDR scenes look more convincing,like bright highlights on a darker background.

It will not be the same as O LED's true per pixel off state,but it closes the gap enough that many users see it as a premium L C D experience.

One of Mini LED's major advantages over O LED is peak brightness.

Mini LED displays can often push very bright HDR highlights which helps in bright rooms and makes HDR effects more dramatic.

In practical terms,sunlight reflections,explosions and bright UI highlights can look extremely intense and crisp.

This is a major reason Mini LED is popular in premium laptops and monitors used in bright environments.

Mini LED has a common artifact called blooming,also called haloing.

Because each dimming zone controls many pixels,a small bright object on a dark background can cause the entire zone behind it to brighten,creating a glow around the bright object.

A classic example is white text on a black background showing a faint halo around letters.

This is a key trade-off compared to OLED where each pixel controls itself and blooming is not a typical issue.

A major advantage is that Mini LED does not have the same burn-in risk profile as O LED,because the image is still formed by an L C D layer and a backlight system,not self emissive organic pixels.

That makes Mini LED appealing for desktops and productivity setups where static elements like taskbars,menu bars and application panels can remain on screen for long sessions.

This is one of the biggest reasons Mini LED can be a safer recommendation for heavy office use.

Mini LED is premium technology and costs more than basic LED backlit L C D because manufacturing a dense backlight array and controlling many dimming zones requires advanced hardware and processing.

You tend to see Mini LED in higher end monitors,premium laptops and premium tablets.

For A,the key idea is that Mini LED is still L C D but with a far more advanced backlight that improves contrast and HDR brightness.

If you compare them directly,O LED wins on perfect blacks,per pixel contrast and eliminating blooming and it is also extremely fast in response time.

Mini LED wins on very high peak brightness and avoiding OLED's burn-in risk,making it a strong fit for bright rooms and static heavy productivity.

For troubleshooting,OLED problems can include burn-in and pixel wear,while Mini LED problems are more likely to resemble L C D issues like backlight uniformity,dimming artifacts or zone behavior.

Mini LED is a premium L C D approach that uses thousands of tiny LEDs and many local dimming zones to dramatically improve contrast and HDR performance.

It can get very bright and does not carry the same burn in risk as O LED but it can show blooming because zones are not the same as per pixel control.

Next we'll shift into touchscreens and display inverters which ties display hardware to user input and classic backlight troubleshooting.

115. 触摸屏与显示逆变器

大家好！

到目前为止，我们一直关注显示器如何创建图像，但许多现代设备还能直接在显示表面检测你的触摸。

触摸屏在手机和平板电脑上已是标准配置，在笔记本电脑上也很常见。

在本讲座中，我们将涵盖你会遇到的两种主要触摸技术：电容式和电阻式。

然后，我们将通过讨论显示器逆变器回到显示故障排查话题，这对于旧款笔记本电脑的背光很重要。

电容式触摸是当今最常见的触摸技术。

屏幕包含一个透明的电极网格，用于产生电场。

当你触摸屏幕时，你的手指会改变该位置的电容，控制器随后检测到触摸的坐标。

这就是为什么电容式触摸感觉轻盈且响应迅速。

因为它不需要压力，所以需要能与电场相互作用的导电触摸。

这里有一个高价值的考试细节。

电容式屏幕需要导电物体。

你的手指之所以有效，是因为人体皮肤能导电。

普通的塑料触控笔不会触发电容式屏幕，因为它无法以正确的方式与电场相互作用。

这也是为什么普通手套通常无法使用，除非指尖含有导电材料。

电容式触控笔设计有导电笔尖，因此在电气表现上就像手指一样。

电容式屏幕支持多点触控，意味着设备可以同时检测多个触摸点。

这正是实现捏合缩放、双指滚动、旋转手势以及许多其他现代交互功能的原因。

控制器通过同时检测网格上多处电容的变化来跟踪每个触摸点。

对于故障排查，如果用户说手势停止工作或只识别到一个触摸点，你应该怀疑驱动程序、校准、固件或数字化仪的问题，而不是基本的显示图像生成问题。

电阻式触摸是一种较旧的方法，它检测的是压力而非导电性。

它使用两层柔性层，中间有一个微小的间隙。

当你按压屏幕时，这两层相互接触并在该点接通电路，控制器根据这种电气变化确定触摸位置。

关键区别在于，电阻式触摸不在乎你用什麼触摸，只要施加压力即可。

因此，它适用于手套、指甲和非导电触控笔。

电阻式触摸在特定环境中具有优势，但对于现代消费用途也有重大缺点。

它通常需要更大的压力才能注册触摸，往往感觉响应较慢，并且通常不支持真正的多点触控手势。

由于涉及额外的层，它还可能降低图像清晰度。

这就是为什么电容式成为消费设备的主导标准，而电阻式仍保留在工业控制、信息亭以及需要戴手套的环境等小众领域。

对于绘图或手写等精密工作，许多设备使用主动式数字化仪系统，这与基本的电容式手指触摸不同。

这些系统支持压感、倾斜、手掌抑制和更精确的跟踪等功能。

这就是为什么专业触控笔感觉像钢笔而不是手指替代品。

对于A Plus考试，关键概念是触摸可以指基本的手指触摸，也可以指用于高级触控笔输入的独立数字化仪层。

现在让我们转向显示器逆变器。

在使用冷阴极荧光灯背光的旧款笔记本电脑中，逆变器是一种电路，它将来自笔记本电脑的低电压直流电转换为点亮冷阴极荧光灯管所需的高压交流电。

这在概念上类似于荧光灯照明比简单的发光二极管需要不同的电源设置。

逆变器是一个经典的硬件故障排查主题，因为它们可能会发生故障，导致屏幕看起来像是坏了，即使液晶显示器仍在生成图像。

逆变器故障的症状非常独特。

笔记本电脑通电并似乎在运行，但屏幕极暗或全黑。

如果你用手电筒照射显示屏，并能隐约看到桌面或登录图像，说明液晶面板仍在工作，问题出在背光系统，这可能包括逆变器或灯管。

这种诊断模式价值很高，因为它能快速区分“未生成图像”和“已生成图像但无光照”。

采用发光二极管背光的现代笔记本电脑不使用冷阴极荧光灯逆变器，因为发光二极管在低电压直流电下运行，可由现代电源电路直接驱动。

这减少了热量，提高了效率，并消除了一个故障点。

对于故障排查，这很重要，因为基于逆变器的故障主要局限于旧的冷阴极荧光灯背光笔记本电脑，而现代发光二极管背光显示器有不同的故障模式，通常与发光二极管背光驱动电路有关，而不是高压逆变器。

电容式触摸检测电容变化并支持多点触控手势，但需要导电输入。

电阻式触摸检测压力并适用于任何物体，但响应较慢且通常缺乏多点触控功能。

对于精密输入，设备可能使用主动式数字化仪，以实现压感和触控笔功能。

显示器逆变器与旧的冷阴极荧光灯背光相关，是导致屏幕变暗的常见原因，此时手电筒测试会显示图像存在但未点亮。

接下来，我们将通过涵盖分辨率、宽高比、刷新率、亮度和响应时间等显示属性来结束本章节。

英文原文

Hey everyone!

Up until now,we've focused on how displays create images,but many modern devices also detect your touch directly on the display surface.

Touch screens are standard on phones and tablets and common on laptops as well.

In this lecture,we'll cover the two main touch technologies you'll see,capacitive and resistive.

And then we'll connect back to display troubleshooting by discussing display inverters,which matter for older laptop backlights.

Capacitive touch is the most common touch technology today.

The screen contains a transparent grid of electrodes that creates an electric field.

When you touch the screen,your finger changes the capacitance at that location and the controller detects the coordinate of the touch.

This is why capacitive touch feels light and responsive.

Because it does not require pressure,it requires a conductive touch that interacts with the electrical field.

Here is a high-yield exam detail.

Capacitive screens require a conductive object.

Your finger works because human skin conducts electricity.

A normal plastic stylus will not trigger a capacitive screen because it does not interact with the electrical field in the right way.

This is also why normal gloves often do not work unless they have conductive material in the fingertips.

Capacitive styluses are designed with conductive tips so they behave like a finger electrically.

Capacitive screens enable multi-touch,meaning the device can detect multiple touch points at the same time.

This is what allows pinch to zoom,two finger scroll,rotation gestures and many other modern interactions.

The controller tracks each touch point by detecting multiple changes in capacitance across the grid simultaneously.

For troubleshooting,if a user says gestures stopped working or only one touch is recognized,you suspect driver,calibration,firmware or digitizer issues rather than basic display image generation.

Resistive touch is an older approach that detects pressure instead of conductivity.

It uses two flexible layers with a small gap between them.

When you press the screen,the layers contact each other and complete a circuit at that point and the controller determines the touch location from that electrical change.

The key difference is that Resistive does not care what you touch with as long as it applies pressure.

So it works with gloves,fingernails and non-conductive styluses.

Resistive touch has strengths in specialized environments,but it also has major drawbacks for modern consumer use.

It usually requires more pressure to register touch,tends to feel less responsive and does not typically support true multi-touch gestures.

It can also reduce image clarity because of the extra layers involved.

That is why capacitive became the dominant standard for consumer devices,while resistive remains in niches like industrial controls,kiosks,and environments where gloves are required.

For precision work like drawing or handwriting,many devices use an active digitizer system which is different from basic capacitive finger touch.

These systems support features like pressure sensitivity,tilt,palm rejection and more accurate tracking.

This is why a professional stylus can feel like a pen rather than a finger substitute.

For A Plus,the key idea is that touch can mean basic finger touch or a separate digitizer layer for advanced stylus input.

Now let's switch to display inverters.

In older laptops that used CCFL backlighting,the inverter is a circuit that converts low voltage DC from the laptop into the high voltage AC needed to power the CCFL lamp.

This is similar in concept to how fluorescent lighting requires a different power setup than simple LEDs.

Inverters are a classic hardware troubleshooting topic because they can fail and make a screen appear dead even when the L C D is still generating the image.

Inverter failure symptoms are distinctive.

The laptop powers on and seems to run,but the screen is extremely dim or dark.

If you shine a flashlight on the display and you can faintly see the desktop or login image,the L C D panel is still working and the issue is the backlight system which can include the inverter or the lamp.

This diagnostic pattern is high yield because it quickly separates no image generated from image generated but no light.

Modern laptops with LED batlights do not use CCFL inverters because LEDs run on low voltage DC and can be driven directly by modern power circuitry.

This reduces heat,improves efficiency and removes a failure point.

For troubleshooting,this matters because inverter based failures are mostly limited to older CCFL batlet laptops while modern LED batlet displays have different failure modes,often tied to the LED backlight driver circuitry rather than a high voltage inverter.

Capacitive touch detects changes in capacitance and supports multi-touch gestures but requires conductive input.

Resistive touch detects pressure and works with any object but is less responsive and usually lacks multi-touch.

For precision input,devices may use active digitizers that enable pressure and stylus features.

Display inverters are tied to older CCFL backlights and are a common cause of dim screens where the flashlight test reveals the image is present but unlit.

Next we'll wrap this section by covering display attributes like resolution,aspect ratio,refresh rate,brightness and response time.

116. 显示属性

大家好！

到目前为止，我们已经了解了显示器的工作原理，但规格参数仍然很重要，因为它们解释了屏幕能做什么，以及为什么两块屏幕的感觉可能完全不同。

显示属性有助于你为用户需求选择合适的显示器或笔记本电脑，并排查诸如文字看起来模糊、运动画面看起来卡顿或屏幕亮度不足等投诉。

在本讲座中，我们将涵盖分辨率、像素密度、宽高比、刷新率、亮度、响应时间、对比度和色域，其方式将直接对应A Plus风格的考题。

分辨率是屏幕上的像素数量，表示为宽度乘以高度。

常见的例子包括一千九百二十乘以一千零八十，通常称为一千零八十p或全高清，两千五百六十乘以一千四百四十，通常称为一千四百四十p或Q H D，以及三千八百四十乘以两千一百六十，通常称为四K或U H D。

更高的分辨率意味着更多的像素，这可以使文本和图像看起来更清晰，尤其是在较大的显示器上。

考试技能在于认识到分辨率仅仅是像素网格，而非物理尺寸。

像素密度以每英寸像素数来衡量，它决定了在给定观看距离下的感知清晰度。

相同的分辨率根据屏幕尺寸的不同，看起来可能会有很大差异。

具有相同分辨率的较小笔记本电脑屏幕看起来可能比大型显示器更清晰，因为像素排列得更紧密。

手机通过使用非常高的像素密度将这一点发挥到极致，使得在正常观看距离下很难看到像素点。

对于故障排查，这解释了为什么用户从高密度笔记本电脑切换到大型低密度显示器时，可能会突然抱怨文字看起来有锯齿。

宽高比是显示器的形状，即宽度与高度之间的关系。

十六比九是显示器和电视常见的宽屏标准。

十六比十稍高一些，在生产型笔记本电脑中很受欢迎，因为它能显示更多的垂直内容，有助于处理文档和网页。

二十一比九或三十二比九等超宽格式可以通过允许并排窗口而无需第二台显示器来帮助多任务处理。

对于考试，宽高比问题通常与用例相关，例如生产力与媒体娱乐。

刷新率是显示器每秒更新的次数，以赫兹为单位进行测量。

六十赫兹常用于一般用途，而游戏显示器通常使用一百四十四、二百四十或更高。

更高的刷新率可以使运动感觉更流畅，并减少模糊感，但计算机也必须能够产生足够的帧数才能从中受益。

就故障排查而言，如果用户购买了高刷新率显示器但感觉仍像六十赫兹，修复方法通常是设置问题，例如系统仍以六十赫兹运行显示器。

自适应同步技术将显示器刷新率与图形系统的帧输出相匹配，这有助于在帧率波动时减少屏幕撕裂和卡顿。

不同的生态系统使用不同的名称，但概念是相同的。

显示器会调整以适应显卡输出，而不是强制固定的刷新节奏。

对于A Plus思维，这通常与游戏流畅度投诉和配置检查相关联。

亮度以尼特为单位进行测量，它决定了屏幕在明亮环境中的可见程度。

许多办公显示器的亮度在几百尼特左右，这在室内没问题，而专注于高动态范围的显示器可能会瞄准一千尼特或更高以实现明亮的高光。

这也是为什么某些显示器在窗户附近或户外难以看清的原因，因为亮度设定了可见度的上限。

在故障排查中，屏幕太暗可能是设置问题、省电模式、背光问题，或者仅仅是该显示器从未设计用于明亮环境。

响应时间是像素变化的速度，它对运动清晰度很重要。

这与我们之前讨论的面板类型有关。

T N面板通常被选择用于极低的响应时间。

I P S面板通常较慢，但在色彩和视角方面更好。

V A面板在某些场景中可能会显示出较慢的过渡，看起来像涂抹。

而O L E D的速度极快。如果用户抱怨重影或模糊，响应时间和面板行为将与刷新率设置一起成为诊断的一部分。

对比度是显示器能产生的最亮白色与最黑黑色之间的差异。

I P S通常在大约一千比一左右，V A可能在大约三千比一或更高，而O L E D实际上是无限的，因为黑色像素可以完全关闭。

一个常见的考试陷阱是动态对比度，这可能是一个营销数字，并不能反映正常观看下的实际可用对比度。

有用的概念是静态对比度及其背后的面板技术。

色域描述了显示器能重现多少种颜色。

s R G B是大多数网络内容和通用计算的基准。

更宽的色域如Adobe R G B和D C I P三针对摄影和电影工作流程，当内容支持时，可以产生更饱和的颜色。

专业显示器通常会宣传覆盖率百分比，如百分之九十九s R G B，以表明色彩能力。

对于A Plus考试，你不需要成为色彩科学家，但你应该理解色域会影响颜色的准确性和生动性，尤其是对于创作者而言。

这就是A Plus问题通常落脚的地方。

对于游戏，优先考虑刷新率、响应时间和自适应同步。

对于内容创作，优先考虑色彩准确性和色域覆盖率，加上分辨率和一致的面板表现，如I P S或O L E D。

对于办公生产力，舒适度和清晰度最重要，通常意味着合理的分辨率、良好的亮度和实用的宽高比，其中I P S是常见的安全推荐。

对于普通用户，要平衡成本和质量，并确保设置与硬件匹配，以便用户真正获得他们付费购买的益处。

显示属性定义了屏幕能做什么，并解释了常见的用户投诉。

分辨率和P P I决定清晰度，宽高比影响工作区形状，刷新率和响应时间影响运动清晰度，亮度决定可见度，对比度塑造图像的深邃感，而色域影响色彩还原。

一旦你能将投诉映射到正确的属性，你就能更快地进行故障排查，并为工作推荐合适的显示器。

英文原文

Hey everyone!

By now we've covered how displays work,but specifications still matter because they explain what a screen can do and why two screens can feel completely different.

Display attributes help you pick the right monitor or laptop for a user's needs and troubleshoot complaints like text looks blurry,motion looks choppy or the screen isn't bright enough.

In this lecture,we'll cover resolution,pixel density,aspect ratio,refresh rate,brightness,response time,contrast and color gamut in a way that maps directly to A plus style questions.

Resolution is the number of pixels on the screen written as width by height.

Common examples include 1920 by 1080 often called 1080p or full HD,2560 by 1440 often called 1440p or QHT and 3840 by 2160 often called 4K or UHT.

Higher resolution means more pixels,which can make text and images look sharper,especially on larger displays.

The exam skill is recognizing that resolution is only the pixel grid,not the physical size.

Pixel density measured as pixels per inch is what determines perceived sharpness at a given viewing distance.

The same resolution can look very different depending on screen size.

A smaller laptop screen with the same resolution can look sharper than a larger monitor because the pixels are packed closer together.

Phones push this even further by using very high pixel density so pixels are hard to see at normal viewing distance.

For troubleshooting,this explains why a user moving from a high density laptop to a large low density monitor might suddenly complain that text looks jagged.

Aspect ratio is the shape of the display,meaning the relationship between width and height.

16 to 9 is the common widescreen standard for monitors and TVs.

16 to 10 is slightly taller and is popular in productivity laptops because it shows more vertical content which helps with documents and web pages.

Ultra-wide formats like 21 to 9 or 32 to 9 can help multitasking by allowing side by side windows without a second monitor.

For the exam,aspect ratio questions usually connect to use case like productivity versus media.

Refresh rate is how many times per second the display updates measured in hertz.

60 hertz is common for general use while gaming displays often use 144240 or higher.

Higher refresh rates can make motion feel smoother and reduce the perception of blur,but the computer must also be capable of producing enough frames to benefit.

Troubleshooting-wise,if a user bought a high refresh monitor but it still feels like 60,the fix is often settings,such as the system still running the display at 60 Hz.

Adaptive sync technologies match the display refresh rate to the frame output from the graphic system,which helps reduce screen tearing and stutter when frame rates fluctuate.

Different ecosystems use different names,but the concept is the same.

The display adjusts to the GPU output rather than forcing a fixed refresh rhythm.

For A plus thinking,this is often tied to gaming smoothness complaints and configuration checks.

Brightness is measured in nits and it determines how well a screen is seen in bright environments.

Many office monitors sit in the mid-hundreds of nits,which is fine indoors,while HDR-focused displays may target 1000 nits or more for bright highlights.

This is also why some displays are hard to see near Windows or outdoors,because brightness sets the ceiling for visibility.

In troubleshooting,screen is too dim,can be a setting,a power saving mode,a backlight issue,or simply a display that was never designed for a bright environment.

Response time is how quickly pixels change and it matters for motion clarity.

This connects to the panel types we covered earlier.

TN is often chosen for very low response times.

IPS is commonly slower but better for color and angles.

VA can show slower transitions that look like smearing in some scenes.

And OLED is extremely fast.If a user complains about ghosting or blur,response time and panel behavior become part of the diagnosis along with refresh rate settings.

Contrast ratio is the difference between brightest white and darkest black a display can produce.

IPS often sits around 1000 to 1,VA can be around 3000 to 1 or higher,and OLED is effectively infinite because black pixels can turn completely off.

A common exam trap is dynamic contrast,which can be a marketing number that does not reflect real usable contrast in normal viewing.

The useful concept is static contrast and the panel technology behind it.

Color gamut describes how many colors a display can reproduce.

sRGB is the baseline for most web content and general computing.

Wider gamuts like Adobe RGB and DCIP3 target photography and cinema workflows and can produce more saturated colors when content supports it.

Professional displays often advertise coverage percentages like 99%sRGB to signal color capability.

For A,you do not need to be a color scientist,but you should understand that gamut affects how accurate and vivid colour appears,especially for creators.

This is where A questions usually land.

For gaming,prioritize refresh rate,response time,and adaptive sync.

For content creation,prioritize color accuracy and gamut coverage,plus resolution and consistent panel behavior like IPS or OLED.

For office productivity,comfort and clarity matter most,often meaning a reasonable resolution,good brightness,and a usable aspect ratio,with IPS being a common safe recommendation.

For general users,balance cost and quality and make sure settings match the hardware so users actually get the benefits they paid for.

Display attributes define what a screen can do and explain common user complaints.

Resolution and PPI determine sharpness,aspect ratio affects workspace shape,refresh rate and response time affect motion clarity,brightness determines visibility,contrast shapes how deep images look and gamut affects color reproduction.

Once you can map a complaint to the correct attribute,you can troubleshoot faster and recommend the right display for the job.

117. 网络线缆类别

大家好，欢迎进入这个新章节，我们将深入探讨线缆和连接器，也就是让一切正常工作的物理连接。

今天我们将从网络线缆类别开始。

当你听到五类增强型、六类或六类增强型时，这些都是双绞线以太网电缆的类别，每个类别都有不同的性能规格。

了解这些类别有助于你为工作选择合适的线缆，排查速度和可靠性投诉，并避免为你实际上不需要的性能付费。

CATdesignation代表类别，它是一个标准化评级系统，定义了线缆在特定测试条件下的表现。

较高的类别编号通常意味着更好的性能，包括更高的可用频率、更强的抗干扰能力以及在更高速度下的更好表现。

制定这些标准是为了让制造商和安装商在描述线缆能够可靠支持的内容时使用相同的语言，特别是针对结构化布线的标准最大距离一百米，约合三百二十八英尺。

五类增强型意味着第五类增强版，它是取代旧式五类标准的现代基线。

五类增强型额定支持每秒一千兆比特，即在一百米距离内每秒一千兆比特的速度。

它的运行频率高达一百兆赫兹，并且仍然非常普遍，因为它价格低廉，且适用于典型的家庭和小型办公室网络。

对于A Plus考试，五类增强型是你应该认为现代以太网安装可接受的最小双绞线类别。

当你的网络主要是一千兆比特，且你正在执行网页浏览、流媒体、打印和文件传输等常规任务时，五类增强型非常合适。

它也常用于跳线和短距离布线，因为它灵活且易于操作。

关键的决策点是未来的速度升级，因为如果你认为以后会在网络的某些部分升级到一万兆比特，那么即使五类增强型今天能完美支持一千兆比特，它也可能成为限制因素。

六类是一个升级，是人们开始考虑一万兆比特能力的起点。

六类支持每秒一万兆比特，但关键的考试细节是距离。

在六类线上运行一万兆比特通常限制在约五十五米，合一百八十英尺左右，超过该距离后，在一百米的完整布线长度上通常会回退到一千兆比特。

六类的运行频率高达二百五十兆赫兹，是五类增强型的两倍多，它采用更严格的构造要求来减少线对之间的串扰。

对于希望平衡成本和未来兼容性的新安装，六类是一个明智的选择。

它常见于商业环境和升级后的家庭网络中，在那里你可能最终会在短距离内使用一万兆比特，例如服务器或网络附加存储，或者交换机之间的上行链路。

与五类增强型相比，价格差异通常远小于布线的人工成本，因此许多技术人员在新建建筑中选择六类，因为人工才是昂贵的部分，而不是线缆本身。

六类增强型意味着第六类增强版，旨在在一百米的完整距离上提供完整的一万兆比特性能。

六类增强型的运行频率高达五百兆赫兹，再次是六类的两倍。

这种线缆更厚且灵活性较差，因为它采用了改进的构造来减少串扰和外部串扰，后者是由同一线束中附近线缆引起的干扰。

对于考试，核心概念很简单。

如果你必须保证在完整的结构化布线距离上实现一万兆比特，六类增强型是标准的双绞线选择。

六类增强型可能更难安装，因为它具有更大的弯曲半径，当你试图在墙壁、导管或拥挤的机架中进行急转弯时，它的容错性较低。

它的成本也高于六类。

但如果环境是企业级的，并且要求everywhere保持一致的一万兆比特性能，那么六类增强型通常是值得的，因为它减少了未来的重新布线需求，并有助于防止高密度布线中的干扰问题。

七类确实存在，但它不是典型以太网安装中的常见选择。

它通常被讨论为一种国际标准化组织风格的标准，而不是大多数安装商在结构化布线中遵循的主流类别路径。

它可以具有重度屏蔽并额定用于更高频率，但一个关键的实际缺点是连接器兼容性，因为在某些情况下，七类的实现可能使用非标准连接器，如G G四五或Terra，而不是标准的R J四五。

对于A Plus级别的支持，最有用的概念是，与五类增强型、六类和六类增强型相比，七类在现场非常罕见。

六类增强型已经支持使用标准R J四五连接器在一百米距离上实现一万兆比特，这就是为什么大多数组织在双绞线方面到此为止。

当性能需求超出六类增强型舒适提供的范围时，许多环境会转而使用光纤布线，因为光纤能更有效地处理更高的速度和更长的距离。

这就是为什么七类通常是一个小众选择，而不是大多数网络的默认升级路径。

以下是实用的A Plus决策逻辑。

如果要求是一千兆比特且正常距离长达一百米，五类增强型就足够且经济。

如果你正在进行新布线并希望留有升级余地，六类是一个强有力的中间选择，特别是如果网络中的一万兆比特部分将是低于约五十五米的短距离布线。

如果你要求在整个一百米结构化布线距离上具备一万兆比特能力，六类增强型是专业选择。

除非特定环境需要它且已确认兼容性，否则七类通常不是首选推荐。

网络线缆类别告诉你双绞线以太网布线能够可靠支持什么。

五类增强型支持在一百兆赫兹下，长达一百米的一千兆比特速度。

六类支持长达约五十五米的一万吉比特速度，在更长距离上回退到一千兆比特，其运行频率高达二百五十兆赫兹。

六类增强型支持在完整的一百米距离上实现一万吉比特速度，运行频率高达五百兆赫兹，但它更厚且更昂贵。

七类确实存在，但由于兼容性和实际升级路径的原因，它并不常见。

接下来，我们将转向T五六八A和T五六八B布线标准，也就是端接这些线缆的两种正确方法。

英文原文

Hey there,welcome to this new section where we are diving deep into cables and connectors,meaning the physical connections that make everything work.

Today we are starting with network cable categories.

When you hear CAT5E,CAT6 or CAT6A,those are categories of twisted pair Ethernet cable and each category has different performance specifications.

Understanding the categories helps you choose the right cable for the job,troubleshoot speed and reliability complaints and avoid paying for performance you don't actually need.

The CAT designation stands for category and it's a standardized rating system that defines how the cable performs under specific test conditions.

Higher category numbers generally mean better performance through higher usable frequencies,better resistance to interference and better behavior at higher speeds.

These standards are defined so that manufacturers and installers can speak the same language when describing what a cable can reliably support,especially over the standard structured cabling maximum distance of 100 meters which is about 328 feet.

CAT 5E means category 5 enhanced and it is the modern baseline that replaced the older CAT 5 standard.

CAT 5E is rated to support 1 gigabit per second which is 1000 megabits per second over distances up to 100 meters.

It operates up to 100 megahertz and it's still extremely common because it is inexpensive and works well for typical home and small office networks.

For the A plus exam,CAT 5E is the minimum twisted pair category you should think of as acceptable for modern Ethernet installs.

CAT5E is a great fit when your network is mostly 1 gigabit and you are doing normal tasks like web use,streaming,printing and file transfers.

It's also common for patch cables and short runs because it's flexible and easy to work with.

The key decision point is future speed upgrades because if you think you'll move to 10 gigabit in parts of the network later,CAT 5E may become the limiting factor even if it works perfectly today for 1 gigabit.

CAT6 is a step up and it's where people start thinking about 10 gigabit capability.

CAT6 supports 10 gigabit per second but the key exam detail is distance.

10 gig over CAT6 is typically limited to about 55 meters which is about 180 feet and beyond that distance it commonly drops back to 1 gigabit at the full 100 meter run length.

CAT6 operates up to 250 megahertz which is more than double CAT 5E and it uses tighter construction requirements to reduce crosstalk between pairs.

CAT6 is a smart choice for new installs where you want a balance of cost and future proofing.

It's common in business environments and upgraded home networks where you may eventually use ten gig for a short run,like a server in NAS,or an uplink between switches.

The price difference from CAT5E is usually small compared to the labor of running cable,so many technicians choose CAT6 during new construction because the labor is the expensive part,not the cable.

CAT6A means category 6 augmented and it is designed for full 10 gigabit performance over the full 100 meter distance.

CAT6A operates up to 500 megahertz,doubling CAT6 again.

The cable is thicker and less flexible because it uses improved construction to reduce crosstalk and alien crosstalk,which is interference caused by nearby cables in the same bundle.

For the exam,the big idea is simple.

If you must guarantee 10 gig over the full structured cabling distance,CAT6A is the standard twisted pair choice.

CAT6A can be harder to install because it has a larger bend radius and it is less forgiving when you try to make tight turns in walls,conduits or crowded racks.

It also costs more than CAT6.

But if the environment is enterprise grade and the requirement is consistent 10 gig performance everywhere,CAT6A is often worth it because it reduces future recabling and helps prevent interference issues in high density cable runs.

CAT 7 exists but it is not a common choice in typical Ethernet installs.

It is often discussed as an ISO style standard rather than the same mainstream category path most installers follow in structured cabling.

It can be heavily shielded and rated for higher frequencies but a key practical drawback is connector compatibility because CAT7 implementations may use non-standard connectors like GG45 or Terra rather than standard RJ45 in some cases.
