138. 固态硬盘（SSD）

大家好，现在让我们从机械硬盘转向固态硬盘，也就是SSD，这项正在彻底变革计算领域的存储技术。

固态硬盘没有活动部件，使用闪存芯片以电子方式存储数据。

与机械硬盘相比，它们速度极快、更耐用、更安静且更节能。

了解固态硬盘技术、其优势及其局限性，有助于你做出明智的存储决策。

让我们深入探讨是什么让固态硬盘如此特别。

固态硬盘将数据存储在NAND闪存芯片中，这与USB闪存驱动器和SD卡使用的技术相同，只是规模更大且控制器更复杂。

在固态硬盘内部，多个闪存芯片连接到一个控制器芯片，该芯片管理数据的存储、检索和优化。

这里没有盘片、没有马达、没有移动磁头，只有固态电子元件。

即使断电，数据也能保留，使其像机械硬盘一样成为真正的非易失性存储。

NAND闪存通过将电子捕获在浮栅晶体管中来存储数据。

当存在电子时，单元代表零。

当不存在电子时，它代表一，或者反之亦然，具体取决于设计。

要写入数据，控制器会施加电压以注入或移除电子。

要读取数据，它会测量每个单元的电荷水平。

每个存储单元在磨损之前只能被写入和擦除有限的次数。

这是闪存技术的根本限制。

固态硬盘在几乎每一个可衡量的方面都比机械硬盘快得惊人。

随机访问时间，即定位和检索数据所需的时间，对于固态硬盘是以微秒为单位，而机械硬盘则是以毫秒为单位。

这快了一百倍。

SATA固态硬盘的顺序读取速度可达每秒五百到五百五十兆字节，而机械硬盘为每秒一百二十到一百六十兆字节。

NVMe固态硬盘的速度可达每秒三千到七千兆字节。

启动时间从使用机械硬盘的一分钟或更长时间，缩短到使用固态硬盘的十到十五秒。

应用程序启动几乎是瞬间完成的。

固态硬盘的速度优势彻底改变了计算体验。

操作系统感觉敏捷且响应迅速。

应用程序立即启动，不再让你等待。

复制、搜索和归档等文件操作完成得快得多。

多任务处理更加流畅，因为操作系统可以快速将数据交换进出随机存取存储器。

即使是在配备旧款中央处理器的普通电脑上，升级到固态硬盘也会带来巨大的差异。

这通常是你能为旧系统所做的最佳单一升级。

NAND闪存根据每个单元存储的位数分为不同类型。

单层单元，即SLC，每个单元存储一位，提供最高的速度、耐用性和可靠性，但价格昂贵，主要用于企业应用。

多层单元，即MLC，每个单元存储两位，平衡了性能和成本。三层单元，即TLC，每个单元存储三位，是消费级固态硬盘的标准。

它以实惠的价格提供良好的性能。

四层单元，即QLC，每个单元存储四位，优先考虑容量和成本而非耐用性。

闪存的限制在于写入耐用性。

每个单元在磨损之前只能被写入有限的次数。

SLC单元可持续十万次写入周期，MLC为一万次，TLC为三千次，QLC为一千次。

这听起来令人担忧，但在实践中，消费级固态硬盘在正常使用下可持续多年。

一个额定写入量为一百五十太字节的五百吉字节TLC固态硬盘，意味着你可以每天写入八十吉字节，持续五年才会达到额定耐用度。

大多数用户的写入量远少于这个数值。

固态硬盘控制器使用磨损均衡算法来延长驱动器寿命。

磨损均衡确保所有闪存单元被均匀使用，而不是反复写入相同的单元。

控制器跟踪每个块被写入的次数，并故意将写入操作分散到整个驱动器上。

它还会移动静态数据，即那些很少变化的文件，将其移到重度使用的单元，同时将新写入指向较少使用的单元。

这显著延长了固态硬盘的实际使用寿命。

除了速度之外，固态硬盘还提供了众多优势。

它们是静音的。

没有活动部件意味着没有任何噪音。

它们具有抗震性。

掉落装有固态硬盘的笔记本电脑不会像装有机械硬盘那样损坏驱动器。

它们更轻、更紧凑。

它们消耗更少的功率，固态硬盘为二到四瓦，而机械硬盘为六到十瓦，可将笔记本电脑的电池寿命延长三十分钟到一小时。

它们产生的热量更少，并且更可靠，因为没有可能故障的机械部件。

固态硬盘并非完美无缺。

每吉字节的成本高于机械硬盘，目前固态硬盘约为每吉字节十到十五美分，而机械硬盘为三到五美分。

最大容量较低。

消费级固态硬盘的容量上限约为四到八太字节，而机械硬盘可达十八太字节或更多。

写入耐用性有限，尽管这对于典型用户来说很少成为问题。

并且由于数据在闪存芯片上的分布和加密方式，从故障固态硬盘中恢复数据比从机械硬盘中恢复更困难且更昂贵。

固态硬盘适用于任何重视性能的场景。

将固态硬盘用作操作系统和应用程序的主驱动器。

这是影响最大的升级。

在笔记本电脑中使用固态硬盘以获得速度、电池寿命和抗震性。

在游戏机中使用固态硬盘以减少加载时间。

在视频编辑中使用固态硬盘，因为你不断需要读写大文件。

即使是预算有限的系统，也能受益于使用小容量固态硬盘作为系统盘，搭配大容量机械硬盘用于文件存储。

这就是固态硬盘技术。

请记住，固态硬盘使用没有活动部件的NAND闪存，提供比机械硬盘快得多的性能，随机访问速度快一百倍。

NAND类型包括SLC、MLC、TLC和QLC，每种类型每个单元存储更多的位，但耐用性降低。

磨损均衡技术通过均匀分布写入操作来延长固态硬盘寿命。

固态硬盘比机械硬盘更快、更安静、更耐用、更轻且更节能，但每吉字节成本更高且最大容量更低。

对于重视速度的主存储，固态硬盘是明确的选择。

接下来，我们将探索固态硬盘通信接口，包括SATA、NVMe和PCIe。

英文原文

Hey everyone,now let's move from mechanical hard drives to SSDs,solid state drives,the storage technology that's revolutionizing computing.

SSDs have no moving parts using flash memory chips to store data electronically.

They are dramatically faster,more durable,quieter and more power efficient than HTDs.

Understanding SSD technology,its advantages and its limitations helps you make informed storage decisions.

Let's dive into what makes SSDs special.

SSDs store data in NAND flash memory chips,the same technology used in USB flash drives and SD cards,just at a much larger scale and with more sophisticated controllers.

Inside an SSD are multiple flash memory chips connected to a controller chip that manages data storage,retrieval and optimization.

There are no platters,no motors,no moving heads,just solid state electronics.

Data persists even when power is remote,making it true non-volatile storage like HTDs.

NAND flash stores data by trapping electrons in floating gate transistors.

When electrons are present,the cell represents a zero.

When absent,it's a one or vice versa depending on the design.

To write data,the controller applies voltage to inject or remove electrons.

To read data,it measures the charge level of each cell.

Each memory cell can be written and erased only a limited number of times before wearing out.

This is the fundamental limitation of flash technology.

SSDs are spectacularly faster than HTDs in almost every measurable way.

Random access time,the time to locate and retrieve data,is measured in microseconds for SSDs versus milliseconds for HTDs.

That's 100 times faster.

Sequential read speeds for SATA SSDs reach 500 to 550 megabytes per second versus 120 to 160 for HTDs.

NVME SSDs reach 3000 to 7000 megabytes per second.

Boot times drop from a minute or more with HTDs to 10 to 15 seconds with SSDs.

Application launches are nearly instantaneous.

The SSD speed advantage transforms the computing experience.

Operating systems feel snappy and responsive.

Applications launch immediately instead of making you wait.

File operations like copying,searching and archiving complete much faster.

Multitasking is smoother because the OS can quickly swap data in and out of RAM.

Even on a modest computer with an older CPU,upgrading to an SSD makes a dramatic difference.

It's often the single best upgrade you can make to an older system.

NAN flash comes in different types,based on how many bits each cell stores.

SLC single level cell stores one bit per cell,offering the highest speed,endurance and reliability,but it's expensive and used mainly in enterprise applications.

MLC multi-level cell stores 2 bits per cell,balancing performance and cost.TLC triple level cell stores 3 bits per cell and is the standard for consumer SSDs.

Good performance at affordable prices.

QLC quad level cell stores 4 bits per cell prioritizing capacity and cost over endurance.

The limitation of flash memory is write endurance.

Each cell can only be written a finite number of times before wearing out.

SLC cells last for 100000 write cycles,MLC for 10000 cycles,TLC for 3000 cycles and QLC for 1000 cycles.

This sounds concerning,but in practice,consumer SSDs last years of normal use.

A 500GB TLC SSD rated for 150 terabytes written means you could write 80GB per day for 5 years before reaching the rated endurance.

Most users write far less.

SSD controllers use WAR leveling algorithms to extend drive lifespan.

Wear leveling ensures that all flash cells are used evenly rather than repeatedly writing to the same cells.

The controller tracks how many times each block has been written and deliberately spreads writes across the entire drive.

It also moves static data,files that rarely change to heavily used cells while directing new writes to less used cells.

This significantly extends the practical lifespan of SSDs.

Beyond speed,SSDs offer numerous advantages.

They are silent.

No moving parts means no noise whatsoever.

They are shock resistant.

Dropping a laptop with an SSD won't damage the drive like it would with an HTD.

They are lighter and more compact.

They consume less power,2 to 4 watts for SSDs versus 6 to 10 watts for HTDs,improving laptop battery life by 30 minutes to an hour.

They generate less heat and they are more reliable because there are no mechanical components to fail.

SSDs aren't perfect.

Cost per gigabyte is higher than HTDs,currently 10 to 15 cents per gigabyte for SSDs versus 3 to 5 cents for HTDs.

Maximum capacities are lower.

Consumer SSDs top out around 4 to 8 terabytes while HTDs reach 18 terabytes or more.

Write endurance is limited,though this rarely matters for typical users.

and data recovery from failed SSDs is more difficult and expensive than from HTDs because of how data is distributed and encrypted across flash chips.

SSDs are ideal for any scenario where performance matters.

Use an SSD as your primary drive for the operating system and applications.

This is the most impactful upgrade.

Use SSDs in laptops for speed,battery life,and shock resistance.

Use SSDs for gaming to reduce load times.

Use SSDs for video editing where you are constantly reading and writing large files.

Even budget systems benefit from a small SSD for the OS paired with a large HDD for file storage.

That's SSD technology.

Remember,SSDs use NAND flash memory with no moving parts,delivering dramatically faster performance than HTDs,100 times faster random access.

NAND types include SLC,MLC,TLC and QLC,each storing more bits per cell but with reduced endurance.

Wear leveling technology extends SSD lifespan by evenly distributing writes.

SSDs are faster,quieter,more durable,lighter and more power efficient than HTDs,but they cost more per gigabyte and have lower maximum capacities.

For primary storage where speed matters,SSDs are the clear choice.

Next,we'll explore SSD communication interfaces including SATA,NVMe and PCIe.

See you there.

139. SSD 通信接口

大家好，固态硬盘提供了惊人的性能，但这种性能取决于固态硬盘如何连接到你的计算机，也就是接口。

不同的接口具有不同的速度能力。

SATA是传统接口，性能良好，而基于PCIe的NVMe则提供尖端速度，能充分释放固态硬盘的潜力。

了解这些接口有助于你选择正确的固态硬盘并避免瓶颈。

让我们逐一探讨每个接口。

SATA是我们之前讨论硬盘时使用过的相同接口。

SATA固态硬盘使用与SATA机械硬盘完全相同的连接器和线缆，使其成为直接替换件。

当前版本的SATA三支持六Gbps的理论带宽，扣除开销后，实际传输速度约为每秒五百五十到六百兆字节。

SATA固态硬盘易于安装、兼容性广泛，且比任何机械硬盘都快得多，是旧系统升级的绝佳选择。SATA固态硬盘的顺序读写速度上限约为每秒五百五十兆字节。

每块SATA固态硬盘都会遇到这个瓶颈，因为这是接口的限制，而非驱动器的限制。

对于随机访问和小文件操作，SATA固态硬盘仍然完胜机械硬盘，提供出色的响应速度。

然而，SATA现在已成为瓶颈。

现代闪存能够实现更快的速度，但SATA无法提供这些速度。

这就是为什么开发了像NVMe这样的新接口。

SATA固态硬盘非常适合几种场景。

升级带有SATA连接的旧电脑，你无需更换主板即可获得比机械硬盘巨大的性能提升。

在无法使用或负担不起NVMe的预算型组装中。

作为峰值速度不关键的次要存储驱动器。

以及任何需要广泛兼容性和简单安装的情况。

SATA固态硬盘是一项成熟、可靠且经济实惠的技术，为大多数用户提供出色的实际性能。

PCIe，即外围组件互连快速，是用于显卡、网卡和其他组件的高速扩展总线。

PCIe提供的带宽远大于SATA。

PCIe以通道模式运行，包括乘一、乘四、乘八、乘十六，其中在PCIe三点零中，每个通道提供约每秒一吉字节，在PCIe四点零中为每秒二吉字节，在PCIe五点零中为每秒四吉字节。

一个乘四的连接根据代际不同，可提供四、八或十六吉字节每秒的带宽。

这种巨大的带宽使固态硬盘的性能远超SATA。

NVMe，即非易失性内存主机控制器接口规范，是专为使用PCIe接口的固态硬盘设计的通信协议。

SATA及其旧协议是为高延迟的旋转硬盘设计的，当用于低延迟的固态硬盘时会导致效率低下。

NVMe是从头开始为闪存存储构建的，具有简化的命令、更低的中央处理器开销以及对巨大队列深度的支持。

基于PCIe的NVMe是高性能固态硬盘的现代标准。

NVMe固态硬盘提供令人难以置信的性能。

PCIe三点零乘四的NVMe驱动器读取速度可达每秒三千到三千五百兆字节，写入速度为每秒两千到三千兆字节，比SATA快五到六倍。

PCIe四点零的NVMe驱动器将此速度翻倍，读取速度达每秒七千兆字节，写入速度达每秒五千兆字节。

PCIe五点零驱动器开始出现，速度超过每秒一万兆字节。

除了原始速度之外，NVMe还提供比SATA更低的延迟和更好的随机性能。

NVMe的速度对典型用途重要吗？

对于基本计算、网页浏览、办公工作、电子邮件，SATA固态硬盘已经非常快，NVMe并没有提供明显的好处。

然而，NVMe在特定场景中表现出色，例如传输四K视频等超大文件，加载包含大量资源的巨型游戏关卡，编译大型软件项目，运行虚拟机，批量处理高分辨率照片，以及任何涉及持续读写大量数据的工作流程。

对于这些用例，NVMe提供了可衡量的时间节省。

NVMe固态硬盘有不同的物理形态。M.2是最常见的，是一种小型的棒状模块，直接插入主板上的M.2插槽。

我们将在下一讲中详细讨论M.2。

U.2是一种二点五英寸的外形规格，用于企业环境，提供大容量和热插拔安装功能。

PCIe附加卡允许你在主板缺乏M.2连接时，将NVMe驱动器安装到PCIe插槽中。

无论物理形态如何，接口都是基于PCIe的NVMe。

SAS，即串行连接SCSI，是一种企业级存储接口，主要用于服务器和高端工作站。

SAS支持硬盘和固态硬盘，速度高达每秒十二吉比特，比SATA快但比NVMe慢。

SAS提供了对企业环境至关重要的功能：全双工通信，允许同时读写；用于冗余的双端口配置；更长的线缆距离；以及企业级可靠性功能。

SAS不出现在消费级系统中。它严格属于专业和技术服务器领域。

SAS用于那些可靠性、冗余性和可管理性比绝对峰值性能更重要的环境。

拥有大型存储阵列的企业服务器使用SAS，是因为其先进的功能和经过验证的可靠性。

高可用性系统受益于SAS双端口配置，该配置提供冗余连接。

SAS控制器和扩展器允许在复杂配置中连接数十甚至数百个驱动器。

对于消费者和专业消费者用途，NVMe的重要性已经取代了SAS。

这就是固态硬盘通信接口。

请记住，SATA是传统接口，使用与机械硬盘相同的连接，速度上限约为每秒五百五十兆字节。

非常适合升级和预算型组装。

NVMe是专为固态硬盘设计的现代协议，运行在PCIe接口上，根据PCIe代际不同，速度从每秒三千到超过一万兆字节不等。

PCIe提供物理连接，通道数决定带宽。

乘四是固态硬盘的标准配置。

SAS是带有可靠性功能的服务器企业级接口。

对于新组装的电脑，选择NVMe以获得最大性能。

对于升级，SATA固态硬盘相比机械硬盘仍能提供巨大的改进。

接下来，我们将探索固态硬盘的外形规格，包括M.2驱动器。

届时见。

英文原文

Hey everyone,SSDs offer amazing performance,but that performance depends on how the SSD connects to your computer,the interface.

Different interfaces have different speed capabilities.

SATA is the traditional interface with good performance,while NVMe over PCIe offers cutting-edge speed that fully unleashes SSD potential.

Understanding these interfaces helps you choose the right SSD and avoid bottlenecks.

Let's explore each interface.

SATA is the same interface we discussed for hard drives.

SATA SSDs use the exact same connectors and cables as SATA HDDs,making them drop-in replacements.

SATA 3,the current version,supports 6Gbps theoretical bandwidth,which translates to about 550 to 600MB per second actual transfer speed after overhead.

SATA SSDs are easy to install,widely compatible and significantly faster than any HDD,making them a great upgrade for older systems.SATA SSDs max out at around 550MB per second sequential read and write speeds.

Every SATA SSD hits this wall because it's the interface limit,not the drives limit.

For random access and small file operations,SATA SSDs still demolish HDDs providing excellent responsiveness.

However,SATA is now a bottleneck.

Modern flash memory is capable of much faster speeds but SATA can't deliver them.

This is why newer interfaces like NVMe were developed.

SATA SSDs are perfect for several scenarios.

Upgrading older computers with SATA connections,you get a huge performance boost over HDDs without needing a new motherboard.

Budget builds where NVMe isn't available or affordable.

Secondary storage drives where peak speed isn't critical.

And any situation where you need broad compatibility and simple installation.

SATA SSDs are mature,reliable and affordable technology that provides excellent real-world performance for most users.

PCIe Peripheral Component Interconnect Express is the high-speed expansion bus used for graphics cards,network cards and other components.

PCIe provides much more bandwidth than SATA.

PCIE operates in lanes X1,X4,X8,X16 with each lane providing about 1 GB per second in PCIe 3.0,2 GB per second in PCIe 4.0 and 4GB per second in PCIe 5.0.

An X4 connection provides 48 or 16 GB per second depending on generation.

This enormous bandwidth enables SSD performance far beyond SATA.

NVME Non-Volatile Memory Express is a communication protocol specifically designed for SSDs using the PCIe interface.

SATA and its older protocols were designed for spinning hard drives with high latency,leading to inefficiencies when used with low latency SSDs.

NVME was built from the ground up for flash storage with streamlined commands,lower CPU overhead and support for massive queue depths.

NVME over PCIe is the modern standard for high performance SSDs.

NVMe SSDs deliver incredible performance.

PCIe 3.0x4 NVMe drives reach 3000 to 3500 megabytes per second reads and 2000 to 3000 megabytes per second writes,5 to 6 times faster than SATA.

PCIe 4.0 NVMe drives double that to 7000MB per second reads and 5000MB per second writes.

PCIe 5.0 drives are starting to appear with speeds exceeding 10000 megabytes per second.

Beyond raw speed,NVMe offers lower latency and better random performance than SATA.

Does NVMe speed matter for typical use?

For basic computing,web browsing,office work,email,SATA SSTs are already so fast that NVMe doesn't provide a noticeable benefit.

However,NVMe shines in specific scenarios,transferring huge files like 4K video,loading massive game levels with lots of assets,compiling large software projects,running virtual machines,working with high resolution photos in batches,and any workflow involving constantly reading and writing large amounts of data.

For these use cases,NVMe provides measurable time savings.

NVMe SSDs come in different physical forms.M.2 is the most common,small,stick-like modules that plug directly into M.2 slots on motherboards.

We'll discuss M.2 in detail in the next lecture.

U.2 is a 2.5-inch form factor used in enterprise environments,offering high capacity and hot swappable installation.

PCIe add-in cards let you install NVMe drives in PCIe slots if your motherboard lacks M.2 connections.

The interface is NVMe over PCIe regardless of physical form factor.

SAS serial attached SCSI is an enterprise storage interface primarily used in servers and high-end workstations.

SAS supports both hard drives and SSDs with speeds up to 12 gigabits per second,faster than SATA but slower than NVMe.

SaaS offers features important for enterprise environments full duplex communication,allowing simultaneous read and write,dual port configurations for redundancy,longer cable distances,and enterprise reliability features.

SAS is not found in consumer systems.It's strictly a professional and server technology.

SAS is used in environments where reliability,redundancy,and manageability matter more than absolute peak performance.

Enterprise servers with large storage arrays use SAS because of its advanced features and proven reliability.

High availability systems benefit from SAS dual port configurations that provide redundant connections.

SAS controllers and expanders allow connecting dozens or hundreds of drives in complex configurations.

For consumer and prosumer use,NVMe has replaced SAS in importance.

That's SSD communication interfaces.

Remember,SATA is the traditional interface using the same connections as HTDs,maxing out around 550MB per second.

Excellent for upgrades and budget builds.

NVME is the modern protocol designed specifically for SSDs,running over the PCIe interface with speeds from 3000 to over 1✓,000MB per second depending on PCIe generation.

PCIe provides the physical connectivity with lanes determining bandwidth.

Time 4 is standard for SSDs.

SAS is an enterprise interface for servers with reliability features.

For new builds,choose NVMe for maximum performance.

For upgrades,SATA SSDs still provide huge improvements over HDDs.

140. SSD 外形规格

大家好，我们之前已经讨论了SSD接口，包括SATA和NVMe。

现在让我们讨论SSD的物理形状。

外形规格决定了您可以如何以及在哪里安装SSD。

我们有传统的二点五英寸驱动器、紧凑的M.2模块、较旧的mSATA驱动器以及企业级U.2驱动器。

了解这些外形规格有助于您识别哪些SSD与您的系统兼容，并选择合适的升级方案。

让我们逐一探讨每种类型。

二点五英寸外形规格是大多数人想到SSD时的印象。

这些驱动器看起来像笔记本电脑硬盘，是矩形金属或塑料外壳，宽二点七五英寸，深三点九英寸，通常高七毫米。

它们拥有与硬盘相同的SATA数据和电源连接器。

二点五英寸SATA SSD是旧系统最简单的升级方案。您只需拔掉旧硬盘，插上SSD即可。

它们适用于任何拥有二点五英寸或三点五英寸驱动器托架和SATA连接的系统。

二点五英寸SSD提供广泛的兼容性。

它们适用于台式机、笔记本电脑和外部硬盘盒。

它们易于安装，无需特殊知识。

它们适用于缺乏M.2插槽的旧主板。

它们提供高达四到八太字节的大容量，而且通常比同等容量的M.2驱动器更便宜。

对于升级旧笔记本电脑或台式机，二点五英寸SATA SSD通常是最简单且最具成本效益的选择。

M.2是为空间受限设备中的SSD设计的现代紧凑外形规格。

M.2驱动器是小型矩形电路板，像口香糖条一样，直接插入主板上的M.2插槽。

它们没有外部外壳，没有线缆，只是一块一面或两面带有芯片的裸露电路板。

M.2插槽同时提供机械固定和电气连接。

M.2支持SATA和NVMe两种接口，这一点非常重要。

M.2驱动器有不同的长度，由四位数字表示。

前两位数字表示宽度（单位为毫米），始终为二十二，后两位表示长度。

M.2二二八零的宽度为二十二毫米，长度为八十毫米。

这是最常见的尺寸。

M.2二二六零的长度为六十毫米。

M.2二二四二的长度为四十二毫米。

驱动器越长，能容纳的芯片就越多，从而实现更高的容量。

大多数主板通过多个安装螺丝位置支持多种长度。

这里是M.2令人困惑的地方。

物理连接器具有不同的防呆缺口（Keying），决定了驱动器支持的接口类型。

M.2 SATA驱动器具有B键和M键，即连接器边缘的缺口。

M.2 NVMe驱动器通常只有M键。

主板上的M.2插槽也有防呆缺口。

有些仅支持SATA，有些仅支持NVMe，有些则两者都支持。

您必须使驱动器的防呆缺口与插槽的防呆缺口相匹配。

防呆缺口可防止安装不兼容的驱动器，但也意味着您不能假设所有M.2驱动器和插槽都兼容。

如何知道M.2驱动器或插槽支持SATA还是NVMe？

请查阅主板手册。

它会指定哪些M.2插槽支持哪些接口。

查看插槽标记。

有些主板将插槽标记为SATA、NVMe或仅NVMe。

检查驱动器规格。

制造商会明确说明是SATA还是NVMe。

物理防呆缺口提供线索。

B键支持SATA，M键支持NVMe或SATA，B加M键支持SATA。

购买M.2驱动器时，请验证其与主板的兼容性。

一旦找到插槽，安装M.2驱动器非常简单。

在主板上找到M.2插槽，通常位于CPU和GPU之间，有时在散热片盖下方。

卸下适当长度位置的安装螺丝。

以大约三十度的角度插入M.2驱动器，将缺口与插槽的防呆键对齐。

将驱动器推入连接器，直到完全就位。

将驱动器向下压平贴紧主板，并用安装螺丝固定。

无需线缆。

您就完成了。

mSATA是一种较旧的紧凑SSD外形规格，早于M.2出现。

mSATA驱动器外观与M.2相似，但连接器不同。

它类似于Mini PCIe卡，但缺口位置不同。

mSATA驱动器仅支持SATA速度，不支持NVMe。

它们在二零一一年至二零一五年左右的笔记本电脑和紧凑系统中很常见，之后被M.2取代。

在处理旧笔记本电脑时您会遇到mSATA，但新系统不再使用mSATA。

U.2是一种企业级SSD外形规格，看起来像二点五英寸驱动器，但使用不同的连接器。

U.2驱动器通过PCIe支持NVMe，在熟悉的二点五英寸外形中提供高性能。

U.2连接器在单个高速连接中结合了数据和电源。

U.2驱动器支持热插拔。

您可以在系统运行时移除和插入它们，这使它们在服务器中非常流行。

由于较大的尺寸可以容纳更多闪存芯片，它们提供比M.2更高的容量。

U.2纯粹是一项企业级技术。

有些SSD以PCIe附加卡的形式出现，像显卡一样插入PCIe插槽。

这些本质上是安装在PCIe适配器卡上的M.2 NVMe驱动器，通常带有用于散热的散热片。

当您的主板缺乏M.2插槽或已用完所有可用M.2插槽时，PCIe卡式SSD非常有用。

它们也适用于那些不支持在M.2插槽中使用NVMe但可以从PCIe设备启动的旧系统。

如果使用相同的控制器和闪存，其性能与M.2 NVMe驱动器相同。

以上就是SSD外形规格。

请记住，二点五英寸SATA SSD是传统外形规格，具有广泛的兼容性和易于安装的特点。

M.2是现代紧凑外形规格，根据防呆缺口的不同支持SATA或NVMe。

常见尺寸为二二八零、二二六零和二二四二。

M.2插槽和驱动器必须在接口（SATA或NVMe）和物理防呆缺口上兼容。

mSATA是在旧笔记本电脑中发现的旧版迷你SATA格式。

U.2是用于NVMe驱动器的企业级二点五英寸外形规格，具有热插拔功能。

PCIe附加卡让您可以在PCIe插槽中使用NVMe SSD。

在购买SSD之前，请查阅主板规格以确定其支持的外形规格和接口。

接下来，我们将深入探讨用于组合多个驱动器的RAID配置。

英文原文

Hey everyone,we've talked about SSD interfaces,SATA and NVMe.

Now let's discuss the physical shapes SSDs come in.

Form factor determines how and where you can install an SSD.

We have traditional 2.5 inch drives,compact M.2 modules,older M SATA drives and enterprise U.2 drives.

Understanding these form factors helps you identify what SSDs are compatible with your system and choose the right upgrade.

Let's explore each type.

The 2.5 inch form factor is what most people think of when they picture an SSD.

These drives look like laptop hard drives,rectangular metal or plastic enclosures measuring 2.75 inches wide,3.9 inches deep and typically 7 millimeters tall.

They have SATA data and power connectors just like hard drives.

2.5 inch SATA SSDs are the easiest upgrade for older systems.You literally unplug your old hard drive and plug in the SSD.

They work in any system with a 2.5 inch or 3.5 inch drive bay and SATA connections.

2.5 inch SSDs offer broad compatibility.

They work in desktops,laptops and external enclosures.

They are easy to install with no special knowledge required.

They work with older motherboards that lack M.2 slots.

They are available in large capacities up to 4 to 8 terabytes and they are often less expensive than equivalent M.2 drives.

For upgrading an older laptop or desktop,a 2.5 inch SATA SSD is usually the simplest and most cost-effective option.

M.2 is the modern compact form factor designed for SSDs in space constrained devices.

M.2 drives are small rectangular circuit boards like sticks of gum that plug directly into M.2 slots on motherboards.

They have no external enclosure,no cables,just a bare circuit board with chips on one or both sides.

M.2 slots provide both mechanical mounting and electrical connection.

M.2 supports both SATA and NVMe interfaces which is important to understand.

M.2 drives come in different lengths designated by four digit numbers.

The first two digits indicate width in millimeters,always 22 and the last two indicate length.

M.22280 is 22 millimeters wide and 80 millimeters long.

This is the most common size.

M.22260 is 60 millimeters long.

M.22242 is 42 millimeters long.

The longer the drive,the more chips it can hold,allowing higher capacities.

Most motherboards support multiple lengths with multiple mounting screw positions.

Here's where M.2 gets confusing.

The physical connector has different keying that determines what interfaces the drive supports.

M.2 SATA drives have B and M keys,notches in the connector edge.

M.2 NVMe drives typically have only an M key.

M.2 slots on motherboards are also keyed.

Some support only SATA,some only NVMe,some support both.

You must match the drive keying to the slot keying.

The key prevents installing incompatible drives,but it also means you can't assume all M.2 drives and slots are compatible.

How do you know if an M.2 drive or slot supports SATA or NVMe?

Check the motherboard manual.

It specifies which M.2 slots support which interfaces.

Look at the slot markings.

Some motherboards label slots as SATA NVMe or NVMe only.

Examine the drive specifications.

Manufacturers clearly state SATA or NVMe.

The physical key notches provide clues.

B key supports SATA,M key supports NVMe or SATA,B plus M supports SATA.

When buying M.2 drives,verify compatibility with your motherboard.

Installing M.2 drives is straightforward once you find the slot.

Locate the M.2 slot on your motherboard,usually between the CPU and GPU,sometimes under a heatsink cover.

Remove the mounting screw at the appropriate length position.

Insert the M.2 drive at about a 30-degree angle,aligning the notches with the slot keys.

Push the drive into the connector until it's fully seated.

Press the drive down flat against the motherboard and secure it with a mounting screw.

No cables required.

You're done.

M SATATA is an older compact SSD form factor that preceded M.2.

M SATA drives look similar to M.2 but with a different connector.

It resembles a mini PCIe card with a different notch position.

M SATA drives only support SATA speeds,not NVMe.

They were common in laptops and compact systems from around 2011 to 2015 before M.2 replaced them.

You'll encounter M SATA when working with older laptops but new systems don't use MSATA anymore.

U.2 is an enterprise SSD form factor that looks like a 2.5-inch drive but uses a different connector.

U.2 drives support NVME over PCIe delivering high performance in the familiar 2.5 inch shape.

The U.2 connector combines data and power in a single high speed connection.

U.2 drives are hot swappable.

You can remove and insert them while the system is running,making them popular in servers.

they offer higher capacities than M point two because the larger size accommodates more flash chips.

U.2 is exclusively an enterprise technology.

Some SSDs come as PCIe add-in cards that plug into PCIe slots like a graphics card.

These are essentially M.2 NVMe drives mounted on PCIe adapter cards,often with heatsinks for cooling.

PCIe card SSDs are useful when your motherboard lacks M.2 slots or you've used all available M.2 slots.

They also work in older systems that don't support NVMe in M.2 slots but can boot from PCIe devices.

Performance is identical to M.2 NVMe drives using the same controller and flash.

That's SSD form factors.

Remember,2.5-inch SATA SSDs are the traditional form factor with broad compatibility and easy installation.

M.2 is the modern compact form factor supporting SATA or NVMe depending on keying.

Common sizes are 22802260 and 2242.

M.2 slots and drives must be compatible by interface,SATA or NVMe and physical keying.

MSATA is an older mini SATA format found in older laptops.

U.2 is an Enterprise 2.5-inch form factor for NVMe drives with hot swap capability.

PCIe add-in cards let you use NVMe SSDs in PCIe slots.

Check your motherboard specifications to determine what form factors and interfaces it supports before buying SSDs.

Next,we'll dive into RAID configurations for combining multiple drives.

141. RAID 配置

大家好，让我们来谈谈RAID，即独立磁盘冗余阵列，这是一项将多个物理驱动器组合成单个逻辑单元的技术。

RAID可以提高性能、为数据保护提供冗余，或者两者兼而有之。

了解常见的RAID级别有助于您设计满足特定速度、容量和可靠性需求的存储系统。

RAID用于服务器、工作站，甚至一些发烧友台式机系统。让我们探讨主要的RAID配置。

RAID的开发旨在解决两个基本的存储问题。第一是性能。

单个驱动器存在局限性，但结合多个驱动器协同工作可以显著提高吞吐量。

第二是可靠性。

所有驱动器最终都会故障，但RAID可以通过在多个驱动器上冗余存储数据来保护数据，这样当一个驱动器故障时，不会丢失任何数据。不同的RAID级别在性能、冗余、容量和成本之间做出不同的权衡。

RAID 0被称为条带化，因为数据被分成块并分散（条带化）到多个驱动器上。

如果您在RAID 0中有两个驱动器，第一个块去往驱动器一，第二个块去往驱动器二，第三个块去往驱动器一，依此类推。

这提供了卓越的性能。

两个驱动器同时工作，读写速度大约翻倍。

然而，RAID 0不提供任何冗余。

如果任一驱动器故障，两个驱动器上的所有数据都将丢失。RAID 0用可靠性换取速度。

RAID 0适用于性能至关重要且数据丢失可接受的特定场景。

视频编辑工作站使用RAID 0作为暂存盘，存放可以重新创建的临时项目文件。

游戏系统有时使用RAID 0来加快加载时间，尽管单个快速固态硬盘通常更好。

适用于您处理的数据已在别处备份，且需要最高速度的情况。

切勿对不可替代的数据使用RAID 0。

它实际上增加了数据丢失的风险。

RAID 1被称为镜像，因为数据在两个驱动器上被复制（镜像）。

每次写入都会发送到两个驱动器，从而创建完美的冗余。

如果一个驱动器故障，另一个驱动器拥有所有数据的完整副本。

您可以移除故障驱动器，更换它，并重建阵列而不会丢失任何东西。

RAID 1提供出色的数据保护。

其代价是容量。

使用两块一太字节的驱动器，您只获得一太字节的可用空间，因为一半的容量用于复制。

RAID 1。

读取性能可能比单个驱动器更快，因为读取可以在两个驱动器之间分配。

写入性能与单个驱动器相似，因为数据必须写入两个驱动器。

RAID 1非常适合必须受保护的关键数据。

例如服务器中的操作系统驱动器、数据库存储、商业文档以及任何数据丢失将是灾难性但不需要巨大容量的场景。

RAID 1简单、可靠并提供安心保障。

RAID 5结合性能和冗余，使用带有分布式奇偶校验的条带化。

RAID 5至少需要三块驱动器。

数据像RAID 0一样在所有驱动器上进行条带化，但对于每个条带，会计算奇偶校验信息并存储在其中一块驱动器上。

奇偶校验位置会在各驱动器间轮换。

驱动器一存储条带一的奇偶校验，驱动器二存储条带二的奇偶校验，依此类推。

如果任何单块驱动器故障，可以使用奇偶校验信息从剩余驱动器中通过数学方式重建数据。

RAID 5提供良好的容量效率。

使用三块一太字节的驱动器，您可获得两太字节的可用空间。

相当于一块驱动器的容量用于奇偶校验。

使用四块驱动器，您可获得三太字节的可用空间。

公式是总容量减去一块驱动器。

读取性能卓越，类似于RAID 0，因为数据跨多个驱动器进行条带化。

写入性能比RAID 0慢，因为控制器必须计算奇偶校验，但仍优于单个驱动器。

RAID 5在容量、性能和冗余之间提供了极佳的平衡。

RAID 5有一个重要的局限性。

它仅能防止单块驱动器故障。

如果在第一块驱动器被更换和重建之前第二块驱动器也发生故障，所有数据都将丢失。故障后重建RAID 5阵列会给剩余驱动器带来压力，对于大型阵列可能需要数小时，在此期间阵列处于脆弱状态。

此外，RAID 5的写入性能会受到奇偶校验计算开销的影响。

出于这些原因，对于关键数据，通常更倾向于使用RAID 6和RAID 10。

RAID 6类似于RAID 5，但使用两个奇偶校验块而不是一个，从而提供针对两块驱动器同时故障的保护。

RAID 6至少需要四块驱动器。

使用四块一太字节的驱动器，您可获得两太字节的可用空间。

相当于两块驱动器的容量用于奇偶校验。

额外的奇偶校验提供了比RAID 5好得多的可靠性，使其对于重建时间较长的大型阵列更安全。

其代价是容量效率略低，且由于要计算两个奇偶校验块，写入性能稍慢。

RAID 10，也称为RAID一加零，结合了RAID 1和RAID 0。

它至少需要四块驱动器。

首先，使用RAID 1将驱动器配对成镜像集。

然后，使用RAID 0将这些镜像对一起进行条带化。

这同时提供了冗余和性能。

只要没有镜像对失去两块驱动器，RAID十就能承受多次驱动器故障。

读写性能都非常出色。

容量的代价很大。

使用四块一太字节的驱动器，您只获得两太字节的可用空间，因为一半的容量用于镜像。

那么如何选择呢？

RAID 0。

当数据丢失可接受时，提供最大性能。

RAID 1。

使用两块驱动器为关键数据提供简单的冗余。

RAID 5。

为三块或更多驱动器提供性能、容量和冗余的平衡。

适用于文件服务器和工作站。

RAID 6。

当您需要防止两块驱动器故障时，提供比RAID 5更好的可靠性。

是大型阵列的首选。

RAID 10。

当预算允许时，提供带有冗余的最大性能。

是数据库和高性能服务器的理想选择。

请记住，RAID不是备份。

它可防止硬件故障，但不能防止删除、损坏或灾难。

以上就是RAID配置。

请记住，RAID 0跨驱动器条带化数据以提高性能，但没有冗余。

如果任何驱动器故障，数据将丢失。

RAID 1跨两块驱动器镜像数据以实现冗余，可用容量减半。

RAID 5使用带有分布式奇偶校验的条带化，跨越三块或更多驱动器。

可承受一块驱动器故障，具有良好的容量效率。

RAID 6使用双重奇偶校验来防止两块驱动器故障。

需要四块或更多驱动器。

RAID 10结合镜像和条带化，以同时获得性能和冗余。

最少需要四块驱动器。

根据您的优先事项进行选择：性能、容量或冗余。

接下来，我们将讨论可移动存储，包括USB驱动器和SD卡。

英文原文

Hey everyone,let's talk about RAID,redundant array of independent disks,a technology that combines multiple physical drives into a single logical unit.

RAID can improve performance,provide redundancy for data protection or both.

Understanding the common RAID levels helps you design storage systems that meet specific needs for speed,capacity and reliability.

RAID is used in servers,workstations and even some enthusiast desktop systems.Let's explore the main RAID configurations.

RAID was developed to solve two fundamental storage problems.First,performance.

Individual drives have limitations,but combining multiple drives working together can dramatically increase throughput.

Second,reliability.

All drives eventually fail,but RAID can protect data by storing it redundantly across multiple drives so that when one fails,no data is lost.Different RAID levels make different trade-offs between performance,redundancy,capacity,and cost.

RAID 0 is called striping because data is divided into blocks and spread striped across multiple drives.

If you have two drives in RAID 0,the first block goes to drive 1,the second block goes to drive 2,third to drive 1 and so on.

This provides excellent performance.

Both drives work simultaneously,roughly doubling read and write speeds.

However,RAID 0 provides zero redundancy.

If either drive fails,all data across both drives is lost.RAID 0 trades reliability for speed.

RAID 0 makes sense in specific scenarios where performance matters and data loss is acceptable.

Video editing workstations use RAID 0 for scratch disks holding temporary project files that can be recreated.

Gaming systems sometimes use RAID 0 for faster load times,though a single fast SSD is often better.

Situations where you are working with data that's backed up elsewhere and you need maximum speed.

Never use RAID 0 for irreplaceable data.

It actually increases your risk of data loss.

RAID 1 is called mirroring because data is duplicated,mirrored,across two drives.

Every write goes to both drives,creating perfect redundancy.

If one drive fails,the other has a complete copy of all data.

You can remove the failed drive,replace it,and rebuild the array without losing anything.

RAID 1 provides excellent data protection.

The trade-off is capacity.

With two 1TB drives,you only get 1TB of usable space since half the capacity is used for duplication.

RAID 1.

Read performance can be faster than a single drive because reads can be split between both drives.

Write performance is similar to a single drive since data must be written to both.

RAID 1 is perfect for critical data that must be protected.

Operating system drives in servers,database storage,business documents and any scenario where losing data would be catastrophic,but you don't need massive capacity.

RAID 1 is simple,reliable and provides peace of mind.

RAID 5 combines performance and redundancy using striping with distributed parity.

RAID 5 requires at least 3 drives.

Data is striped across all drives like RAID 0,but for each stripe,parity information is calculated and stored on one of the drives.

The parity location rotates across drives.

Drive 1 stores parity for stripe 1,drive 2 for stripe 2 and so on.

If any single drive fails,the data can be mathematically reconstructed from the remaining drives using the parity information.

RAID 5 provides good capacity efficiency.

With three 1TB drives,you get 2TB usable.

1 drive's worth is used for parity.

With 4 drives,you get 3 terabytes usable.

The formula is total capacity minus 1 drive.

Read performance is excellent,similar to RAID 0,because data is striped across multiple drives.

Write performance is slower than RAID 0 because the controller must calculate parity,but it's still better than a single drive.

RAID 5 offers a great balance of capacity,performance and redundancy.

RAID 5 has an important limitation.

It only protects against a single drive failure.

If a second drive fails before the first is replaced and rebuilt,all data is lost.Rebuilding RAID 5 arrays after a failure is stressful on the remaining drives and can take many hours for large arrays,during which time the array is vulnerable.

Additionally,RAID 5 write performance suffers from the parity calculation overhead.

For these reasons,RAID 6 and RAID 10 are often preferred for critical data.

RAID 6 is similar to RAID 5 but uses 2 parity blocks instead of 1,providing protection against 2 simultaneous drive failures.

RAID 6 requires at least 4 drives.

With 4 1TB drives,you get 2TB usable.

2 drives worth is parity.

The extra parity provides much better reliability than RAID 5,making it safer for large arrays where rebuild times are long.

The trade-off is slightly lower capacity efficiency and somewhat slower write performance due to calculating two parity blocks.

RAID 10,also called RAID 1 plus 0,combines RAID 1 and RAID 0.

It requires at least 4 drives.

First,drives are paired into mirrored sets using RAID 1.

Then those mirrored pairs are striped together using RAID 0.

This provides both redundancy and performance.

RAID ten can survive multiple drive failures as long as no mirrored pair loses both drives.

Performance is excellent for both reads and writes.

The capacity trade-off is significant.

With four 1TB drives,you only get 2TB usable since half the capacity is mirroring.

So how do you choose?

RAID 0.

Maximum performance when data loss is acceptable.

RAID 1.

Simple redundancy for critical data with 2 drives.

RAID 5.

Balanced performance,capacity and redundancy for 3 or more drives.

Good for file servers and workstations.

RAID 6.

Better reliability than RAID 5 when you need to protect against 2 drive failures.

Preferred for large arrays.

RAID 10.

Maximum performance with redundancy when budget allows.

Ideal for databases and high-performance servers.

Remember,RAID is not a backup.

It protects against hardware failure but not deletion,corruption,or disasters.

That's RAID configurations.

Remember,RAID 0 stripes data across drives for performance with no redundancy.

Data loss if any drive fails.

RAID 1 mirrors data across 2 drives for redundancy with half usable capacity.

RAID 5 uses striping with distributed parity across 3 or more drives.

Survives 1 drive failure with good capacity efficiency.

RAID 6 uses dual parity for protection against 2 drive failures.

Requires 4 or more drives.

RAID 10 combines mirroring and striping for both performance and redundancy.

Requires 4 drives minimum.

Choose based on your priorities,performance,capacity or redundancy.

See you there.

142. 可移动存储

大家好，我们目前讨论过的所有存储设备，如机械硬盘、固态硬盘和RAID阵列，都是内部或半永久性的。

现在让我们谈谈可移动存储，它是专为便携性和设备间轻松传输而设计的。

USB闪存盘、SD卡和外部驱动器是移动数据、备份文件以及随时扩展存储的重要工具。

了解它们的类型、功能和用例，有助于您选择合适的便携式存储解决方案。

USB闪存盘，也称为拇指驱动器、笔式驱动器或U盘，是直接插入USB端口的小型便携式存储设备。

其内部包含与固态硬盘类似的NAND闪存、一个控制器芯片和一个USB连接器。

它们的容量从几吉字节到一太字节甚至更高不等。

USB闪存盘在计算机间传输文件、携带文档、创建可启动安装介质和临时存储方面极其方便。

它们价格低廉、耐用，并且可以挂在钥匙扣上。

不同USB闪存盘的性能差异巨大。

使用USB 2.0的廉价驱动器可能每秒只能达到十到三十兆字节。

USB 3.0驱动器的速度范围在每秒五十到一百五十兆字节之间。

高端的USB 3.1或3.2驱动器可以达到每秒三百到四百兆字节或更高。

闪存和控制器的质量会产生巨大影响。

对于经常处理大文件的用户，请投资购买优质的USB 3.0或更新版本的驱动器。

与廉价驱动器相比，速度差异非常显著。

USB闪存盘有一些您需要了解的局限性。

廉价驱动器中的闪存通常质量较低，耐久性差，仅适合偶尔传输，不适合持续重写。

小型驱动器很容易丢失。

如果驱动器在插入时受到碰撞，USB连接器可能会损坏。

它们很容易被偷窃或遗留在公共电脑上，而且当驱动器快满时性能会下降。

对于关键数据，USB驱动器不应是您唯一的副本。

它们很方便，但并不是最可靠的长期存储方式。

SD卡，即安全数字卡，是主要用于相机、智能手机、平板电脑、无人机和便携式设备的小型闪存卡。

标准SD卡的尺寸为三十二乘二十四毫米。

Mini SD和Micro SD是更小的变体。

Micro SD非常小巧，尺寸为十五乘十一毫米，是现代手机和运动相机中最常见的类型。

SD卡与USB驱动器和固态硬盘一样使用NAND闪存，以电子方式存储数据，没有移动部件。

SD卡具有速度等级评级，表明最低持续写入速度。

Class 10保证每秒十兆字节，足以用于高清视频录制。

UHS速度等级1（U1）也保证新卡每秒十兆字节的速度。

UHS速度等级3（U3）保证每秒三十兆字节，这是录制4K视频所必需的。

视频速度等级V30、V60、V90表示高比特率视频所需的最低速度分别为每秒三十、六十或九十兆字节。

请务必使卡的速度与您的设备要求相匹配。

SD卡有三种容量类型，具有不同的规格。

SD卡支持高达二吉字节的容量。

SDHC（高容量）支持四吉字节到三十二吉字节。

SDXC（扩展容量）支持六十四吉字节到二太字节。

这些不仅仅是容量的差异。

旧设备可能仅支持SD或SDHC，而无法识别SDXC卡。

请检查您的设备规格，了解最大支持容量和卡类型。

大多数现代设备都支持SDXC。

Micro SD卡是最小的SD格式，广泛用于智能手机、平板电脑、行车记录仪和无人机。

尽管体积微小，Micro SD卡却提供与全尺寸SD卡相同的容量和速度。

最高可达一太字节。

Micro SD卡附带SD卡适配器套，让您可以在全尺寸SD卡插槽中使用它们。

这种多功能性使得Micro SD非常流行。

一张卡配合适配器可在手机中使用，需要时也可在相机中使用。

外部驱动器是带有USB、USB-C或雷雳连接的便携式存储设备。

它们在带有接口电子元件的保护外壳内包含标准的二点五英寸或三点五英寸驱动器。

外部机械硬盘提供巨大的容量，通常为二到八太字节，成本低廉，非常适合备份和媒体库。

外部固态硬盘在紧凑耐用的包装中提供快速性能，非常适合随时处理大文件或扩展笔记本电脑存储。

许多外部驱动器包含备份软件和密码保护功能。

选择外部驱动器时，请考虑几个因素。

二点五英寸驱动器由总线供电。

它们直接通过USB运行，无需外部电源适配器，因此更便携。

三点五英寸驱动器需要墙壁电源，但以更低的成本提供更高的容量。USB 3.0或更新版本对于合理的传输速度至关重要。

避免将USB 2.0用于存储驱动器。

一些外部固态硬盘使用带有高速接口的USB-C，提供接近内部固态硬盘的性能。

对于备份而言，可靠性比速度更重要。

选择知名品牌并考虑保修期限。

不同的可移动存储适用于不同的需求。

USB闪存盘：在计算机间传输中小型文件、可启动安装介质、临时工作存储。

SD卡：相机、智能手机、无人机、需要扩展存储的便携式设备。

外部机械硬盘：备份存储、归档大型媒体库、传输海量数据。

外部固态硬盘：移动工作站、现场视频编辑、高性能扩展笔记本电脑存储、快速传输大文件。

请根据容量需求、性能要求、便携性和预算进行选择。

以上就是可移动存储。

请记住，USB闪存盘是方便的便携式存储，容量从吉字节到太字节不等。

为了获得良好的性能，请选择USB 3.0或更新版本。

SD卡有SD、SDHC和SDXC容量之分，速度等级表明最低写入速度。

使速度与您的设备要求相匹配。

Micro SD是用于手机和相机的微型格式，通常包含全尺寸适配器。

外部机械硬盘为备份和归档提供巨大容量。

外部固态硬盘提供快速的便携性能。

每种类型服务于不同的需求。

请根据您的具体用例进行选择。

接下来，我们将通过查看光驱（包括CD、DVD和蓝光）来结束本章节。

届时见。

英文原文

Hey everyone,all the storage we have discussed so far HTDs,SSDs,RAID arrays is internal or semi-permanent.

Now let's talk about removable storage that's designed for portability and easy transfer between devices.

USB flash drives,SD cards and external drives are essential tools for moving data,backing up files and expanding storage on the go.

Understanding their types,capabilities and use cases helps you choose the right portable storage solution.

USB flash drives also called thumb drives,pen drives or USB sticks are small portable storage devices that plug directly into USB ports.

Inside is NAND flash memory similar to SSDs,a controller chip and a USB connector.

They range from a few gigabytes to one terabyte or more in capacity.

USB flash drives are incredibly convenient for transferring files between computers,carrying documents,creating bootable insulation media and temporary storage.

They are inexpensive,durable and fit on a keychain.

Performance varies dramatically between USB flash drives.

Budget drives using USB 2.0 might only achieve 10 to 30 megabytes per second.

USB 3.0 drives range from 50 to 150 megabytes per second.

High-end USB 3.1 or 3.2 drives can reach 300 to 400 megabytes or more.

The quality of the flash memory and controller makes a huge difference.

For frequent use with large files,invest in a quality USB 3.0 or newer drive.

The speed difference is dramatic compared to cheap drives.

USB flash drives have limitations you should understand.

The flash memory in cheap drives is often low quality with poor endurance,suitable for occasional transfers but not constant rewriting.

Small drives get lost easily.

USB connectors can be damaged if the drive is bumped while plugged in.

They are easy to steal or leave behind in public computers and performance degrades when drives are nearly full.

For critical data,USB drives shouldn't be your only copy.

They are convenient but not the most reliable long-term storage.

SD cards,secure digital cards,are small flash memory cards used primarily in cameras,smartphones,tablets,drones and portable devices.

Standard SD cards measure 32 by 24 millimeters.

Mini SD and micro SD are smaller variants.

Micro SD is tiny at 15 by 11 millimeters and the most common type in modern phones and action cameras.

S D cards use NAND flash just like USB drives and S S D s,storing data electronically without moving parts.

S D cards have speed class ratings that indicate minimum sustained write speeds.

Class 10 guarantees 10 megabytes per second,adequate for HD video recording.

UHS Speed Class 1 also guarantees 10MB per second on newer cards.

UHS Speed Class 3 U3 guarantees 30MB per second necessary for 4K video recording.

Video speed classes V30,V60,V90 indicate 3060 or 90MB per second minimum speeds for high bitrate video.

Always match the card speed to your device's requirements.

SD cards come in three capacity types with different specifications.

SD cards support up to 2GB.

SDHC high capacity supports 4GB to 32GB.

SDXC extended capacity supports 64GB to 2TB.

These aren't just capacity differences.

Older devices may only support SD or SDHC and won't recognize SDXC cards.

Check your device's specifications for maximum supported capacity and card type.

Most modern devices support SDXC.

Micro SD cards are the smallest SD format used extensively in smartphones,tablets,dash cameras and drones.

Despite their tiny size,micro SD cards offer the same capacities and speeds as full size SD cards.

Up to 1 terabyte is available.

Micro SD cards come with SD card adapter sleeves that let you use them in full size SD card slots.

This versatility makes micro SD popular.

One card works in your phone with the adapter and in your camera when needed.

External drives are portable storage devices with USB,USB-C or Thunderbolt connections.

They contain standard 2.5 inch or 3.5 inch drives inside protective enclosures with interface electronics.

External HDDs offer massive capacity 2 to 8 terabytes typically at low cost,perfect for backups and media libraries.

External SSDs provide fast performance in compact durable packages ideal for working with large files on the go or expanding laptop storage.

Many external drives include backup software and password protection features.

When choosing external drives,consider several factors.

2.5 inch drives are bus powered.

They run directly from USB without external power adapters,making them more portable.

3.5 inch drives require wall power but offer higher capacities at lower cost.USB 3.0 or newer is essential for reasonable transfer speeds.

avoid USB two point zero for storage drives.

Some external SSDs use USB C with high speed interfaces,delivering near internal SSD performance.

For backups,reliability matters more than speed.

Choose reputable brands and consider warranty length.

Different removable storage fits different needs.

USB flash drives transferring small to medium files between computers,bootable installation media,temporary working storage.

SD cards,cameras,smartphones,drones,portable devices needing expansion storage.

External HDDs backup storage,archiving large media libraries,transporting huge amounts of data.

External SSDs Mobile workstations,editing video on location,expanding laptop storage with performance,transferring large files quickly.

Choose based on capacity needs,performance requirements,portability and budget.

That's removable storage.

Remember,USB flash drives are convenient portable storage ranging from gigabytes to terabytes.

Choose USB 3.0 or newer for good performance.

SD cards come in SD,SDHC and SDXC capacities with speed classes indicating minimum write speeds.

Match speed to your device requirements.

Micro SD is the tiny format used in phones and cameras,often including full size adapters.

External HDDs offer massive capacity for backups and archiving.

External SSDs provide fast portable performance.

Each type serves different needs.

Choose based on your specific use case.

Next,we'll finish this section by looking at optical drives including C D,D V D and Blu-ray.

See you there.

143. 光驱

大家好，让我们通过讨论光驱来结束存储章节，包括CD、DVD和蓝光。

这些驱动器使用激光在光盘上读取，有时也能写入数据。

在二十世纪九十年代和二十一世纪初，光学介质在软件分发、音乐、电影和数据备份方面占据主导地位。

如今，随着下载和流媒体的兴起，光驱变得越来越罕见。

但了解它们对于支持旧系统和处理归档媒体仍然很重要。

让我们来探索不同的类型。

光盘通过将数据以微小的凹坑和平面存储在反射层上来保存数据。

驱动器中的激光照射在旋转的光盘上，并检测反射模式。

凹坑和平面代表二进制数据。

写入数据涉及使用更强大的激光来创建或改变这些模式，要么是在可记录光盘中烧录染料层，要么是在可重写光盘中改变晶体状态。

所需的精度令人惊叹。

凹坑的长度不到一微米，而激光必须在光盘以数百转每分钟的速度旋转时精确跟踪它们。

CD于二十世纪八十年代初推出用于音乐，后来被改编用于数据存储。

标准CD的容量约为七百兆字节，或可存储八十分钟的音频。

CD-ROM是只读介质，数据在工厂压制而成。

CD-R（可记录）可以使用CD刻录机写入一次。

CD-RW（可重写）可以擦除并重写数百次。

CD驱动器的读取速度以原始标准倍数的形式表示。

五十二倍速的CD驱动器读取速度为每秒一百五十千字节的五十二倍。

DVD于二十世纪九十年代中期问世，提供了比CD高得多的容量。

标准单层DVD的容量为四点七吉字节，大约是CD的七倍。

双层DVD通过拥有两个数据层并由激光重新聚焦读取，容量可达八点五吉字节。

DVD-ROM是只读的，通常用于电影和商业软件。

DVD-R和DVD+R是可记录格式。

两者工作方式相似，但使用略有不同的标准。

DVD-RW和DVD+RW是可重写的。

大多数驱动器同时支持加号和减号格式。

DVD驱动器的速度指定为每秒一点三五兆字节基本标准的倍数。

十六倍速的DVD驱动器读取速度约为每秒二十二兆字节。

大多数现代DVD驱动器都是组合驱动器。

它们可以读取和写入DVD，也可以读取和写入CD。

向后兼容性很重要。

由于技术相似，只是激光波长和聚焦不同，DVD驱动器可以完美地读取CD。

这种通用兼容性使得DVD驱动器成为替代CD驱动器的实用选择。

蓝光（Blu-ray）因其使用的蓝色激光波长而得名，于二十一世纪中期开发，用于高清视频和大数据存储。

标准单层蓝光光盘容量为二十五吉字节，双层光盘容量为五十吉字节，而BDXL扩展容量光盘可达一百或一百二十八吉字节。

容量的巨大提升源于使用了波长更短的蓝紫激光，它可以读写更小的凹坑，从而在相同的物理空间内打包更多的数据。

蓝光有多种格式。

BD-ROM是只读的，用于商业电影和游戏。

BD-R是可记录的，只能写入一次。

BD-RE是可重写的。

BDXL通过使用额外层将容量扩展到五十吉字节以上。

蓝光驱动器具有向后兼容性。

它们可以使用不同的激光模式读取和写入DVD及CD。

这意味着蓝光驱动器实际上是三合一的，能够处理所有三种光学格式。

然而，标准DVD驱动器无法读取蓝光光盘。

它们缺乏必要的蓝色激光。

蓝光驱动器的速度指定方式不同。

一倍速蓝光等于每秒四点五兆字节。

十二倍速的蓝光驱动器读取速度约为每秒五十四兆字节。

这比DVD快，但仍比现代固态硬盘甚至机械硬盘慢得多。

蓝光写入特别慢。

以四倍速刻录一张五十吉字节的光盘需要超过四十五分钟。

大容量和低速使得蓝光更适合归档存储，而非工作存储。

光驱在很大程度上已从现代计算机中消失。

笔记本电脑多年前就取消了光驱，以减轻重量和厚度。

许多台式机机箱不再包含用于光驱的五点二五英寸托架。

几个因素导致了这种衰退。

可下载软件取代了安装光盘，流媒体服务取代了实体介质收藏，USB驱动器和云存储取代了备份和传输用例，而外部光驱则满足了偶尔的需求。

大多数用户根本不再需要光驱。

对于偶尔需要光学介质的用户，外部USB光驱提供了解决方案。

这些便携式设备通过USB连接，适用于任何计算机，包括从未配备内部驱动器的笔记本电脑。

外部驱动器的价格通常为DVD型二十到五十美元，蓝光型五十到一百美元。

它们可用于安装旧软件、访问归档数据、翻录音乐收藏或刻录备份光盘。

如果您使用旧系统或拥有光学介质库，请备一个。

尽管使用率下降，光学介质在特定情况下仍然相关。

长期归档存储。

妥善保存的光盘可以持续数十年。

仅存在于光盘上的旧版软件。

访问云时代之前的旧备份和档案。

播放电影和音乐的实体介质收藏。

一些企业备份系统仍使用蓝光进行离线存储。

政府和医疗法规有时要求使用光学归档。

而且收藏实体介质在爱好者中仍然流行。

以上就是光驱。

请记住，CD容量为七百兆字节，DVD容量为四点七到八点五吉字节，蓝光光盘容量为二十五到一百二十八吉字节。

每种格式都有只读（ROM）版本、可记录（R）版本和可重写（RW或RE）版本。

较新的驱动器具有向后兼容性。

DVD驱动器可读取CD，蓝光驱动器可读取DVD和CD。

由于下载和流媒体的兴起，光驱已基本从现代系统中消失，但外部USB驱动器可在需要时提供访问。

光学介质对于归档存储和访问旧内容仍然有用。

至此，第十六节关于存储设备的内容全部结束。

我们涵盖了带有旋转盘片和various RPM速度的HDD、HDD外形规格、带有闪存和显著速度优势的SSD、包括SATA和NVMe在内的SSD接口、如M.2和二点五英寸等SSD外形规格、用于性能和冗余的RAID配置、包括USB驱动器和SD卡在内的可移动存储、以及用于旧介质的光驱。

您现在掌握了将在实际工作中遇到的所有存储技术的全面知识。

完成本章节的表现非常出色。

英文原文

Hey everyone,let's finish our storage section by discussing optical drives,CD,DVD and Blu-ray.

These drives read and sometimes write data on optical disks using lasers.

Optical media was dominant in the 1990s and 2000s for software distribution,music,movies and data backup.

Today,optical drives are increasingly rare as downloads and streaming have taken over.

But understanding them remains important for supporting legacy systems and working with archived media.

Let's explore the different types.

Optical disks store data as microscopic pits and LANs on a reflective layer.

A laser in the drive shines on the spinning disk and the reflection pattern is detected.

Pits and LANs represent binary data.

Writing data involves using a more powerful laser to create or alter these patterns,either by burning die layers in recordable disks or changing crystal states in rewritable disks.

The precision required is remarkable.

Pits are less than a micrometer long and the laser must track them accurately while the disk spins at hundreds of RPM.

CDs were introduced in the early 1980s for music and later adapted for data storage.

Standard CDs hold about 700 megabytes or 80 minutes of audio.

CD-ROM is read-only media with data pressed at the factory.

CD-R recordable can be written once using CD burners.

CDRW rewritable can be erased and rewritten hundreds of times.

CD drives read at various speeds expressed as multiples of the original standard.

A 52 dime CD drive reads at 52 times the base speed of 150 kilobytes per second.

DVDs arrived in the mid-1990s offering much higher capacity than CDs.

Standard single layer DVDs hold 4.7 gigabytes,about 7 times a CD.

Dual layer DVDs hold 8.5GB by having two data layers read by refocusing the laser.

DVD-ROM is read-only,typically used for movies and commercial software.

DVD-R and DVD-plus R are recordable formats.

Both work similarly but use slightly different standards.

DVD-RW and DVD plus RW are rewritable.

Most drives support both plus and minus formats.

DVD drive speeds are specified as multiples of the base 1.35 megabytes per second standard.

A 16x DVD drive reads at about 22 megabytes per second.

Most modern DVD drives are combo drives.

They can read and write DVDs and also read and write C Ds.

Backward compatibility is important.

D V D drives read C D's perfectly fine since the technology is similar,just with different laser wave-lengths and focussing.

This universal compatibility made DVD drives practical for replacing CD drives.

Blu-ray,named for the blue laser wavelength it uses,was developed in the mid-2000s for high-definition video and large data storage.

Standard single-layer Blu-ray discs hold 25GB,dual-layer discs hold 50 gigabytes,and BDXL extended capacity discs reach 100 or 128 gigabytes.

The dramatic capacity increase comes from using a shorter wavelength blue-violet laser that can read and write much smaller pits,packing far more data in the same physical space.

Blu-ray has several formats.

BD-ROM is read-only,used for commercial movies and games.

BDR is recordable,write once.

BDRE is rewritable.

BDXL extends capacity beyond 50 gigabytes using additional layers.

Blu-ray drives are backward compatible.

They can read and write DVDs and CDs using different laser modes.

This means a Blu-ray drive is actually three drives in one,handling all three optical formats.

However,standard DVD drives cannot read Blu-ray discs.

They lack the necessary blue laser.

Blu-ray drive speeds are specified differently.

1x Blu-ray equals 4.5 megabytes per second.

A 12x Blu-ray drive reads at about 54 megabytes per second.

This is faster than DVDs but still much slower than modern SSDs or even HDDs.

Blu-ray writing is particularly slow.

Burning a 50GB disc at 4x speed takes over 45 minutes.

The high capacity and slow speed makes Blu-ray more suitable for archival storage rather than working storage.

Optical drives have largely disappeared from modern computers.

Laptops dropped optical drives years ago to reduce weight and thickness.

Many desktop cases no longer include 5.25 inch base for optical drives.

Several factors drove this decline.

Downloadable software replaced insulation disks,streaming services replaced physical media collections,USB drives and cloud storage replaced backup and transfer use cases,and external optical drives became available for occasional needs.

Most users simply don't need optical drives anymore.

For users who occasionally need optical media,external USB optical drives provide a solution.

These portable units connect via USB and work with any computer including laptops that never had internal drives.

External drives typically cost twenty to fifty dollars for D V D and fifty to one hundred dollars for Blu-ray.

They're useful for installing old software,accessing archived data,ripping music collections or burning backup disks.

Keep one available if you work with legacy systems or have an optical media library.

Despite declining use,optical media remains relevant in specific situations.

Long-term archival storage.

Properly stored optical discs can last decades.

Legacy software that only exists on disk.

Accessing old backups and archives from the pre-cloud era.

Playing physical media collections of movies and music.

Some enterprise backup systems still use Blu-ray for offline storage.

Government and healthcare regulations sometimes require optical archiving.

And collecting physical media remains popular for enthusiasts.

That's optical drives.

Remember,CDs hold 700 megabytes,DVDs hold 4.7 to 8.5 gigabytes,and Blu-ray discs hold 25 to 128GB.

Each format has read-only ROM versions,recordable R versions,and rewritable RW or RE versions.

Newer drives are backward compatible.

DVD drives read C D's,Blu-ray drives read DVDs and C Ds.

Optical drives have mostly disappeared from modern systems due to downloads and streaming,but external USB drives provide access when needed.

Optical media remains useful for archival storage and accessing legacy content.

And that completes section 16 on storage devices.

We've covered HTDs with their spinning platters and various RPM speeds,HTD form factors,SSDs with their flash memory and dramatic speed advantages,SSD interfaces including SATA and NVMe,SSD form factors like M.2 and 2.5 inch,RAID configurations for performance and redundancy,

removable storage including USB drives and SD cards,and optical drives for legacy media.

You now have comprehensive knowledge of all the storage technologies you'll encounter in the field.

Excellent work finishing this section.

144. 主板外形规格

大家好，欢迎进入这个新章节，我们将深入探讨主板、CPU和扩展卡，这些是让计算机运转的核心组件。

今天我们从主板板型开始讲起。

基本上，就是主板所采用的不同尺寸。

可以把它想象成T恤的尺码：小、中、大，只不过这是针对电脑主板的。

了解这些尺寸有助于您为自己的装机选择合适的motherboard，无论您是在组装一台大型游戏主机还是一台小巧的客厅电脑。

让我们来探索这些尺寸。

主板板型基本上是标准化的尺寸，并规定了组件安装位置的特定规则。

这就像乐高积木都能拼合在一起一样。

不管是哪家公司制造的，它们都能协同工作。

这种标准化意味着，当您购买一个ATX机箱时，任何ATX主板都能完美适配，所有螺丝孔都能整齐对齐。

您选择的尺寸决定了您可以添加多少张扩展卡、组件有多少散热空间，以及最终您的电脑在桌面上占据多大空间。

ATX，即高级技术扩展型，是主板尺寸中的“老大哥”，尺寸为十二英寸乘以九点六英寸。

自英特尔在一九九五年推出以来，它一直是首选尺寸，并且至今仍是其中最受欢迎的选择。

ATX主板空间宽敞，通常提供七个扩展插槽，供您安装显卡、声卡以及任何其他您想添加的设备。

它们通常拥有四条内存插槽、充足的M.2插槽用于高速存储，以及大量的USB端口和连接器。

如果您正在组装一台高性能台式机，ATX是您的得力助手。

ATX主板的设计非常巧妙。

CPU插座的位置远离扩展插槽，因此您的大型CPU散热器不会阻挡其他设备。

所有端口都按照标准布局整齐地排列在背板上。

您拥有一个大型二十四针电源连接器和一个专为CPU设计的八针连接器。

额外的空间意味着制造商可以添加更好的供电设计、更多的风扇连接器用于散热，甚至炫酷的RGB灯光控制。

这就像拥有一套宽敞的公寓，而不是拥挤的单身工作室。

每样东西都有其位置。

当您希望有成长空间时，请选择ATX。

也许您以后会添加第二张显卡、更多存储空间或用于直播的采集卡。

它非常适合游戏电脑、视频编辑工作站以及任何需要灵活性的装机方案。

您需要一个中塔或全塔机箱，也就是那些随处可见的标准台式机箱。

当然，机箱成本会稍高一些，占用的桌面空间也更多，但您获得的灵活性通常物超所值。

大多数商店购买的台式机都使用ATX，因为这合乎逻辑。

Micro ATX就像是ATX的小弟。

它的尺寸是九点六英寸见方，所以比ATX短，但宽度相同。

可以把它想象成被截短的ATX主板。

您只有四个扩展插槽，而不是七个，有时只有三条或四条内存插槽，而不是四条。

最棒的是什么？

Micro ATX使用与ATX相同的螺丝孔，所以如果您愿意，实际上可以将Micro ATX主板装入ATX机箱中。

螺丝孔是匹配的。

您只是没有用完所有的孔位而已。

它是向后兼容的，这非常方便。

Micro ATX牺牲了一些扩展插槽，但保留了ATX的大部分优点。

您仍然拥有多个PCIe插槽，空间足以容纳一张显卡，或许还能加上一张声卡或采集卡。

您拥有的内存插槽数量对大多数人来说已经足够。

十六到六十四GB对于游戏和工作来说绰绰有余。

您拥有用于高速固态硬盘的M.2插槽、所需的所有USB端口，以及与ATX相同的电源连接器。

较小的尺寸意味着组件之间距离更近，这可能会使理线变得更具挑战性，散热效果也略逊一筹，但现代Micro ATX主板处理得很好。

当您想节省一些资金和桌面空间，但仍需要不错的扩展能力时，Micro ATX是完美的选择。

它非常适合预算型游戏装机、不需要七个扩展插槽的办公电脑、需要放入娱乐中心的家庭影院电脑，以及任何您觉得ATX大材小用但Mini ITX又限制太多的装机方案。

它是那个完美的中间地带。

您节省了机箱成本，节省了桌面空间，但仍然有空间安装优质显卡和一些额外设备。

许多预算和中端系统都通过Micro ATX实现了这种平衡。

Mini ITX则真正进入了紧凑领域，仅为六点七英寸见方，不到ATX尺寸的一半。

这些微型主板是工程学的奇迹。

您通常只有一个PCIe插槽（通常预留给显卡）和两条内存插槽，但制造商不知何故将所有其他功能都塞了进去：用于存储的M.2插槽、USB-C端口、内置Wi-Fi和蓝牙、高品质音频以及可靠的供电设计。

这就像把一套单身公寓塞进一个步入式衣橱里。

每样东西都必须完美放置，但它确实行得通。

使用Mini ITX装机比较大尺寸的主板更具挑战性。

每一毫米都至关重要，因此组件布局非常关键。

散热具有挑战性，因为空气流动的空间较小。

您可能需要更小的CPU散热器或更多的机箱风扇。

理线变成了一道谜题。

有时您需要更短的定制线缆才能装下所有东西。

由于只有两个插槽，您的总内存限制为三十二或六十四GB，而那唯一的PCIe插槽意味着一旦您添加了显卡，就没有余地了。

没有空间安装其他任何东西。

Mini ITX回报的是周密的规划。

当尺寸真正重要时，Mini ITX大放异彩。

想要一台可以携带参加局域网派对的游戏电脑吗？

选Mini ITX。

需要一台看起来不像电脑的客厅电脑吗？

选Mini ITX。

为狭窄的办公桌组装小型办公系统吗？

选Mini ITX。

设置一台藏在壁橱里的家庭服务器吗？

选Mini ITX。

发烧友爱好者喜欢挑战在微型机箱中容纳高端组件。

有些Mini ITX机箱比鞋盒还小。

如果您能接受只使用一张扩展卡和两根内存条，您就可以在极小的封装中构建出令人惊讶的强大系统。

让我们将它们并排比较一下。

ATX：十二乘九点六英寸，七个插槽，四条或更多内存插槽，您的“我要一切”选项。

Micro ATX：九点六英寸见方，四个插槽，通常四条内存插槽，您的“平衡且实用”选项。

Mini ITX：六点七英寸见方，一个插槽，两条内存插槽，您的“紧凑为王”选项。

它们都使用相同的电源连接器，所以这不是问题。

有趣的是，更小并不总是意味着更便宜。

Mini ITX主板的成本可能与ATX一样高甚至更高，因为将所有东西塞进去实际上是更难的工程设计。

请根据您需要安装多少设备以及您有多少空间来选择。

以上就是主板板型。

请记住，ATX是您十二乘九点六英寸、拥有七个插槽的全尺寸主力军。

当您想要所有选项时，它是完美的选择。

Micro ATX是您九点六英寸见方、拥有四个插槽的中间选择。

当您想节省空间和资金但仍保持灵活性时，它是理想之选。

Mini ITX是您六点七英寸见方、拥有一个插槽的紧凑冠军。

当尺寸是您的首要任务时，它令人惊叹。

它们都与标准电源和安装方式完美兼容。

根据您需要安装的内容以及桌面上有多少空间来选择。

接下来，我们将讨论BIOS和UEFI，这是唤醒计算机的秘密启动软件。
