英文原文

Hey everyone,welcome to this new section where we are diving into motherboards,CPUs and expansion cards,the core components that make computers work.

Today we are starting with motherboard form factors.

Basically,the different sizes motherboards come in.

Think of it like t-shirt sizes,small,medium,and large,except for computer motherboards.

Understanding these sizes helps you pick the right motherboard for your build,whether you're making a massive gaming rig or a tiny living room PC.

Let's explore these sizes.

Motherboard form factors are basically standardized sizes with specific rules about where things go.

It's like how Lego bricks all fit together.

Doesn't matter which company made them,they just work.

This standardization means that when you buy an ATX case,any ATX motherboard will fit perfectly with all the screw holes lining up nicely.

The size you pick determines how many expansion cards you can add,how much breathing room your components get for cooling and ultimately how big your computer will be sitting on your desk.

ATX,which stands for Advanced Technology Extended,is the big daddy of motherboard sizes at 12 inches by 9.6 inches.

It's been the go-to size since Intel introduced it back in 1995 and it's still the most popular choice today.

ATX boards are spacious,typically giving you 7 expansion slots for all your graphics cards,sound cards and whatever else you want to add.

They usually have 4 RAM slots,plenty of M.2 slots for fast storage and tons of USB ports and connectors.

If you're building a serious desktop,ATX is your friend.

ATX boards are designed smartly.

The CPU socket is positioned away from the expansion slots so your big CPU cooler doesn't block everything else.

All your ports are neatly arranged on the back panel in a standard layout.

You've got a big 24 pin power connector and an 8 pin connector just for the CPU.

The extra space means manufacturers can add better power delivery,more fan connectors for cooling and even fancy RGB lighting controls.

It's like having a roomy apartment instead of a cramped studio.

Everything has its place.

Go with ATX when you want room to grow.

Maybe you'll add a second graphics card later or more storage or a capture card for streaming.

It's perfect for gaming PCs,video editing workstations and any build where you want flexibility.

You'll need a mid-tower or full tower case which are those standard desktop towers you see everywhere.

Sure,the case costs a bit more and takes up more desk space but you get so much more flexibility that it's usually worth it.

Most storeboard desktops use ATX because it just makes sense.

Micro ATX is like ATX's little sibling.

It's 9.6 inches square,so it's shorter but just as wide.

Think of it as a chopped down ATX board.

Instead of seven expansion slots,you get four and sometimes you get three or four RAM slots instead of four.

The cool thing?

Micro ATX uses the same screw holes as ATX,so you can actually put a micro ATX board in an ATX case if you want.

The screw holes match up.

You just don't use all of them.

It's backward compatible,which is pretty handy.

Micro ATX gives up some expansion slots but keeps most of the good stuff from ATX.

You still get multiple PCIe slots,room for a graphics card plus maybe a sound card or capture card.

You've got enough RAM slots for most people.

16 to 64GB is plenty for gaming and work.

You get M.2 slots for fast SSDs,all the USB ports you need and the same power connectors as ATX.

The smaller size means things are a bit closer together which can make cable management trickier and cooling slightly less optimal but modern micro ATX boards handle it just fine.

Micro ATX is perfect when you want to save some money and desk space but still need decent expansion.

It's great for budget gaming builds,office computers that don't need 7 expansion slots,home theater PCs that need to fit in your entertainment center and basically any build where you're thinking ATX is overkill but mini ITX is too limiting.

It's that sweet middle ground.

You save on case costs,you save desk space but you still have room for a good graphics card and some extras.

A lot of budget and mid-range systems nail this balance with micro ATX.

Mini ITX is where things get really compact,just 6.7 inches square which is less than half the size of ATX.

These tiny boards are engineering marvels.

You only get one PCIe slot usually saved for your graphics card and two RAM slots but manufacturers somehow pack in everything else M.2 slots for storage,USB-C ports,built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth,quality audio and solid power delivery.

It's like fitting a studio apartment into a walk-in closet.

Everything has to be perfectly placed but it works.

Building with mini ITX is trickier than larger sizes.

Every millimeter counts so component placement is critical.

Cooling is challenging because there's less space for air to flow.

You might need a smaller CPU cooler or more case fans.

Cable management becomes a puzzle.

Sometimes you need shorter custom cables to fit everything.

You're limited to 32 or 64 gigabytes of RAM total with just two slots and that single PCIe slot means once you add a graphics card you're done.

No room for anything else.

Mini ITX rewards careful planning.

Mini ITX shines when size really matters.

Want a gaming PC you can carry to LAN parties?

Mini ITX.

Need a living room PC that doesn't look like a computer?

Mini ITX.

Building a small office system for a cramped desk?

Mini ITX.

Setting up a home server you're hiding in a closet?

Mini ITX.

Enthusiast builders love the challenge of fitting high-end components in tiny cases.

Some mini ITX cases are smaller than shoeboxes.

If you can live with one expansion card and two RAM sticks,you can build surprisingly powerful systems in incredibly small packages.

Let's put them side by side.

ATX 12 by 9.6 inches 7 slots 4 or more RAM slots your Give Me Everything option.

Micro ATX 9.6 inches square 4 slots usually 4 RAM slots your balanced and practical option.

Mini ITX 6.7 inches square 1 slot 2 RAM slots your compact is king option.

They all use the same power connectors so that's not an issue.

Interestingly smaller doesn't always mean cheaper.

Mini ITX boards can cost as much or more than ATX because cramming everything in is actually harder engineering.

Pick based on how much stuff you need to install and how much space you have.

That's motherboard form factors.

Remember,ATX is your full size workhorse at 12 by 9.6 inches with 7 slots.

Perfect when you want all the options.

Micro ATX is your middle ground at 9.6 inches square with 4 slots.

Ideal when you want to save space and money but still have flexibility.

Mini ITX is your compact champion at 6.7 inches square with 1 slot.

Amazing when size is your top priority.

They all play nice with standard power supplies and mounting.

Choose based on what you need to install and how much room you have on your desk.

Next up we'll talk about BIOS and UEFI,the secret startup software that wakes up your computer.

See you there.

145. BIOS 与 UEFI 概述

大家好，让我们来谈谈计算机中那位无名英雄，也就是当您按下电源按钮时唤醒一切设备的固件。

在Windows、Linux或Mac OS甚至开始考虑加载之前，有一款特殊软件会检查您所有的硬件并做好准备。

那就是BIOS，即基本输入输出系统，这是老派的方式；或者是UEFI，即可统一可扩展固件接口，这是现代的方式。

您在现实中会同时见到两者，所以让我们拆解一下它们的作用，以及为什么UEFI正在占据主导地位。

BIOS本质上是存储在主板芯片上的计算机晨间例行程序。

当您按下电源按钮时，CPU的第一项任务就是运行BIOS代码。

可以把它想象成计算机的闹钟。

BIOS会执行一项名为POST（加电自检）的快速健康检查，确保您的CPU、内存和键盘都在位且工作正常。

然后它唤醒您的硬盘，检查您的显卡，基本上就是在说“好的，所有东西都在这儿了”。

最后，它寻找您的操作系统并移交控制权。

就在这时，您看到了Windows标志。

您知道启动时按下Delete或F2键会出现的那个屏幕吗？

那就是BIOS设置实用程序，相当于计算机的后台控制面板。

它通常是蓝色或黑色的屏幕，菜单看起来直接出自二十世纪九十年代，因为它们基本上就是那个时代的产物。

在这里，您可以更改启动顺序、启用或禁用USB端口、调整风扇转速、设置密码以及微调各种硬件设置。

这功能很强大，但外观看起来很古老，因为BIOS是一项老旧技术，几十年来在视觉上没有太大变化。

BIOS自二十世纪八十年代就存在了，老实说，它已显老态。

它只能处理容量高达二点二太字节的驱动器，任何更大的容量都会让BIOS感到困惑。

与现代标准相比，它的启动速度非常慢。

其界面仅支持键盘，不支持鼠标，看起来就像来自复古计算机博物馆的东西。

BIOS运行在十六位模式下，按今天的标准来说这非常古老，而且它没有内置安全功能，使其容易受到某些类型的攻击。

正是这些局限性促使了UEFI的开发。

UEFI，即可统一可扩展固件接口，是BIOS的现代替代品，这就好比将智能手机与翻盖手机进行比较。

UEFI始于二十世纪九十年代末的开发，并已成为二零一零年左右制造的计算机的标准配置。

它能做BIOS能做的一切，但做得更好、更快，并且拥有更多的功能。

最重要的是，它是为具有现代需求的现代计算机而设计的，包括大容量硬盘、快速启动时间、安全功能和网络能力。

如果您的计算机机龄不到十年，它很可能具备UEFI。

关于UEFI，您注意到的第一件事就是它看起来确实很现代。

UEFI设置通常拥有图形界面、支持鼠标、图标，有时甚至还有动画，而不是那种带有文本菜单的蓝色屏幕。

不同的主板制造商使他们的UEFI看起来各不相同。

微星的界面看起来不同于华硕，而华硕又不同于技嘉，但它们都支持鼠标控制，并且看起来比旧的BIOS好得多。

一些UEFI界面甚至拥有主题和配色方案。

使用起来实际上很愉快。

UEFI在启动计算机方面比BIOS快得多。

BIOS可能只需要三十到六十秒就能到达加载Windows的阶段，而UEFI可以在五到十秒内完成。

这是因为UEFI能更高效地初始化硬件，并且可以同时检查多个设备，而不像BIOS那样一次只能检查一个。

结合快速启动功能和现代固态硬盘，您可以在十五秒或更短的时间内从按下电源按钮到使用计算机。

如果您还记得过去等待几分钟才能启动计算机的日子，这简直是一场革命。

还记得BIOS最大只支持二点二太字节吗？

UEFI对那个限制嗤之以鼻。

UEFI使用GPT（GUID分区表）代替旧的MBR系统，这意味着它可以处理高达九点四泽字节的驱动器，没错，是泽字节。

为了让您有个概念，您需要超过四百万块二太字节的硬盘才能达到那个极限。

基本上，UEFI支持您在现实生活中会遇到的任何驱动器容量。

这一点至关重要，因为现在四十八太字节甚至十八太字节的驱动器已经很常见了。

UEFI包含BIOS从未有过的内置安全功能。

其中最重要的是安全启动。

它在加载操作系统之前验证该操作系统是否未被篡改。

安全启动检查数字签名，以确保您加载的是合法的Windows或Linux，而不是伪装成Windows的恶意软件。

这可以防止引导套件和根套件恶意软件，它们试图在操作系统加载之前感染您的计算机。

这就像门口有个保安在检查身份证，然后才让任何人进入。

这是BIOS永远无法做到的事情。

UEFI可以连接网络。

UEFI包含网络驱动程序，在某些实现中甚至可以浏览网页。

这使得诸如远程管理之类的酷炫功能成为可能，IT部门可以在操作系统加载之前通过网络配置或排查计算机故障。

您还可以从网络位置启动、直接下载固件更新并执行远程诊断。

对于管理数百台计算机的企业来说，这具有极高的价值。

无需亲自前往每台机器。

现在您可能会想，那些期望使用BIOS的旧版操作系统和软件怎么办？

UEFI已经考虑到了这一点。

大多数UEFI实现都包含CSM，即兼容性支持模块，这基本上是BIOS仿真模式。

启用后，UEFI会假装成老派的BIOS，因此旧版操作系统可以正常工作。

您会在UEFI设置中看到此选项，标记为传统启动或CSM。

像Windows 10、Windows 11和最近的Linux发行版这样的现代操作系统在UEFI原生模式下效果最佳，但如果需要用于旧系统，也有传统选项可用。让我们直接比较一下它们。

BIOS：源自二十世纪八十年代的古老十六位技术；仅有文本界面且由键盘控制；二点二太字节驱动器限制；启动较慢；无安全功能；但兼容一切。

UEFI：现代的三十二位或六十四位技术。

支持鼠标的图形界面。

可处理海量驱动器，启动速度快得多，内置安全功能如安全启动，具备网络能力，并且在需要时包含BIOS兼容模式。

UEFI在各方面都客观上更优越，这就是为什么所有新计算机都使用它的原因。

如果您使用的是二零一二年左右之后制造的计算机，您几乎肯定是在处理UEFI。

以上就是BIOS和UEFI。

请记住，BIOS是老派固件。

文本界面，速度慢，限制为二点二太字节，但可靠且兼容性广泛。

UEFI是现代替代品。

图形界面，速度快，可处理巨大驱动器，包含安全功能，甚至支持网络。

大多数现代计算机使用UEFI，但如果需要，也可以运行在传统BIOS模式下。

当您访问设置时，请记住要按的键，通常是Delete、F2或F10，具体因制造商而异。

固件在您的操作系统之前运行并设置所有硬件，使其对于故障排查和配置至关重要。

接下来，我们将深入探讨BIOS和UEFI启动选项以及如何配置启动顺序。

届时见。

英文原文

Hey everyone,let's talk about the unsung hero of your computer,the firmware that wakes everything up when you hit that power button.

Before Windows or Linux or Mac OS even thinks about loading,there's special software that checks all your hardware and gets things ready.

That's BIOS,basic input and output system,the old school way or UEFI,Unified Extensible Firmware Interface,the modern way.

You'll see both in the wild,so let's break down what they do and why UEFI is taking over.

BIOS is basically your computer's morning routine stored on a chip on the motherboard.

When you press the power button,the CPU's first job is running BIOS code.

Think of it as the computer's alarm clock.

BIOS does a quick health check called POST,Power On Self-Test,making sure your CPU,RAM and keyboard are all there and working.

Then it wakes up your hard drives,checks your graphics card and basically says okay everything's here.

Finally it looks for your operating system and hands things off.

That's when you see the Windows logo.

You know that screen you get when you press delete or F2 during startup?

That's the BIOS setup utility,your computer's backstage control panel.

It's usually a blue or black screen with menus that look straight out of the 1990s because they basically are.

Here you can change boot order,enable or disable USB ports,adjust fan speeds,set passwords and tweak all sorts of hardware settings.

It's powerful stuff but it looks ancient because BIOS is old technology that hasn't changed much visually in decades.

BIOS has been around since the 1980s and honestly it's showing its age.

It can only work with drives up to 2.2 terabytes,anything bigger and BIOS gets confused.

It's super slow at startup compared to modern standards.

The interface is keyboard only,no mouse support and looks like something from a retro computer museum.

BIOS runs in 16-bit mode which is ancient by today's standards and it has no built-in security features making it vulnerable to certain types of attacks.

These limitations are why UEFI was developed.

UEFI Unified Extensible Firmware Interface is the modern replacement for BIOS and it's like comparing a smartphone to a flip form.

UEFI was developed starting in the late 1990s and has become standard on computers made since around 2010.

It does everything BIOS does but better,faster and with way more features.

Most importantly,it's designed for modern computers with modern needs,big hard drives,fast boot times,security features and network capabilities.

If your computer is less than 10 years old,it probably has UEFI.

One of the first things you'll notice about UEFI is it actually looks modern.

Instead of blue screens with text menus,UEFI setups often have graphical interfaces with mouse support,icons,and sometimes even animations.

Different motherboard manufacturers make their UEFI look different.

MSIs look different from ASUSs,which looks different from gigabytes,but they all support mouse control and look way better than old BIOS.

Some UEFI interfaces even have themes and color schemes.

It's actually pleasant to use.

UEFI is significantly faster than BIOS at starting up your computer.

Where BIOS might take 30 to 60 seconds just to get to the point of loading Windows,UEFI can do it in 5 to 10 seconds.

This is because UEFI initializes hardware more efficiently and can check multiple devices simultaneously instead of one at a time like BIOS.

Combined with fast boot features and modern SSDs,you can go from pressing the power button to using your computer in 15 seconds or less.

That's a game changer if you remember the old days of waiting minutes for your computer to start.

Remember how BIOS maxes out at 2.2 terabytes?

UEFI laughs at that limitation.

UEFI uses GPT,GUID partition table,instead of the old MBR system,which means it can handle drives up to 9.4 zettabytes,that's zettabytes with a Z.

To put that in perspective,you'd need over 4 million 2TB hard drives to hit that limit.

Basically,UEFI supports any drive size you'll ever encounter in real life.

This is crucial since 48 and even 18TB drives are common now.

UEFI includes built-in security features that BIOS never had.

The big one is Secure Boot.

It verifies that the operating system hasn't been tampered with before loading it.

Secure Boot checks digital signatures to make sure you're loading legitimate Windows or Linux,not some malware pretending to be Windows.

This protects against boot kit and rootkit malware that try to infect your computer before the operating system even loads.

It's like having a security guard at the door checking IDs before anyone gets in.

Here's something BIOS could never do.

UEFI can connect to networks.

UEFI includes network drivers and can even browse the web in some implementations.

This enables cool features like remote management where IT departments can configure or troubleshoot computers over the network before the operating system loads.

You can also boot from network locations,download firmware updates directly and perform remote diagnostics.

For businesses managing hundreds of computers,this is incredibly valuable.

no need to physically go to each machine.

Now you might wonder,what about older operating systems and software that expect BIOS?

UEFI thought of that.

Most UEFI implementations include CSM,Compatibility Support Module,which is basically BIOS emulation mode.

When enabled,UEFI pretends to be old school BIOS,so older operating systems work fine.

You'll see this as legacy boot or CSM in the UEFI settings.

Modern operating systems like Windows 10,Windows 11 and recent Linux distributions work best with UEFI native mode,but the legacy option is there if you need it for older systems.Let's compare them directly.

BIOS Ancient 16-bit technology from the 1980s Text-only interface with keyboard control,2.2TB drive limit,slower startup,no security features,but works with everything.

UEFI Modern 32-bit or 64-bit technology.

Graphical interface with mouse support.

Handles massive drives,much faster startup,built-in security like secure boot,network capabilities and includes BIOS compatibility mode when needed.

UEFI is objectively better in every way,which is why all new computers use it.

If you're working on a computer made after 2012 or so,you're almost certainly dealing with UEFI.

That's BIOS and UEFI.

Remember,BIOS is the old school firmware.

Text interface,slow,limited to 2.2TB,but reliable and widely compatible.

UEFI is the modern replacement.

Graphical interface,fast,handles huge drives,includes security features and even supports networking.

Most modern computers use UEFI but can run in legacy BIOS mode if needed.

When you are accessing setup,remember the key to press,usually delete F2 or F10,varies by manufacturer.

The firmware runs before your operating system and sets up all your hardware,making it crucial for troubleshooting and configuration.

Next,we'll dive into BIOS and UEFI boot options and how to configure your startup sequence.

See you there.

146. BIOS UEFI 启动选项

大家好！

既然我们已经了解了BIOS和UEFI是什么，现在让我们谈谈它们控制的最重要内容之一：启动过程。

启动选项决定了计算机如何启动、从哪个驱动器启动以及使用何种模式。

了解启动顺序、启动模式和快速启动设置，有助于您排查启动问题、安装操作系统并优化计算机性能。

让我们深入探讨这些启动选项。

让我们从基础开始。

启动究竟意味着什么？

当您打开计算机时，启动是将操作系统从存储设备加载到内存中的过程，这样您才能真正使用计算机。

该术语源自“自举”（bootstrapping），就像拽着自己的鞋带把自己提起来一样。

您的计算机基本上是通过一系列步骤，将自己从完全关闭状态提升到fully运行状态。

固件（BIOS或UEFI）管理此过程的第一部分，即找到操作系统并将控制权移交给它。

启动顺序本质上是计算机寻找操作系统的优先级列表。

想象一下您在找钥匙。

您先检查口袋，然后是桌子，接着是外套。

计算机也是如此行事。

它检查启动顺序中的第一个设备，如果在那里找到了操作系统，很好，就从该设备启动。

如果没有，它就移动到第二个设备，然后是第三个，依此类推。

启动顺序中常见的设备包括您的主硬盘或固态硬盘、USB驱动器、光驱和网络启动选项。

启动顺序至关重要，原因有几点。

通常情况下，您希望计算机从安装了Windows或Linux的主驱动器启动。

该驱动器应排在顺序的第一位。

但是，如果您要从U盘安装新操作系统怎么办？

您需要暂时将USB移到顶部，这样计算机就会从安装程序启动，而不是从现有的操作系统启动。

或者也许您正在从光盘运行诊断程序。

这时您需要将光驱放在第一位。弄错启动顺序意味着您的计算机可能无法正常启动，或者在需要时找不到您的USB安装程序。

若要更改启动顺序，您需进入BIOS或UEFI设置，通常在启动期间按下Delete、F2、F10或F12键，具体取决于您的主板制造商。

查找名为启动、启动顺序、启动优先级或类似名称的部分。

您将看到一个设备列表，可以使用键盘命令重新排列它们，通常是加号和减号键，或者是F5和F6键。

在UEFI中，您或许可以用鼠标拖放。

某些系统还允许您在启动期间按下F12键，调出一次性启动菜单，而无需更改永久顺序。

这对于USB安装来说超级方便。

以下是日常使用的典型启动顺序。

第一，是装有您操作系统的主固态硬盘或硬盘。

第二，如果您有备用硬盘，可能是它。

第三是USB驱动器，第四是光驱，最后是网络启动。

此顺序意味着您的计算机通常从主驱动器启动，但如果您插入可启动的U盘，它也会检查该设备。

对于故障排查或安装操作系统，您可以暂时将USB移到第一位。

有些人会完全禁用未使用的启动选项，例如如果您没有光驱就禁用它，以稍微加快启动过程。

有趣的地方来了。

UEFI系统可以两种不同的模式启动：UEFI模式或传统BIOS模式。

UEFI模式是现代方式。

它使用GPT分区，支持安全启动，并且启动更快。

传统模式模拟旧版BIOS行为。

它使用MBR分区，并兼容旧版操作系统。为了获得最佳效果，Windows 10和Windows 11应使用UEFI模式。

像Windows 7这样的旧版操作系统可能需要传统模式。

混合模式会导致问题。如果您在UEFI模式下安装Windows，则必须在UEFI模式下启动，而不能在传统模式下。

您如何知道自己在用哪种模式？

在Windows中，按下Windows键加R，输入MSInfo32并按回车键。

这将打开系统信息。

在顶部附近查找BIOS模式。

它会显示UEFI或传统。

如果显示UEFI，那就太好了。

您正运行在现代模式下。

如果显示传统，说明您正在使用旧的BIOS兼容模式。

这在排查启动问题或计划安装新操作系统时很重要。

您需要使启动介质与启动模式相匹配。

切换启动模式并不像翻转开关那么简单。

它需要重新安装您的操作系统。

原因如下。

UEFI模式使用GPT分区，而传统模式使用MBR分区。

这是组织硬盘的两种根本不同的方式。

如果您在传统模式下安装Windows，然后切换到UEFI模式，您的计算机将找不到操作系统。

它在寻找GPT分区表，却发现了MBR。

若要切换模式，您需要备份数据，更改BIOS或UEFI设置，然后重新安装Windows。

这很麻烦，所以第一次就要做对。

快速启动是一项UEFI功能，通过跳过某些检查和初始化来加快启动速度。

快速启动不再仔细检查每个硬件部件，而是基于上一次成功启动进行假设。

这可以将启动时间从二十秒缩短到十秒或更短。

相当不错。

然而，快速启动可能会引发问题。

它可能会阻止您进入BIOS或UEFI设置，因为它跳过了您可以按下Delete或F2键的时间窗口。

它还可能导致检测新硬件或从USB驱动器启动时出现问题。

对于日常使用，快速启动很棒。

对于故障排查或安装操作系统，您需要暂时禁用它。

某些主板提供超快速启动或即时启动，这比普通快速启动更为激进。

这实际上会跳过几乎所有内容，包括制造商标志屏幕。

启动时间可以缩短到五秒或更短。

令人印象深刻。

但问题来了。

超快速启动通常使得进入BIOS或UEFI设置变得几乎不可能。

您可能必须使用Windows恢复选项来访问UEFI设置，或者使用主板上的专用按钮。

只有在百分之百确定所有配置都正确后，才启用超快速启动。

否则，您可能会把自己锁在外面。

让我们来谈谈故障排查。

如果您的计算机无法启动，首先检查启动顺序。

确保您的主驱动器排在第一位。第二，验证启动模式。

UEFI安装需要UEFI模式。

传统安装需要传统模式。

第三，暂时禁用快速启动。

它可能会引起奇怪的问题。

如果您无法访问BIOS或UEFI设置，请尝试不同的功能键：F2、Delete、F10、F12或Escape。

制造商使用不同的按键。

如果您正在安装操作系统且未检测到USB，请确保USB在启动顺序中排第一，并验证USB是否已正确创建。

这些简单的检查能解决大多数与启动相关的问题。以上就是BIOS和UEFI启动选项。

请记住，启动顺序决定了计算机首先检查哪个设备以寻找操作系统，通常是您的主固态硬盘或硬盘，但您可以暂时优先选择USB进行安装。

启动模式很重要。

UEFI模式是现代且更快的，采用GPT分区。

传统模式模拟旧版BIOS，采用MBR分区，如果不重新安装，两者不可互换。

快速启动加快了启动速度，但可能会干扰BIOS访问和USB启动。

故障排查时请禁用它。

在启动期间按下Delete、F2、F10或F12键访问启动选项，具体取决于您的制造商。

接下来，我们将讨论BIOS中的USB权限，以及您为何可能出于安全考虑要禁用USB端口。

届时见。

英文原文

Hey everyone!

Now that we know what BIOS and UEFI are,let's talk about one of the most important things they control,the boot process.

Boot options determine how your computer starts up,which drive it boots from,and what mode it uses.

Understanding boot order,boot modes and fast boot settings helps you troubleshoot startup problems,install operating systems and optimize your computer's performance.

Let's dive into these boot options.

Let's start with the basics.

What does booting even mean?

When you turn on your computer,booting is the process of loading the operating system from storage into memory so you can actually use the computer.

The term comes from bootstrapping,like pulling yourself up by your bootstraps.

Your computer is basically pulling itself from completely off to fully running through a series of steps.

The firmware,BIOS or UEFI,manages the first part of this process,finding the operating system and handing control over to it.

Boot order is basically your computer's priority list for where to look for an operating system.

Imagine you are looking for your keys.

You check your pocket first,then the table,then your jacket.

Your computer does the same thing.

It checks the first device in the boot order and if it finds an operating system there,great,it boots from that.

If not,it moves to the second device,then the third and so on.

Common devices in the boot order include your main hard drive or SSD,USB drives,optical drives and network boot options.

Boot order is crucial for several reasons.

Normally,you want your computer to boot from your main drive where Windows or Linux is installed.

That should be first in the order.

But what if you are installing a new operating system from a USB stick?

You need to temporarily move USB to the top so your computer boots from the installer instead of your existing OS.

Or maybe you are running diagnostics from a CD.

You'd need the optical drive first.Getting boot order wrong means your computer might not start properly or it might not find your USB installer when you need it.

To change boot order,you enter the BIOS or UEFI setup usually by pressing delete,F2,F10 or F12 during startup,depending on your motherboard manufacturer.

Look for a section called boot,boot order,boot priority or something similar.

You'll see a list of devices and you can rearrange them using keyboard commands,often the plus and minus keys or F5 and F6.

In UEFI,you might be able to drag and drop with your mouse.

Some systems also let you press F12 during startup for a one-time boot menu without changing the permanent order.

Super handy for USB installs.

Here's a typical boot order for everyday use.

First,your main SSD or hard drive with your operating system.

Second,maybe a secondary hard drive if you have one.

Third,USB drives,fourth optical drives,and last network boot.

This order means your computer boots normally from your main drive,but if you plug in a bootable USB stick,it'll check that too.

For troubleshooting or installing operating systems,you temporarily move USB to first place.

Some people disable unused boot options entirely,like optical drives if you don't have one,to speed up the boot process slightly.

Here's where things get interesting.

UEFI systems can boot in two different modes,UEFI mode or legacy BIOS mode.

UEFI mode is the modern way.

It uses GPT partitioning,support secure boot and boots faster.

Legacy mode emulates old BIOS behavior.

It uses MBR partitioning and works with older operating systems.Windows 10 and Windows 11 should use UEFI mode for best results.

Older operating systems like Windows 7 might need legacy mode.

Mixing modes can cause problems.If you install Windows in UEFI mode,you must boot in UEFI mode,not legacy.

How do you know which mode you are using?

In Windows,press Windows Key plus R,type MSInfo32 and press Enter.

This opens system information.

Look for BIOS mode near the top.

It'll say either UEFI or Legacy.

If it says UEFI,you're golden.

You're running in modern mode.

If it says legacy,you're using the old BIOS compatibility mode.

This matters when you're troubleshooting boot problems or planning to install a new operating system.

You need to match your boot media to your boot mode.

Switching boot modes isn't as simple as flipping a switch.

It requires reinstalling your operating system.

Here's why.

UEFI mode uses GPT partitioning while legacy mode uses MBR partitioning.

These are fundamentally different ways of organizing your hard drive.

If you install Windows in legacy mode and then switch to UEFI mode,your computer won't find the operating system.

It's looking for a GPT partition table but finds MBR instead.

To switch modes,you need to backup your data,change the BIOS slash UEFI setting and reinstall Windows.

It's a hassle,so get it right the first time.

FastBoot is a UEFI feature that speeds up startup by skipping certain checks and initializations.

Instead of carefully checking every piece of hardware,FastBoot makes assumptions based on the last successful boot.

This can cut boot time from 20 seconds to 10 seconds or less.

Pretty sweet.

However,FastBoot can cause issues.

It might prevent you from entering BIOS or UEFI setup because it skips the window where you can press Delete or F2.

It can also cause problems detecting new hardware or booting from USB drives.

For everyday use,fast boot is great.

For troubleshooting or installing operating systems,you'll want to disable it temporarily.

Some motherboards offer ultra fast boot or instant boot even more aggressive than regular fast boot.

This literally skips almost everything including the manufacturer logo screen.

Boot times can drop to 5 seconds or less.

Impressive.

But here's the catch.

Ultra fast boot often makes it nearly impossible to enter BIOS or UEFI setup.

You might have to use Windows Recovery options to access UEFI settings or use a special button on the motherboard.

Only enable ultra fast boot once you're 100%sure everything is configured correctly.

Otherwise,you might lock yourself out.

Let's talk troubleshooting.

If your computer won't boot,first check boot order.

Make sure your main drive is first.Second,verify boot mode.

UEFI installations need UEFI mode.

Legacy installations need legacy mode.

Third,disable fast boot temporarily.

It can cause weird issues.

If you can't access BIOS or UEFI setup,try different function keys F2,Delete,F10,F12 or escape.

Manufacturers use different keys.

If you are installing an operating system and the USB isn't detected,make sure USB is first in boot order and verify the USB was created correctly.

These simple checks solve most boot related problems.That's BIOS and UEFI boot options.

Remember,boot order determines which device your computer checks first for an operating system,typically your main SSD or hard drive,but you can temporarily prioritize USB for installations.

Boot mode matters.

UEFI mode is modern and faster with GPT partitioning.

Legacy mode emulates old BIOS with MBR partitioning and they're not interchangeable without reinstalling.

Fast boot speeds up startup but can interfere with BIOS access and USB booting.

Disable it when troubleshooting.

Access boot options by pressing delete,F2,F10 or F12 during startup,depending on your manufacturer.

Next we'll talk about USB permissions in BIOS and why you might want to disable USB ports for security.

See you there.

147. BIOS 中的 USB 权限

大家好，让我们来谈谈一个您可能从未想过的问题。

通过BIOS或UEFI设置控制USB端口。

您实际上可以启用或禁用USB端口，控制计算机是否可以从USB启动，并设置各种与USB相关的安全选项。

这听起来可能有些偏执，但在某些环境中，如企业办公室、学校或安全设施，控制USB访问是一个严肃的安全问题。

让我们探讨一下为什么要管理USB权限以及如何管理。

想想USB端口能做什么。

它们可以传输文件、启动计算机、为设备充电、连接键盘和鼠标，基本上能以无数种方式与您的系统交互。

从安全角度来看，USB端口是潜在的漏洞。

有人可能会插入加载了恶意软件的U盘。

他们可以将机密文件复制到闪存驱动器然后带走。

他们可以从USB驱动器启动以绕过Windows密码。

他们甚至可以使用USB设备进行硬件键盘记录。

在高安全环境中，控制USB访问并非偏执。

这是针对非常真实威胁的必要保护。

终极方案是通过BIOS或UEFI完全禁用USB端口。

当您禁用USB时，端口实际上会停止工作。

插入闪存驱动器，什么也不会发生，连指示灯都不亮。

这可以防止所有基于USB的攻击，但也带来了明显的问题：USB键盘和鼠标也无法工作。

此设置仅真正适用于信息亭系统或位于极度安全区域的计算机，那里的USB端口无论如何都已被物理封存。

大多数组织不会走到这一步，因为这对日常工作来说限制太大了。

一个更实用的选择是禁用USB存储设备，同时保持其他USB设备正常工作。

某些BIOS或UEFI实现允许您区分USB存储设备（如闪存驱动器和外部硬盘）与其他USB设备（如键盘、鼠标和打印机）。

这是许多组织的最佳平衡点。

员工仍然可以使用他们的USB键盘和鼠标，但无法插入USB驱动器来复制文件或引入恶意软件。

当然，聪明的用户可能会找到变通方法，但这提高了门槛并阻止了随意的滥用。

另一个重要的USB权限是计算机是否可以从USB设备启动。

还记得上一讲中的启动顺序吗？

您可以配置BIOS或UEFI以完全从启动选项中移除USB，或者要求输入密码才能从USB启动。

这可以防止有人启动Live Linux USB驱动器来访问您的文件、重置密码或绕过安全设置。

在企业环境中，您通常希望禁用此项或为其设置密码保护。

对于家庭用户和IT部门，保持USB启动启用会使系统恢复和安装变得容易得多。

一些高级的UEFI实现允许您控制单个USB端口或端口组。

例如，您可以禁用易于访问的前面板USB端口，同时保持后部端口启用。

或者您可以禁用USB 3.0端口，同时保持USB 2.0端口工作。

这种细粒度的控制在您希望保留部分USB功能但又想使其使用变得不那么方便的情况下非常有用。

这就像把饼干罐放在高架上，不是够不到，但不方便到足以让您三思而后行。

若要配置USB权限，请在启动期间进入BIOS或UEFI设置，通常通过按下Delete、F2或F10键。

查找标记为集成外设、高级、安全或USB配置的部分。

确切位置因制造商而异。

您将找到诸如USB控制器、传统USB支持、USB存储支持、外部USB端口和从USB启动等选项。

某些设置可能是简单的启用或禁用开关，而其他设置则提供更详细的控制。

现代UEFI界面使这些设置比旧的BIOS屏幕更容易查找和配置。

您将看到一个有趣的设置：传统USB支持。

这使得USB键盘和鼠标能在DOS、旧版操作系统中工作，并在主操作系统加载之前的启动过程中工作。

如果您禁用传统USB支持，您的USB键盘在BIOS或UEFI设置中以及Windows启动菜单中将无法工作。

很尴尬。

您将需要PS/2键盘来更改设置。

除非您出于特定安全原因需要禁用它，否则大多数人应该保持传统USB支持启用。

属于那种“没有理由就别动”的设置之一。

在企业环境中，USB限制通常是综合安全策略的一部分。

IT部门可能会在BIOS级别禁用USB存储，通过Windows组策略强制执行设备控制策略，使用Microsoft Intune等软件管理设备访问，要求批准的USB驱动器进行加密，并通过日志系统审计USB使用情况。

BIOS级别的控制是基础层，可捕捉绕过操作系统安全的尝试。

它并非万无一失。

坚定的攻击者可以重置BIOS设置，但它可以阻止随意的威胁和懒惰的用户。

对于家庭用户，考量则不同。

为了便利、安装操作系统、连接设备、传输文件和一般计算，您可能需要完整的USB功能。

只有当您与不完全信任的人共用计算机，或者正在设置信息亭或面向公众的系统时，禁用USB功能才有意义。

否则，不便之处超过了安全益处。

只要保持明智即可。

不要插入您捡到的随机U盘。

保持防病毒软件更新并践行良好的安全习惯。

对于家庭环境来说，这通常就足够了。

如果USB设备无法工作，BIOS设置可能是罪魁祸首。

检查BIOS或UEFI中是否启用了USB端口。

有人可能禁用了它们。

如果您的键盘在启动期间无法工作，请验证传统USB支持是否已启用。

如果闪存驱动器无法被识别，请确保未禁用USB存储。

有时，在BIOS更新或更换电池后，设置会重置为默认值。

如果您正在帮助某人排查神秘的USB问题，检查BIOS设置应列入您的清单。这是一件容易被忽视的事情，但可以完全解释为什么USB设备突然停止工作。

以上就是BIOS中的USB权限。

请记住，您可以出于安全目的通过BIOS或UEFI设置控制USB端口。

选项包括完全禁用USB（对大多数用户来说限制太大），或仅禁用USB存储而保持键盘和鼠标工作。

更好的平衡。

您可以防止从USB启动以阻止密码绕过攻击。

传统USB支持使USB键盘能在启动期间和BIOS设置中工作。

通常应该启用。

这些设置在企业和安全环境中比在家中更重要。

在BIOS或UEFI设置中的安全或USB配置等部分下访问这些选项。

接下来，我们将探讨TPM（可信平台模块）及其安全功能。

英文原文

Hey everyone,let's talk about something you might not have thought about.

Controlling USB ports through BIOS or UEFI settings.

You can actually enable or disable USB ports,control whether computers can boot from USB and set various USB related security options.

This might sound paranoid,but in certain environments like corporate offices,schools or secure facilities,controlling USB access is a serious security concern.

Let's explore why and how you'd manage USB permissions.

Think about what USB ports can do.

They can transfer files,boot computers,charge devices,connect keyboards and mice and basically interact with your system in countless ways.

From a security perspective,USB ports are potential vulnerabilities.

Someone could plug in a USB stick loaded with malware.

They could copy confidential files to a flash drive and walk out.

They could boot from a USB drive to bypass Windows passwords.

They could even use USB devices for hardware keyloggers.

In high security environments,controlling USB access isn't paranoia.

It's necessary protection against very real threats.

The nuclear option is disabling USB ports completely through BIOS or UEFI.

When you disable USB,the ports literally stop working.

Plug in a flash drive and nothing happens,not even a light.

This prevents all USB-based attacks but creates obvious problems.No USB keyboards or mice work either.

This setting is really only useful for kiosk systems or computers in extremely secure areas where USB ports are physically sealed anyway.

Most organizations don't go this far because it's too restrictive for daily work.

A more practical option is disabling USB storage devices while keeping other USB devices working.

Some BIOS or UEFI implementations let you distinguish between USB storage like flash drives and external hard drives and other USB devices like keyboards,mice and printers.

This is the sweet spot for many organizations.

Employees can still use their USB keyboards and mice but they can't plug in USB drives to copy files or introduce malware.

Of course,clever users might find workarounds but it raises the barrier and deters casual misuse.

Another important USB permission is whether the computer can boot from USB devices.

Remember boot order from the last lecture?

You can configure BIOS or UEFI to completely remove USB from the boot options or require a password to boot from USB.

This prevents someone from booting a live Linux USB stick to access your files,reset passwords or bypass security.

In corporate environments,you typically want this disabled or password protected.

For home users and IT departments,keeping USB boot enabled makes system recovery and installation much easier.

Some advanced UEFI implementations let you control individual USB ports or groups of ports.

For example,you might disable front panel USB ports,which are easy to access,while leaving rear ports enabled.

Or you might disable USB 3 ports while keeping USB 2 ports working.

This granular control is useful in situations where you want some USB functionality but want to make it less convenient to use.

It's like putting your cookie jar on a high shelf,not impossible to reach,but inconvenient enough to make you think twice.

To configure USB permissions,enter your BIOS or UEFI setup during boot,usually by pressing delete,F2 or F10.

Look for sections labeled Integrated Peripherals,Advanced,Security or USB configuration.

The exact location varies by manufacturer.

You'll find options like USB controller,legacy USB support,USB storage support,external USB ports and boot from USB.

Some settings might be simple enable or disable toggles while others offer more detailed control.

Modern UEFI interfaces make these settings easier to find and configure than old BIOS screens.

Here's an interesting setting you'll see,Legacy USB support.

This makes USB keyboards and mice work in DOS,older operating systems,and during boot before your main OS loads.

If you disable legacy USB support,your USB keyboard won't work in BIOS or UEFI setup or in the Windows boot menu.

Awkward.

You'd need a PS or 2 keyboard to change settings.

Most people should leave legacy USB support enabled unless you specifically need to disable it for security reasons.

It's one of those don't touch it unless you have a reason settings.

In corporate environments,USB restrictions are often part of a comprehensive security policy.

IT departments might disable USB storage at the BIOS level,enforce device control policies through Windows Group policy,use software like Microsoft Intune to manage device access,require encryption on approved USB drives,and audit USB usage through logging systems.

The BIOS level control is the foundation layer that catches attempts to bypass operating system security.

It's not foolproof.

Determined attackers can reset BIOS settings,but it stops casual threats and lazy users.

For home users,the calculus is different.

You probably want full USB functionality for convenience,installing operating systems,connecting devices,transferring files,and general computing.

Disabling USB features only makes sense if you share your computer with people you don't fully trust or if you're setting up a kiosk or public facing system.

Otherwise,the inconvenience outweighs the security benefit.

Just be smart.

Don't plug in random USB sticks you find.

Keep your antivirus updated and practice good security hygiene.

That's usually enough for home environments.

If USB devices aren't working,BIOS settings might be the culprit.

Check that USB ports are enabled in BIOS or UEFI.

Someone might have disabled them.

Verify legacy USB support is enabled if your keyboard doesn't work during boot.

Make sure USB storage isn't disabled if flash drives won't be recognized.

Sometimes,after BIOS updates or battery replacements,settings reset to defaults.

If you are helping someone troubleshoot mysterious USB problems,checking BIOS settings should be on your list.It's an easy thing to overlook but can completely explain why USB devices suddenly stopped working.

That's USB permissions in BIOS.

Remember,you can control USB ports through BIOS or UEFI settings for security purposes.

Options include disabling USB entirely,too restrictive for most users,or disabling USB storage only while keeping keyboards and mice working.

Better balance.

You can prevent booting from USB to stop password bypass attacks.

Legacy USB support makes USB keyboards work during boot and in BIOS setup.

Usually should be enabled.

These settings matter more in corporate and secure environments than at home.

Access these options in your BIOS or UEFI setup under sections like security or USB configuration.

Next,we'll explore TPM,Trusted Platform Module and its security features.

See you there.

148. TPM 安全功能

大家好，让我们来谈谈TPM，即可信平台模块，这是一项变得至关重要的安全功能，尤其是随着Windows 11对其提出了要求。

TPM本质上是您主板上的一块安全芯片，用于存储加密密钥并帮助保护您的计算机免受篡改。

如果您听说过BitLocker加密，或者想知道为什么Windows 11无法安装在较旧的计算机上，TPM是答案的重要组成部分。

让我们揭开TPM的作用及其重要性的神秘面纱。

TPM是一款专用的安全芯片。

可以把它想象成您主板上的一台微型计算机，它只有一个任务，就是安全。

它就像您加密密钥的私人保镖。

TPM将加密密钥、密码和证书安全地存储在独立于主系统的硬件中。

由于它是基于硬件的，因此比仅仅将密钥存储在软件中要安全得多，因为在软件中恶意软件可能会访问它们。

TPM可以是焊接到主板上的独立芯片，即离散TPM或DTPM，也可以是基于固件的，集成在您的CPU中，即固件TPM或FTPM。

TPM有不同的版本，主要是TPM 1.2和TPM 2.0。

TPM 1.2是二零一一年的旧标准，而TPM 2.0是二零一四年的当前标准，具有更高的安全性和功能。

关键点来了。

Windows 11需要TPM 2.0，而不是1.2。

这就是为什么一些拥有TPM 1.2的稍旧计算机无法正式运行Windows 11的原因。

TPM 2.0提供了更好的加密算法、改进的密钥管理以及对现代安全功能的支持。

如果您今天购买主板，它肯定具备TPM 2.0。

但二零一五年或更早的计算机可能只有TPM 1.2或者根本没有TPM。

许多计算机拥有TPM硬件，但默认情况下是禁用的。

您需要在BIOS或UEFI设置中启用它。

进入您的BIOS或UEFI设置，查找标记为安全、高级或PCHFW配置的部分。

您可能会看到它被称为TPM、TPM设备、安全芯片、英特尔系统上的PTT（平台信任技术）或AMD系统上的FTPM（固件TPM）。

这通常是一个简单的启用或禁用开关。

启用TPM后，保存并重启。

Windows将检测到它并开始将其用于安全功能。

如果您找不到该设置，您的系统可能没有TPM，或者它可能有不同的名称。

BitLocker是Windows的全盘加密功能，而TPM使其效果更佳。

BitLocker加密您的整个驱动器，因此如果有人窃取您的笔记本电脑或硬盘，如果没有您的密码，他们就无法访问您的数据。

如果没有TPM，BitLocker会要求您每次启动时都插入USB闪存盘。

非常烦人。

有了TPM，加密密钥被安全地存储在TPM芯片中，如果未被篡改，启动将自动进行。

它是透明的、安全的，而且实际上可用。

这就是企业喜欢TPM的原因。

他们可以在不让员工生活变得痛苦的情况下强制实施加密。

神奇之处在于：当您启用带有TPM的BitLocker时，TPM芯片会存储加密密钥，并且仅在启动过程未被篡改时才释放它。

每次启动计算机时，TPM都会检查您的BIOS、引导加载程序和启动文件是否未被更改。

如果一切正常，TPM会释放密钥，您的计算机将正常启动。

您甚至不知道BitLocker正在运行。

但是，如果有人修改您的引导扇区以安装恶意软件，或者有人移除您的硬盘并将其放入另一台计算机，TPM将不会释放密钥。

攻击者将被困在BitLocker密码屏幕前，无法通过。

安全启动是另一项与TPM协同工作的安全功能。

虽然安全启动使用数字签名验证您的操作系统是否未被篡改，但TPM为这些验证过程提供安全存储。

它们共同构建了一条信任链。TPM验证固件状态，固件通过安全启动验证引导加载程序，引导加载程序再验证Windows。

每一步在移交控制权之前都会检查下一步。

这使得恶意软件极难感染启动过程，因为任何更改都会破坏链条并阻止系统启动。

这就像一系列锁着的门，每扇门都会检查下一把钥匙。

除了BitLocker，TPM还存储其他敏感凭据。

Windows Hello（面部识别或指纹登录）使用TPM安全地存储生物特征数据。

Windows登录的PIN码可以由TPM保护。

用于VPN和企业网络的证书可以存储在TPM中。

一些企业应用程序将身份验证令牌存储在TPM中。

关键原则是：任何需要存储在计算机上的安全敏感信息，放在TPM中都比放在常规存储中更好，因为软件可能会访问常规存储。

硬件安全性从根本上强于软件安全性。

TPM有一个很酷的功能：远程证明。

TPM可以生成一份报告，证明正在使用哪些固件和启动组件，以及它们是否被篡改。

并且它可以以加密方式对该报告进行签名。

这对企业安全来说意义重大。

当您连接到企业网络时，公司可以询问您的TPM：“此系统是否处于受信任的启动状态？”而TPM会提供一个极难伪造的签名回答。

如果您的计算机通过了证明，您将获得访问权限。

如果没有，您将被阻止访问，直到IT部门解决问题。

这就像保镖在检查您的身份证，只不过这个身份证无法伪造，因为它是由TPM硬件创建的。

TPM并非没有争议。

有些人担心隐私问题。

TPM会让公司或政府监视您吗？

答案是否定的。TPM不会报告您在做什么，只会报告您的系统是否被篡改以及是否可以释放密钥。

有些人不喜欢Windows 11需要TPM，称其为计划性报废。

这里有一些道理。

要求TPM 2.0确实排除了一些较旧但仍能正常工作的计算机。

一些Linux用户和爱好者觉得TPM很烦人，因为它会使自定义设置变得复杂。

还有人担心企业控制问题。

如果您的雇主使用TPM证明，他们对设备状态的可见度会更高。

这些都是合理的担忧，但对于大多数用户来说，安全益处大于缺点。

想知道您的计算机是否有TPM吗？

在Windows中，按下Windows键加R，输入tpm.msc并按回车键。

这将打开TPM管理。

如果您看到有关TPM状态和版本的信息，说明您拥有它。

如果您看到“找不到兼容的TPM”，要么是您没有TPM，要么是它在BIOS或UEFI中被禁用了。

您也可以在Windows安全中心中检查，转到设备安全并查找安全处理器详细信息。

如果您正在选购新计算机并关心Windows 11，请确保规格列表中列出了TPM 2.0。

以上就是TPM，即可信平台模块。

请记住，TPM是您主板上的一块安全芯片，可安全地存储加密密钥并帮助防止篡改。

它有独立芯片形式或内置于CPU中的固件形式。

Windows 11需要TPM 2.0，而较旧的TPM 1.2则不够用。

在BIOS或UEFI设置中启用TPM。

根据您的系统，查找TPM、PTT或FTPM。

TPM通过安全地存储密钥并检查启动完整性，使BitLocker加密变得实用。

它与安全启动协同工作，构建一条信任链以保护您的启动过程。

TPM还存储Windows Hello、VPN和企业应用程序的凭据。

尽管存在一些争议，但TPM显著提高了大多数用户的安全性。

接下来，我们将更详细地探讨安全启动和启动密码。

届时见。

英文原文

Hey everyone,let's talk about TPM,Trusted Platform Module,a security feature that's become super important especially with Windows 11 requiring it.

TPM is basically a security chip on your motherboard that stores encryption keys and helps protect your computer from tampering.

If you've heard about BitLocker encryption or wondered why Windows 11 won't install on older computers,TPM is a big part of the answer.

Let's demystify what TPM does and why it matters.

TPM is a dedicated security chip.

Think of it as a tiny computer on your motherboard with one job,security.

It's like having a personal bodyguard for your encryption keys.

TPM securely stores cryptographic keys,passwords and certificates in hardware that's separate from your main system.

Because it's hardware based,it's much more secure than just storing keys in software where malware could potentially access them.

TPM can be a discrete chip soldered to your motherboard,discrete TPM or DTPM,or it can be firmware based,integrated into your CPU,firmware TPM or FTPM.

TPM comes in versions,mainly TPM 1.2 and TPM 2.0.

TPM 1.2 is the older standard from 2011 and TPM 2.0 is the current standard from 2014 with improved security and functionality.

Here's the kicker.

Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0,not 1.2.

This is why some slightly older computers that have TPM 1.2 can't officially run Windows 11.

TPM 2.0 offers better encryption algorithms,improved key management and support for modern security features.

If you're buying a motherboard today,it'll definitely have TPM 2.0.

But computers from 2015 or earlier might only have TPM 1.2 or no TPM at all.

Many computers have TPM hardware but it's disabled by default.

You need to enable it in BIOS or UEFI settings.

Enter your BIOS or UEFI setup and look for sections labeled security,advanced or PCHFW configuration.

You might see it called TPM,TPM Device,Security Chip,PTT on Intel Systems,Platform Trust Technology or FTPM on AMD systems firmware TPM.

It's usually a simple enable or disable toggle.

After enabling TPM,save and reboot.

Windows will detect it and start using it for security features.

If you can't find the setting,your system might not have TPM or it might be called something different.

BitLocker is Windows'full disk encryption feature,and TPM makes it way better.

BitLocker encrypts your entire drive,so if someone steals your laptop or hard drive,they can't access your data without your password.

Without TPM,BitLocker requires you to insert a USB stick every time you boot.

Super annoying.

With TPM,the encryption keys are stored securely in the TPM chip,and boot happens automatically if nothing's been tampered with.

It's transparent,secure,and actually usable.

This is why businesses love TPM.

They can enforce encryption without making employees'lives miserable.

Here's the magic:when you enable BitLocker with TPM,the TPM chip stores the encryption key and only releases it if the boot process hasn't been tampered with.

Every time you start your computer,TPM checks that your BIOS,bootloader,and boot files haven't changed.

If everything's normal,TPM releases the key and your computer boots normally.

You don't even know BitLocker is running.

But if someone modifies your boot sector to install malware,or if someone removes your hard drive and puts it in another computer,TPM won't release the key.

The attacker is stuck at a BitLocker password screen with no way through.

Secure Boot is another security feature that works alongside TPM.

While Secure Boot verifies that your operating system hasn't been tampered with using digital signatures,TPM provides the secure storage for those verification processes.

Together,they create a chain of trust.TPM verifies firmware state,firmware verifies the bootloader through secure boot,and the bootloader verifies Windows.

Each step checks the next step before passing control forward.

This makes it incredibly hard for malware to infect the boot process because any changes break the chain and prevent the system from starting.

It's like a series of locked doors where each door checks the next key.

Beyond BitLocker,TPM stores other sensitive credentials.

Windows Hello,the facial recognition or fingerprint login,uses TPM to store biometric data securely.

PIN codes for Windows login can be protected by TPM.

Certificates for VPNs and corporate networks can be stored in TPM.

Some enterprise applications store authentication tokens in TPM.

The key principle is:anything security sensitive that needs to be stored on your computer is better off in TPM than in regular storage where software could potentially access it.

Hardware security is fundamentally stronger than software security.

Here's a cool TPM feature:remote attestation.

TPM can generate a report proving what firmware and boot components are in use and whether they've been tampered with.

And it can sign that report cryptographically.

This is huge for enterprise security.

when you connect to a corporate network,the company can ask your TPM,Is this system in a trusted boot state?

And TPM provides a signed answer that's extremely difficult to fake.

If your computer passes attestation,you get access.

If not,you're blocked until IT fixes the problem.

It's like a bouncer checking your ID,except the ID can't be forged because TPM hardware creates it.

TPM isn't without controversy.

Some people worry about privacy.

Does TPM let companies or governments spy on you?

The answer is no.TPM doesn't report what you're doing,just whether your system has been tampered with and whether keys can be released.

Some people dislike that Windows 11 requires TPM,calling it planned obsolescence.

There's some truth here.

Requiring TPM 2.0 does exclude older but still functional computers.

Some Linux users and tinkerers find TPM annoying because it can complicate custom setups.

And there are concerns about corporate control.

If your employer uses TPM attestation,they have more visibility into device posture.

Valid concerns,but for most users,the security benefits outweigh the drawbacks.

Want to know if your computer has TPM?

In Windows,press Windows Key plus R,type tpm.msc and press enter.

This opens TPM management.

If you see information about TPM status and version,you have it.

If you see compatible TPM cannot be found,either you don't have TPM or it's disabled in BIOS or UEFI.

You can also check in Windows security,go to device security and look for security processor details.

If you're shopping for a new computer and care about Windows 11,make sure TPM 2.0 is listed in the specifications.

That's TPM,Trusted Platform Module.

Remember,TPM is a security chip on your motherboard that securely stores encryption keys and helps protect against tampering.

It comes in discrete chip form or firmware form built into your CPU.

TPM 2.0 is required for Windows 11 while older TPM 1.2 isn't sufficient.

Enable TPM in BIOS or UEFI settings.

Look for TPM,PTT or FTPM,depending on your system.

TPM makes BitLocker encryption practical by storing keys securely and checking boot integrity.

It works with Secure Boot to create a chain of trust protecting your boot process.

TPM also stores credentials for Windows Hello,VPNs and enterprise applications.

Despite some controversies,TPM significantly improves security for most users.

Next,we'll explore secure boot and boot passwords in more detail.

See you there.

149. 安全启动与启动密码

大家好，我们刚刚了解了TPM。

现在让我们深入探讨另外两个BIOS或UEFI安全功能：安全启动和启动密码。

安全启动可防止未经授权的操作系统和恶意软件在启动过程中加载，而启动密码则限制谁能开启计算机或更改BIOS设置。

这些功能共同构建了多层防护。

无论您是在保护企业笔记本电脑还是家用电脑，了解这些工具都能帮助您加固系统。

让我们来看看它们是如何工作的。

安全启动就像夜店门口的保镖在检查身份证。

它在允许加载之前，验证您的操作系统和启动文件是否合法。

当启用安全启动时，您的UEFI固件会检查引导加载程序和操作系统文件上的数字签名。

这些签名就像防篡改封条。

如果签名有效且受信任，启动将正常继续。

如果签名缺失、无效或不受信任，启动将停止并显示错误。

这可以防止根套件和引导套件，即那些试图在Windows加载之前感染计算机的恶意软件。

没有有效签名，就不予放行。

安全启动使用数字证书链。

微软和其他组织拥有签署密钥，UEFI固件默认信任这些密钥。

当微软对Windows进行签名时，该签名证明了“是的，这是合法的Windows，而不是伪装成Windows的恶意软件”。

您的UEFI固件拥有一个名为签名数据库的受信任证书数据库，并据此检查引导加载程序。

如果引导加载程序由受信任的密钥签名，启动将继续。

这种信任链确保启动过程的每一步都经过上一步的验证。

这实际上非常巧妙。

有趣的地方来了。

安全启动可能会使Linux安装变得复杂。

许多Linux发行版现在支持带有已签名引导加载程序的安全启动，因此它们运行良好。

Ubuntu、Fedora和其他主要发行版都内置了安全启动支持。

然而，一些较小的发行版或自定义内核未签名，这意味着安全启动会阻止它们。

解决方案是暂时禁用安全启动以安装Linux，或者自行管理签名密钥，但这属于高级操作领域。

对于Windows和Linux的双启动系统，您需要选择支持安全启动的发行版，或者愿意禁用它。

若要管理安全启动，请进入UEFI设置并查找启动安全或认证部分。

您将看到安全启动选项，通常显示为启用或禁用状态。

某些系统提供安全启动模式下拉菜单，选项包括标准或自定义。

禁用安全启动通常很简单。

只需将其关闭，保存并重启。

然而，某些系统要求先设置管理员密码才能禁用安全启动，以防止未经授权的更改。

禁用安全启动后，您可以安装未签名的操作系统，但会失去这一安全层。

您可能需要在以下几种情况下禁用安全启动：安装早于安全启动出现的旧版本Windows（如Windows 7）；安装不支持安全启动的Linux发行版；排查安全启动可能干扰的启动问题；安装某些未签名的硬件驱动程序；或者为高级设置运行自定义引导加载程序。

对于日常的Windows 10或Windows 11使用，请保持安全启动启用。

它能防范真实的威胁。

仅在您有特定理由时禁用它，并在之后尽可能重新启用。

现在让我们谈谈启动密码。

管理员密码，也称为管理员密码或设置密码，用于保护您的BIOS或UEFI设置。

设置后，您必须输入此密码才能访问设置实用程序。

这可以防止未经授权的人员更改启动顺序、禁用安全功能或修改硬件设置。

在企业环境中，IT部门会设置管理员密码且不向用户透露。

这将系统锁定。

用户可以正常使用计算机，但无法更改固件设置。

对于个人电脑，管理员密码是可选的，但如果他人能物理接触您的机器，则非常有用。

开机密码，也称为用户密码或启动密码，限制更为严格。

设置后，您每次启动计算机时都必须输入此密码，甚至在操作系统加载之前。

可以把它看作是Windows之前的密码。

如果没有正确的密码，计算机根本无法启动。

您会被卡在密码屏幕处。

这可以防止有人物理窃取您的计算机并试图启动它。

然而，这对日常使用来说不太方便。

您每次启动都需要输入此密码。

若要设置密码，请进入BIOS或UEFI设置并查找安全部分。

您通常会看到设置管理员密码和设置用户密码或设置开机密码的选项。

选择该选项，输入您想要的密码（通常为六到二十个字符），然后确认。

请记下此密码并妥善保存。

如果您忘记了固件密码，恢复访问权限将非常困难，可能需要通过移除主板电池或使用专用跳线来物理重置CMOS。

某些企业系统拥有制造商提供的主密码，但消费级主板通常没有，因此请认真对待这些密码。

让我们厘清密码类型。

管理员或管理员密码保护BIOS或UEFI设置。

您需要它来更改配置，但不需要它来启动计算机，这有利于防止篡改。

开机或用户密码是启动计算机所必需的。

安全性更强，但日常使用不便。

硬盘密码（由某些硬盘支持）在硬件级别锁定驱动器，独立于Windows密码，这可能很强大，但如果忘记密码则风险很大。

在实际环境中，您可以分层使用这些措施。

使用管理员密码锁定固件设置。

使用Windows登录进行用户访问，并使用BitLocker进行数据保护。

这些安全功能提供了实实在在的好处。

它们防止普通用户篡改系统设置，防范某些形式的物理访问滥用，并作为纵深防御补充操作系统安全。

然而，它们也有局限性。

固件密码有时可以通过硬件方法重置。

拥有物理访问权限的坚定攻击者，只要有足够的时间和工具，就能绕过保护措施，而忘记密码可能会将您拒之门外。

实践考试的思路是将控制措施与环境相匹配，而不是在所有地方启用所有功能。

以下是一些明智的做法。

对于家中的个人电脑，保持安全启动启用，并依赖Windows密码和BitLocker；如果您需要强大的保护，除非有明确理由，否则无需添加额外的固件密码。

对于工作笔记本电脑，常见的做法是启用安全启动，由IT部门设置管理员密码以防止篡改，并将BitLocker加密作为基线。

对于家庭共用电脑，启用安全启动，使用独立的Windows账户，如果有人喜欢摆弄设置，还可以设置管理员密码。

对于真正敏感的数据，结合使用安全启动、管理员密码、在适当情况下使用开机密码以及全盘加密，并安全地记录密码。

以上就是安全启动和启动密码的内容。

请记住，安全启动验证引导加载程序和操作系统上的数字签名，防止恶意软件感染启动过程。

它与Windows 10和Windows 11开箱即用兼容，大多数现代Linux发行版也支持它，但您可能需要为旧操作系统或未签名的引导加载程序暂时禁用它。

管理员密码保护BIOS或UEFI设置免受未经授权的更改，而开机密码则要求计算机在启动前必须输入密码。

在BIOS或UEFI安全设置中设置这些密码并妥善保存，因为如果忘记，恢复可能会很困难。

与TPM和BitLocker一起，这些功能为您的计算机提供了强大的保护。

接下来，我们将讨论BIOS或UEFI中的温度监控和风扇控制。

届时见！

英文原文

Hey everyone,we just learned about TPM.

Now let's dig deeper into two more BIOS or UEFI security features,Secure Boot and Boot Passwords.

Secure Boot prevents unauthorized operating systems and malware from loading during startup,while boot passwords restrict who can even turn on your computer or change BIOS settings.

Together,these features create multiple layers of protection.

Whether you are securing a corporate laptop or protecting a home computer,understanding these tools helps you lock things down.

Let's explore how they work.

Secure Boot is like a bouncer at a club checking IDs.

It verifies that your operating system and boot files are legitimate before allowing them to load.

When Secure Boot is enabled,your UEFI firmware checks digital signatures on bootloaders and operating system files.

These signatures are like tamper-proof seals.

If the signature is valid and trusted,boot continues normally.

If the signature is missing,invalid or not trusted,boot stops with an error.

This prevents rootkits and boot kits,malware that tries to infect your computer before Windows even loads.

No valid signature,no entry.

Secure Boot uses a chain of digital certificates.

Microsoft and other organizations have signing keys that UEFI firmware trusts by default.

When Microsoft signs Windows,that signature proves yes,this is legitimate Windows,not malware pretending to be Windows.

Your UEFI firmware has a database of trusted certificates called the signature database and checks bootloaders against it.

If the bootloader was signed by a trusted key,boot continues.

This chain of trust ensures that every step of the boot process is verified by the previous step.

It's actually pretty clever.

Here's where things get interesting.

Secure boot can complicate Linux installations.

Many Linux distributions now support secure boot with signed bootloaders,so they work fine.

Ubuntu,Fedora and other major distributions have secure boot support built in.

However,some smaller distributions or custom kernels aren't signed,which means secure boot blocks them.

The solution is to disable secure boot temporarily to install Linux or manage signing keys yourself,which is advanced territory.

For dual boot systems with Windows and Linux,you'll need distributions that support secure boot or be willing to disable it.

To manage secure boot,enter your UEFI setup and look for boot security or authentication sections.

You'll see a secure boot option,typically with enable or disable status.

Some systems have a secure boot mode dropdown with options like standard or custom.

Disabling secure boot is usually straightforward.

Just toggle it off,save and reboot.

However,some systems require setting a supervisor password before you can disable secure boot,which prevents unauthorized changes.

After disabling Secure Boot,you can install unsigned operating systems,but you lose that security layer.

You might need to disable secure boot in several situations:installing older versions of Windows like Windows 7 that predate secure boot,installing Linux distributions without secure boot support,troubleshooting boot problems where secure boot might be interfering,

installing certain hardware drivers that aren't signed,or running custom bootloaders for advanced setups.

For everyday Windows 10 or Windows 11 use,keep Secure Boot enabled.

It protects against real threats.

Only disable it when you have a specific reason and re-enable it afterward if possible.

Now let's talk about boot passwords.

The supervisor password,also called Administrator Password or Setup Password,protects your BIOS or UEFI settings.

When set,you must enter this password to access the setup utility.

This prevents unauthorized people from changing boot order,disabling security features,or modifying hardware settings.

In corporate environments,IT departments set supervisor passwords and don't share them with users.

This locks down the system.

Users can use their computer normally,but they can't change firmware settings.

For personal computers,supervisor passwords are optional but useful if others have physical access to your machine.

The power on password,also called user password or boot password,is more restrictive.

When set,you must enter this password every time you start the computer before the operating system even loads.

Think of it as a pre-Windows password.

Without the correct password,the computer won't boot at all.

You are stuck at a password screen.

This protects against someone physically stealing your computer and trying to start it.

However,it's inconvenient for daily use.

You need to enter this password every boot.

To set passwords,enter BIOS or UEFI setup and look for a security section.

You'll typically see options for set supervisor password and set user password or set power on password.

Select the option,enter your desired password,often 6-20 characters,and confirm it.

Write this password down and store it safely.

If you forget your firmware password,recovering access is difficult and might require physically resetting CMOS by removing the motherboard battery or using a special jumper.

Some enterprise systems have master passwords from the manufacturer,but consumer boards often don't,so treat these passwords seriously.

Let's clarify the password types.

Supervisor or administrator password protects BIOS or UEFI settings.

You need it to change configurations but not to boot the computer,which is good for preventing tampering.

Power on or user password is required to boot the computer at all.

Stronger security but daily inconvenience.

Hard drive password,supported by some drives,locks the drive at the hardware level and is separate from Windows passwords,which can be powerful but risky if forgotten.

In real environments,you can layer these.

Lock firmware settings with a supervisor password.

Use a Windows login for user access and use BitLocker for data protection.

These security features provide real benefits.

They prevent casual users from tampering with system settings,protect against some forms of physical access abuse and complement operating system security for defense in depth.

However,they have limitations.

Firmware passwords can sometimes be reset through hardware methods.

Determined attackers with physical access can bypass protections given enough time and tools and forgotten passwords can lock you out.

The practical exam mindset is to match the control to the environment,not to enable every feature everywhere.

Here are smart practices.

For personal computers at home,keep secure boot enabled and rely on Windows passwords and BitLocker if you need strong protection without adding extra firmware passwords unless you have a clear reason.

For work laptops,secure boot enabled,a supervisor password set by IT to prevent tampering and bit locker encryption as a baseline is common.

For shared family computers,secure boot enabled,separate Windows accounts and possibly a supervisor password if people like to tinker.

For truly sensitive data,combine secure boot,supervisor password,power on password where appropriate and full disk encryption and document passwords securely.

That's secure boot and boot passwords.

Remember,secure boot verifies digital signatures on bootloaders and operating systems,preventing malware from infecting the boot process.

It works with Windows 10 and Windows 11 out of the box and most modern Linux distributions support it too,but you might disable it temporarily for older operating systems or unsigned bootloaders.

Supervisor password protects BIOS or UEFI settings from unauthorized changes while power on password requires a password before the computer will boot at all.

Set these passwords in BIOS or UEFI security settings and store them safely because recovery can be difficult if you forget.

Together with TPM and BitLocker,these features create strong protection for your computer.

Next,we'll talk about temperature monitoring and fan control in BIOS or UEFI.

See you there!

150. 温度监控与风扇控制

大家好，让我们来谈谈一个关键却常被忽视的话题。

监控计算机温度并控制风扇转速。

您的BIOS或UEFI内置了工具，可监控组件的运行温度并相应调整风扇转速。

过热是导致系统不稳定、崩溃和硬件损坏的主要原因之一。

了解热管理有助于让您的计算机保持凉爽、安静且稳定运行。

让我们探讨需要关注哪些温度以及如何控制散热。

热量是电子元件的大敌。

当您的CPU、GPU或其他组件温度过高时，会发生几种不良情况。

首先，会触发热节流。

您的CPU会自动降频以减少热量，导致性能下降。

其次，随着组件超负荷运转，系统崩溃和蓝屏会变得更加频繁。

第三，长期暴露在高温下会缩短组件的使用寿命。

一台持续运行在九十摄氏度的CPU，其寿命不如运行在六十摄氏度的CPU长。

第四，在极端情况下，组件可能会遭受永久性损坏。

监控温度并非杞人忧天，而是一种能节省资金和避免烦恼的预防性维护。

若要在BIOS或UEFI中检查温度，请在启动期间进入设置实用程序。

根据您的主板不同，按下Delete、F2或F10键。

查找标记为硬件监控、HW Monitor、PC健康状态或系统信息的部分。

您将看到带有实时读数的温度传感器列表。

典型的传感器包括通常最重要的CPU温度、主板或系统温度，有时还有芯片组温度。

某些系统还会显示电压读数和风扇转速。

这些读数会实时更新，因此您可以观察系统在空闲时温度的变化。

让我们谈谈具体数值。

对于CPU，在空闲状态下，即仅停留在BIOS屏幕时，三十到四十五摄氏度属于正常范围。

在负载下，大多数CPU的典型温度为六十到八十摄氏度，游戏和工作站CPU在高负载压力下有时会达到八十五摄氏度，这仍然可能是正常的。

持续高于九十摄氏度则令人担忧，表明存在散热问题。不同的CPU有不同的最高温度，通常称为TJmax。

许多Intel CPU的最高温度约为一百度，而许多AMD Ryzen CPU约为九十五度。

您的CPU在达到最高温度之前会进行节流，但为了延长寿命和保持性能，您希望温度远低于该极限。

除了温度外，BIOS或UEFI还会显示以RPM（每分钟转数）为单位的风扇转速。

典型的机箱风扇转速根据尺寸和设置在六百到一千五百RPM之间。

CPU风扇在负载下可能运行在八百到两千RPM或更高。

主板上的风扇接头会将这些转速报告回系统。

如果风扇显示零RPM，则说明它未连接、未插入正确的接头或已故障。

有些风扇不报告转速。

它们工作正常，但接头接收不到信号。

监控风扇转速有助于您在过热发生之前及早发现故障。

大多数BIOS或UEFI系统提供风扇控制模式。

手动模式将风扇设置为固定速度，例如百分之五十或百分之八十，而不考虑温度。

这很简单且可预测，但并非最佳选择。

自动或智能模式会根据温度调整风扇转速。

温度低时风扇转得慢以保持安静，温度高时转得快以提供更好的散热，这通常是最佳选择。

PWM模式是一种更精确且更安静的自动控制类型。

DC模式是更简单的电压控制。

大多数现代风扇和主板都支持PWM，这通常是首选。

高级的BIOS或UEFI实现允许您创建自定义风扇曲线。

风扇曲线是一个图表，显示不同温度下的风扇转速。

例如，在三十度时，风扇以百分之二十的速度运行以保持安静。

在五十度时，它们加速到百分之五十。

在七十度时，它们达到百分之八十，而在八十度及以上时，它们全速运行。

您可以调整这些点以平衡噪音和散热。

想要更安静的运行？

在低温下保持较低的转速。

需要最大散热？

更早地提高风扇转速。

自定义曲线让您完全控制散热行为。

若要调整风扇控制，请在BIOS或UEFI中查找标记为风扇控制、Q-Fan Control、Smart Fan或硬件监控的部分。

您将看到主板上每个风扇接头的选项，如CPU Fan、SysFan 1、SysFan 2等。

对于每个接头，您通常可以选择一种模式。

静音或安静模式优先考虑低噪音，标准或正常模式平衡噪音和散热，性能或涡轮模式优先考虑最大散热，而自定义或手动模式允许您定义自己的曲线。

某些系统还允许您设置最小和最大风扇转速，以防止风扇完全停止或旋转过快。CPU风扇和系统风扇之间有一个重要的区别。

CPU风扇接头为您的CPU散热器供电，并且通常根据CPU温度进行温控。

这一点很重要，因为如果CPU升温，其风扇应立即响应。

系统风扇，有时称为机箱风扇，负责提供穿过机箱的气流，其控制可能基于CPU温度、主板温度或传感器的综合数据。

某些系统允许您选择哪个温度传感器控制哪些风扇。

为了获得最佳效果，请将CPU风扇链接到CPU温度，并将系统风扇链接到主板温度或最相关的高温传感器。

如果您发现温度过高，这是您的检查清单。首先，检查风扇转速。

所有风扇都在运行吗？它们在负载下是否加速了？

第二，检查您的风扇曲线设置。

也许风扇没有足够早地增加转速。

第三，验证您的CPU散热器是否正确安装，接触良好且涂抹了导热硅脂。

第四，检查是否有灰尘堆积并将其清理掉。

第五，验证机箱气流。

进风和排风风扇应正确定向且未被阻挡。

第六，考虑环境因素。

炎热的房间会升高温度。

大多数温度问题如果您系统地排查，都有简单的解决方法。

您还可以使用软件工具在Windows内部监控温度，这些工具读取相同的传感器，通常带有图表、警报和日志记录功能。

软件监控对于日常使用更为方便，因为您无需重启进入BIOS或UEFI，并且可以显示游戏或渲染等实际工作负载下的温度。

BIOS监控仍然适用于系统空闲时的基线检查以及安全地更改风扇设置。

一个可靠的工作流程是在BIOS或UEFI中设置风扇曲线，然后在Windows中根据用户实际运行的工作负载验证温度。

以上就是温度监控和风扇控制的内容。

请记住，热管理对于系统稳定性和寿命至关重要。

在BIOS或UEFI的硬件监控或电脑健康部分访问温度读数。

正常的CPU温度在空闲时为三十到四十五度，在负载下为六十到八十五度，而持续高于九十度的温度通常表明存在问题。

风扇控制模式包括手动和自动，其中带PWM的自动模式通常最佳。自定义风扇曲线让您能够精确平衡噪音和散热。

将CPU风扇链接到CPU温度，并保持气流畅通无阻。

接下来，我们将探讨BIOS或UEFI中的虚拟化支持。

届时见。

英文原文

Hey everyone,let's talk about something critical but often overlooked.

Monitoring your computer's temperature and controlling fan speeds.

Your BIOS or UEFI has built-in tools to watch how hot your components are running and adjust fan speeds accordingly.

Overheating is one of the main causes of system instability,crashes and hardware damage.

Understanding thermal management helps you keep your computer running cool,quiet and stable.

Let's explore what temperatures to watch and how to control your cooling.

Heat is the enemy of electronics.

When your CPU,GPU or other components get too hot,several bad things happen.

First,thermal throttling kicks in.

Your CPU automatically slows down to reduce heat,killing performance.

Second,system crashes and blue screens become more common as components struggle.

Third,long-term exposure to high temperatures shortens component lifespan.

A CPU running at 90 degrees Celsius constantly won't last as long as one running at 60 degrees.

Fourth,in extreme cases,components can suffer permanent damage.

Monitoring temperature isn't paranoia,it's preventive maintenance that saves money and frustration.

To check temperatures in BIOS or UEFI,enter your setup utility during boot.

Press Delete,F2 or F10 depending on your motherboard.

Look for sections labeled hardware monitor,HW monitor,PC health status or system information.

You'll see a list of temperature sensors with real-time readings.

Typical sensors include CPU temperature,often the most important,motherboard or system temperature and sometimes chipset temperature.

Some systems also show voltage readings and fan speeds.

These readings update in real time so you can watch temperatures change as your system sits idle.

Let's talk numbers.

For CPUs at idle,just sitting at the BIOS screen,30 to 45 degrees Celsius is normal.

Under load,60 to 80 degrees is typical for most CPUs with gaming and workstation CPUs sometimes reaching 85 degrees under heavy stress and that can still be normal.

Above 90 degrees consistently is concerning and suggests cooling problems.Different CPUs have different maximum temperatures,often called TJmax.

Many Intel CPUs are around 100 degrees and many AMD Ryzen CPUs are around 95 degrees.

Your CPU will throttle before hitting the maximum but you want to stay well below it for longevity and performance.

Along with temperatures,BIOS or UEFI shows fan speeds measured in RPM,revolutions per minute.

Typical case fans run at 600 to 1500 RPM depending on size and settings.

CPU fans might run eight hundred to two thousand rpm or higher under load.

Fan headers on your motherboard report these speeds back to the system.

If a fan shows 0 RPM,it's either not connected,not plugged into the right header or failed.

Some fans don't report speed.

They work fine,but the header doesn't get the signal.

Monitoring fan speeds helps you catch failures early before overheating happens.

Most BIOS or UEFI systems offer fan control modes.

Manual mode sets fans to a fixed speed like 50%or 80%regardless of temperature.

This is simple and predictable but not optimal.

Automatic or smart mode adjusts fan speed based on temperature.

Fans spin slower when cool for quiet operation and faster when hot for better cooling,which is usually the best choice.

PWM mode is a type of automatic control that's more precise and quieter.

DC mode is simpler voltage control.

Most modern fans and motherboards support PWM which is typically preferable.

Advanced BIOS or UEFI implementations let you create custom fan curves.

A fan curve is a graph showing fan speed at different temperatures.

For example,at 30 degrees fans run at 20%speed for quiet operation.

At 50 degrees they ramp to 50%.

At 70 degrees they hit 80%and at 80 degrees and above they run full speed.

You can adjust these points to balance noise and cooling.

Want quieter operation?

Keep speeds lower at low temperatures.

Need maximum cooling?

Ramp up fans earlier.

Custom curves give you total control over cooling behavior.

To adjust fan control,look for sections in BIOS or UEFI labeled fan control,Q fan control,smart fan or hardware monitor.

You'll see options for each fan header on your motherboard CPU fan,sysfan 1,sysfan 2 and so on.

For each header,you can usually select a mode.

Silent or quiet prioritizes low noise,standard or normal balances noise and cooling,performance or turbo prioritizes maximum cooling and custom or manual lets you define your own curve.

Some systems also let you set minimum and maximum fan speeds to prevent fans from stopping completely or spinning too fast.There's an important distinction between CPU fans and system fans.

The CPU fan header powers your CPU cooler and is usually temperature controlled based on CPU temperature.

And that matters because if the CPU heats up,its fan should respond immediately.

System fans,sometimes called chassis fans or case fans,provide airflow through your case and might be controlled by C P U temperature,motherboard temperature,or a composite of sensors.

Some systems let you choose which temperature sensor controls which fans.

For best results,link the CPU fan to CPU temperature and link system fans to motherboard temperature or the hottest relevant sensor.

If you're seeing high temperatures,here's your checklist.First,check fan speeds.

Are all fans running and are they ramping up under load?

Second,check your fan curve settings.

Maybe fans aren't increasing speed early enough.

Third,verify your CPU cooler is properly installed with good contact and thermal paste applied.

Fourth,check for dust buildup and clean it out.

Fifth,verify case airflow.

Intake and exhaust fans should be oriented correctly and not blocked.

Sixth,consider the environment.

A hot room will raise temperatures.

Most temperature problems have simple fixes if you troubleshoot systematically.

You can also monitor temperatures from within Windows using software tools that read the same sensors,often with graphs,alerts and logging.

Software monitoring is more convenient for day-to-day use because you don't need to reboot into BIOS or UEFI and it shows temperatures under real workloads like games or rendering.

BIOS monitoring is still useful for baseline checking when the system is idle and for changing fan settings safely.

A solid workflow is to set fan curves in BIOS or UEFI,then validate temperatures in Windows under the workloads the user actually runs.

That's temperature monitoring and fan control.

Remember,thermal management is crucial for system stability and lifespan.

Access temperature readings in BIOS or UEFI under hardware monitor or PC health sections.

Normal CPU temperatures are 30 to 45 degrees idle and 60 to 85 degrees under load,while consistent temperatures above 90 degrees usually indicate a problem.

Fan control modes include manual and automatic and automatic with PWM is usually best.Custom fan curves let you balance noise and cooling precisely.

Link CPU fans to CPU temperature and keep airflow clean and unobstructed.

Next,we'll explore virtualization support in BIOS or UEFI.

See you there.

151. 虚拟化支持

大家好，让我们来聊聊虚拟化，这项技术让你能在一台电脑上同时运行多个操作系统。

也许你想在Windows里运行Linux，或者在虚拟机中测试软件，而无需冒主系统受损的风险。

你的处理器拥有让虚拟化高效运行的特殊功能，但它们通常在BIOS或UEFI中默认处于禁用状态。

你需要启用它们。

了解虚拟化支持有助于你使用VirtualBox、VMware、Hyper-V等工具，甚至运行安卓模拟器。

让我们探索它是如何工作的。

虚拟化让你能够创建称为虚拟机或VM的虚拟计算机，它们运行在你真实的计算机内部。

每台虚拟机都认为自己是一台拥有独立处理器、内存、硬盘和硬件的真实计算机，但这一切都是通过软件模拟的。

你可以将Windows作为主操作系统，然后同时运行一个Linux虚拟机和一个Windows Server虚拟机，所有这些都在这同一台物理计算机上。

这对于测试、开发、运行不兼容的软件以及学习新操作系统非常有用，而无需单独的物理计算机。

这就像在一个机箱里拥有了多台计算机。

过去运行虚拟机速度慢得令人痛苦，因为软件必须模拟一切。

后来处理器制造商添加了硬件虚拟化功能，让虚拟机能够更直接地访问处理器。

英特尔称其为VTX，即x86虚拟化技术。

AMD称其为AMDV，有时也称为SVM，意为安全虚拟机。

启用这些功能后，虚拟机的运行速度会快得多，有时几乎接近原生运行速度。

如果没有它们，虚拟化要么无法实现，要么慢得难以忍受。

这就是为什么如果你想有效使用虚拟机，在BIOS中启用虚拟化至关重要的原因。

英特尔VTX和AMDV基本上做着同样的事情。

它们添加了特殊的处理器指令，帮助管理程序，也就是运行你虚拟机的软件，高效地管理虚拟机。

这些功能让虚拟机能够直接使用处理器资源，而不是所有内容都通过软件转换。

它们还提供内存管理功能，防止虚拟机之间相互干扰或影响宿主系统。

这些技术在底层实现上有所不同。

英特尔和AMD使用不同的实现方式，但从你的角度来看，它们达成了相同的目标：快速、高效的虚拟化。

如果你使用的是英特尔处理器，你需要启用VTX。

如果是AMD处理器，你需要启用AMDV。

要启用虚拟化，请在启动期间进入BIOS或UEFI设置。

设置位置因制造商而异，但请查找标记为高级、处理器配置、系统配置或安全的部分。

该设置可能被称为英特尔虚拟化技术、英特尔VTX、AMDV、SVM模式、虚拟化或简称VT。

它通常是一个简单的启用或禁用开关。

有些系统还有其他相关设置，比如用于英特尔的VT到D，那是用于高级设备虚拟化，或者用于AMD的IOMMU。

对于基本的虚拟机使用，你只需要启用主虚拟化设置即可。

保存更改并重启。

你可能会想，既然虚拟化如此有用，为什么许多电脑上默认是禁用的呢？

有几个原因。

首先，大多数用户从不使用虚拟机，因此制造商不会启用大多数人都不需要的功能。

其次，存在微小的性能开销，尽管对大多数任务来说可以忽略不计。

第三，过去存在一些关于虚拟化被利用的安全担忧，尽管现代实现是安全的。

第四，制造商可能会禁用它以避免与某些软件出现兼容性问题。

无论原因是什么，这对需要它的用户来说都很令人沮丧。

好消息是，一旦你知道在哪里找，启用它只需一分钟。

想知道虚拟化是否已启用而无需重启进入BIOS吗？

很简单。

打开任务管理器，按下Control加Shift加Escape，然后点击性能选项卡。

在左侧面板中选择处理器。

查看右下角的处理器详细信息。

有一行显示虚拟化已启用或虚拟化已禁用。

这告诉你当前的状态。

如果显示已启用，那你就准备好了。

安装VirtualBox或你想要的任何管理程序。

如果显示已禁用，你需要重启进入BIOS并启用它。

这个快速检查可以避免你安装了虚拟机软件后才发现它无法工作。

管理程序是实际利用处理器的虚拟化功能来创建和管理虚拟机的软件。

流行的管理程序包括VirtualBox，免费且非常适合初学者，VMware Workstation，更专业且具备高级功能，VMware Player，免费，更简单的版本，Hyper-V，微软内置于Windows专业版和企业版中，还有Parallels，在Mac上很流行。

所有这些都需要启用处理器虚拟化。

有些管理程序在没有启用的情况下也能启动，但运行速度极慢。

另一些如Hyper-V，如果不启用虚拟化则根本无法工作。

先在BIOS中启用它，然后安装你选择的管理程序。

如果你使用的是Windows十专业版、企业版或Windows十一专业版，你可以使用Hyper-V，这是微软内置的虚拟化平台。

Hyper-V实际上非常好。

它是微软内部使用的平台，也是Azure云服务运行的基础。

然而，Hyper-V有严格的要求。

你需要在BIOS中启用处理器虚拟化，需要六十四位Windows，需要支持SLAT即二级地址转换的六十四位处理器。

大多数现代处理器都具备这一点，你至少需要四GB内存，不过建议八GB或更多。

一旦启用，Hyper-V能提供出色的虚拟机性能，特别是在Windows内部运行Windows虚拟机时。

这里有一个许多人没有意识到的事情：用于游戏或应用开发的安卓模拟器也使用处理器虚拟化。

像BlueStacks、Knox Player和Android Studio模拟器这样的模拟器，在启用VTX或AMDV后运行速度会快得多。

如果没有虚拟化，这些模拟器的速度慢得无法使用。

如果你想在电脑上玩手机游戏或开发安卓应用，在BIOS中启用虚拟化会带来翻天覆地的变化。

那个令人沮丧地缓慢、需要五分钟才能启动的模拟器，在启用虚拟化后，三十秒就能启动。

这可能是普通用户需要启用虚拟化最常见的原因。

想玩得更深入一点吗？

嵌套虚拟化允许你在虚拟机内部运行虚拟机。

例如，你可以在VMware虚拟机中运行Hyper-V。

这对于测试复杂设置或学习高级虚拟化非常有用，而无需多台物理计算机。

英特尔VTX和AMDV在最近的处理器上支持嵌套虚拟化，但你需要启用额外的设置。

在VMware中，你在虚拟机设置中启用虚拟化英特尔VTX和EPT，或者虚拟化AMDV和RVI。

在Hyper-V中，你使用PowerShell命令。

这是高级内容，但它是可行的。

性能会有所下降。

虚拟机里的虚拟机速度较慢，但仍可用于测试和学习。

如果虚拟化无法工作，这是你的故障排除清单。首先，验证处理器支持。

并非所有处理器都有VTX或AMDV，不过过去十年的任何处理器可能都有。

第二，在BIOS或UEFI中启用虚拟化。

这是最常见的问题。

第三，如果你想使用VMware或VirtualBox，请禁用Hyper-V。

Hyper-V会独占控制权，并可能阻止其他管理程序工作。

第四，检查BIOS更新。

一些旧版BIOS存在有缺陷的虚拟化实现。

第五，在任务管理器中验证虚拟化是否显示为已启用。

大多数虚拟化问题归根结底是忘记在BIOS中启用它，或者是管理程序之间的冲突。

这就是虚拟化支持。

请记住，虚拟化让你能够使用虚拟机同时运行多个操作系统。

英特尔处理器需要启用VTX，AMD处理器需要启用AMDV或SVM。

在BIOS或UEFI的高级或处理器配置部分找到这些设置。

硬件虚拟化使虚拟机的运行速度远快于纯软件虚拟化。

检查任务管理器的性能选项卡，以验证Windows中是否已启用虚拟化。

流行的管理程序包括VirtualBox、VMware、Hyper-V等。

它们都需要启用处理器虚拟化。

安卓模拟器也从虚拟化支持中受益匪浅。

如果虚拟机无法工作，请再次检查BIOS设置，并确保一次只激活一个管理程序。

接下来，我们将探讨带有TPM和HSM模块的硬件加密。

到时见。

英文原文

Hey everyone,let's talk about virtualization,the technology that lets you run multiple operating systems on one computer at the same time.

Maybe you want to run Linux inside Windows or test software in a virtual machine without risking your main system.

Your CPU has special features that make virtualization work efficiently,but they are often disabled by default in BIOS or UEFI.

You need to enable them.

Understanding virtualization support helps you use tools like VirtualBox,VMware,Hyper-V and even run Android emulators.

Let's explore how it works.

Virtualization lets you create virtual computers called virtual machines or VMs that run inside your real computer.

Each VM thinks it's a real computer with its own CPU,RAM,hard drive and hardware,but it's all simulated in software.

You could have Windows as your main operating system,then run a Linux VM and a Windows Server VM at the same time,all on the same physical computer.

This is incredibly useful for testing,development,running incompatible software and learning new operating systems without needing separate physical computers.

It's like having multiple computers in one box.

Running virtual machines used to be painfully slow because software had to simulate everything.

Then CPU manufacturers added hardware virtualization features that let virtual machines access the CPU more directly.

Intel calls theirs VTX,virtualization technology for x86.

AMD calls theirs AMDV,sometimes called SVM for secure virtual machine.

With these features enabled,virtual machines run much faster,sometimes nearly as fast as running natively.

Without them,virtualization is either impossible or unbearably slow.

This is why enabling virtualization in BIOS is crucial if you want to use VMs effectively.

Intel VTX and AMDV do basically the same thing.

They add special CPU instructions that help hypervisors,that's the software running your VMs,manage virtual machines efficiently.

These features let VMs use CPU resources directly instead of everything being translated through software.

They also provide memory management features that prevent VMs from interfering with each other or the host system.

The technologies are different under the hood.

Intel and AMD use different implementations,but from your perspective,they accomplish the same goal,fast,efficient virtualization.

If you have an Intel CPU,you need VTX enabled.

AMD CPU,you need AMD V enabled.

To enable virtualization,enter your BIOS or UEFI setup during boot.

The setting location varies by manufacturer,but look in sections labelled Advanced,CPU configuration,system configuration or security.

The setting might be called Intel Virtualization Technology,Intel VTX,AMD V,SVM Mode,Virtualization or just VT.

It's usually a simple enable or disable toggle.

Some systems have additional related settings like VT-D for Intel,that's for advanced device virtualization,or IOMMU for AMD.

For basic VM use,you just need the main virtualization setting enabled.

Save changes and reboot.

You might wonder if virtualization is so useful,why is it disabled by default on many computers?

A few reasons.

First,most users never use virtual machines,so manufacturers don't enable features most people don't need.

Second,there's a tiny performance overhead,though it's negligible for most tasks.

Third,some older security concerns existed about virtualization being exploited,though modern implementations are secure.

Fourth,manufacturers might disable it to avoid compatibility issues with certain software.

Whatever the reason,it's frustrating for users who need it.

The good news is,enabling it takes just a minute once you know where to look.

Want to know if virtualization is already enabled without rebooting into BIOS?

Easy.

Open Task Manager,press Ctrl-Shift-Escape and click the Performance tab.

Select CPU in the left panel.

Look at the bottom right where you see CPU details.

There's a line that says Virtualization Enabled or Virtualization Disabled.

That tells you the current status.

If it says enabled,you're good to go.

Install VirtualBox or whatever hypervisor you want.

If it says disabled,you'll need to reboot into BIOS and enable it.

This quick check saves you from installing VM software only to find out it won't work.

Hypervisors are the software that actually create and manage virtual machines using the CPU's virtualization features.

Popular hypervisors include VirtualBox,free and great for beginners,VMware Workstation,more professional with advanced features,VMware Player,free,simpler version,Hyper-V,Microsoft's built-in Windows Pro and Enterprise,and Parallels,popular on Mac.

These all require CPU virtualization to be enabled.

Some hypervisors will start without it but run terribly slow.

Others like Hyper-V simply won't work at all without virtualization enabled.

Enable it in BIOS,then install the hypervisor of your choice.

If you are using Windows 10 Pro Enterprise or Windows 11 Pro,you have access to Hyper-V,Microsoft's built-in virtualization platform.

Hyper-V is actually really good.

It's what Microsoft uses internally and what Azure Cloud Services run on.

However,Hyper-V has strict requirements.

You need CPU virtualization enabled in BIOS,you need 64-bit Windows,you need a 64-bit CPU with SLAT,second-level address translation.

Most modern CPUs have this,and you need at least 4GB of RAM,though 8 or more is recommended.

Once enabled,Hyper-V provides excellent VM performance,especially for running Windows VMs inside Windows.

Here's something many people don't realize:Android emulators for gaming or app development also use CPU virtualization.

Emulators like BlueStacks,Knox Player,and Android Studios Emulator run way faster with VTX or AMD V enabled.

Without virtualization,these emulators crawl at unusable speeds.

If you're trying to play mobile games on your PC or developing Android apps,enabling virtualization in BIOS makes a night and day difference.

That frustratingly slow emulator that takes 5 minutes to boot,with virtualization enabled,it boots in 30 seconds.

This is probably the most common reason regular users need to enable virtualization.

Want to get really meta?

Nested virtualization lets you run virtual machines inside virtual machines.

You could run Hyper-V inside a VMware VM,for example.

This is useful for testing complex setups or learning advanced virtualization without needing multiple physical computers.

Intel VTX and AMD V support nested virtualization on recent CPUs,but you need to enable additional settings.

In VMware,you enable virtualize Intel VTX and EPT or virtualize AMDV and RVI in VM settings.

In Hyper-V,you use PowerShell commands.

It's advanced stuff,but it works.

Performance takes a hit.

VMs inside VMs are slower,but it's still usable for testing and learning.

If virtualization isn't working,here's your troubleshooting checklist.First,verify CPU support.

Not all CPUs have VTX or AMDV,though anything from the last 10 years probably does.

Second,enable virtualization in BIOS or UEFI.

This is the most common issue.

Third,disable Hyper-V if you want to use VMware or VirtualBox.

Hyper-V takes exclusive control and can prevent other hypervisors from working.

Fourth,check for BIOS updates.

Some older BIOS versions have buggy virtualization implementations.

Fifth,verify in Task Manager that virtualization shows as enabled.

Most virtualization problems come down to forgetting to enable it in BIOS or conflicts between hypervisors.

That's virtualization support.

Remember,virtualization lets you run multiple operating systems simultaneously using virtual machines.

Intel CPUs need VTX enabled,AMD CPUs need AMD V or SVM enabled.

Find these settings in BIOS or UEFI under Advanced or CPU configuration sections.

Hardware virtualization makes VMs run much faster than software-only virtualization.

Check Task Manager Performance tab to verify virtualization is enabled in Windows.

Popular hypervisors include VirtualBox,VMware,Hyper-V and others.

They all need CPU virtualization enabled.

Android emulators also benefit hugely from virtualization support.

If VMs aren't working,double check BIOS settings and ensure only one hypervisor is active at a time.

Next,we'll explore hardware encryption with TPM and HSM modules.

See you there.

152. 硬件加密：TPM 与 HSM

大家好，我们之前提到了TPM，但现在让我们深入探讨硬件加密，即使用专用硬件芯片来处理加密，而不是仅依赖软件。

我们将更深入地介绍可信平台模块即TPM，并引入硬件安全模块即HSM，它是TPM的企业级大哥。

硬件加密比软件加密安全得多，因为密钥永远不会以软件可以访问的形式存在。

让我们探索这些技术如何在硬件层面保护你的数据。

软件加密不错，但它存在漏洞。

存储在软件内存中的加密密钥可能会被复杂的恶意软件提取，或者通过冷启动攻击，即攻击者冻结内存并在关机后读取，以及内存转储技术来获取。

硬件加密通过将密钥存储在防篡改的硬件中来解决这个问题，该硬件与你的主系统在物理上是分离的。

密钥永远不会离开这个安全芯片。

加密和解密都在芯片内部进行。

这使得攻击的难度呈指数级增加。

这就像把密码写在便利贴上与把它锁在保险箱里的区别。

硬件加密就是那个保险箱。
