英文原文

Hey everyone,capacitors are small cylindrical components on motherboards that help stabilize and smooth power delivery.

They are supposed to have flat tops and clean surfaces.

If you see bulging,leaking or burst capacitors,that's a serious sign the motherboard is failing or already unstable.

This is one of the few cases where a visual inspection can directly confirm a likely hardware cause.

Capacitor failure can cause random restarts,boot problems,instability under load or systems that suddenly won't power on.

Today we'll learn what capacitors do,what failure looks like and what your realistic repair options are.

This is a classic older hardware troubleshooting topic but it still shows up.

Capacitors store and release electrical energy to keep power delivery smooth and stable.

Think of them like little shock absorbers for electricity,helping prevent sudden voltage dips and spikes from affecting sensitive components.

Motherboards have many capacitors,especially around areas that feed power to high demand components like the CPU.

When capacitors work correctly,the system receives stable power and runs reliably.

When they fail,power becomes unstable and instability causes crashes and strange behavior.

This is why capacitor problems can look random even though the cause is physical and consistent.

They are small components with a big impact on stability.

Healthy capacitors typically have flat tops and no residue around them.

Failed capacitors may look swollen with the top bulging like a dome instead of being flat.

Some will leak brown or orange residue and some may split open at the top like they burst.You may also see the capacitor leaning slightly if the base has deformed.

The best inspection method is looking from the side so you can compare tops across multiple capacitors.

If you see a cluster of bulging capacitors near the CPU area,that's a strong sign the board is failing.

Visual confirmation is a powerful clue because it doesn't depend on software logs or guesswork.

Bad capacitors can cause a wide range of instability.

Systems may crash under load,reboot randomly or fail to boot reliably.

You might see issues that worsen over time because capacitor health degrades gradually.

Some systems become sensitive to heavy CPU workloads because the power delivery becomes unstable when demand increases.

You may also see post problems or power on issues depending on where the failing capacitors are located.

The key is that symptoms often feel inconsistent.

It works sometimes,it crashes under load,it reboots randomly.

If you combine those symptoms with visible bulging capacitors,the diagnosis becomes very strong.

At that point,you stop chasing software fixes and focus on hardware replacement decisions.

Capacitors can fail due to age,heat,and manufacturing quality.

Your notes mention that capacitor problems were especially common in the early 2000s and that even good boards can see failures after 8 to 10 years.

Heat accelerates wear,so systems that run hot or have poor airflow may see capacitor failures sooner.

Older desktops that stayed on continuously can also reach failure earlier.

This is why inspecting capacitors is especially useful when troubleshooting older systems with weird stability issues.

It's a quick check that can prevent wasted time reinstalling software over and over.

Age-based failures are normal in electronics and capacitors are a common weak point over long time periods.

Capacitors can technically be replaced with soldering equipment and the correct replacement parts.

Your notes mention parts cost like$5 to$10,which can be true for the components themselves.

However,it requires real electronics repair skills,desoldering cleanly,soldering properly,and selecting correct capacitor ratings.

If done incorrectly,you can damage the motherboard further.

For trained repair techs,capacitor replacement can be a viable repair in certain cases.

For most IT support workflows,motherboard replacement is faster and more reliable.

The practical question is not is it possible,but is it worth it?

Repair might make sense if the board is relatively valuable,hard to replace,or part of a system where replacement would be very expensive.

It can also make sense if you already have soldering skills and want to repair as a learning or hobby project.

But if the board is old and cheap to replace,spending time on board level repair often isn't practical.

Your notes highlight this trade-off well.

A modern board might justify repair while an old board often doesn't.

Also remember that if multiple capacitors are failing,there may be broader aging issues.

Repairing one part doesn't always restore long-term reliability.

That's why replacement is often the professional choice.

If you find bulging capacitors,treat it like a confirmed hardware problem.

First,advise the user about the instability risk and the likelihood of worsening behavior over time.

Next,make sure important data is backed up because instability can lead to corrupted files or sudden failure.

Then,decide on repair or replacement based on system age,cost and value.

If replacing the motherboard,consider whether the CPU and RAM are compatible with modern boards because very old platforms may force broader upgrades.

If the system is extremely old,replacing the whole computer may be the most efficient solution.

The goal is to make a practical decision,not a perfect one.

You can't prevent all aging,but you can reduce stress.

Good airflow,working fans and regular dust cleaning reduce heat and can extend component life.

Avoid cheap power supplies because unstable power can stress motherboard components.

Keep the system out of enclosed spaces where heat builds up.

Monitoring temperatures and fixing overheating early can prevent stress that accelerates wear.

While capacitors still age naturally,reducing heat and power stress can delay failures.

Preventive maintenance is cheaper than emergency replacement.

This is why cooling and power quality show up repeatedly in troubleshooting lectures.

Capacitor swelling is a visible sign of motherboard power delivery failure and often explains random instability,crashes under load and boot problems.Healthy capacitors are flat and clean,while failed capacitors bulge,leak or burst.

You can technically replace capacitors with soldering skills,but in most IT situations,motherboard replacement is the practical solution.

If you see bulging capacitors,backup data and plan for replacement because the problem usually gets worse.

This is a great example of using visual inspection to confirm a hardware root cause quickly.

Next up,we'll cover inaccurate system date and time,which is usually a simple fix involving the CMOS battery.

212. 系统日期时间不准确

大家好，当计算机持续显示错误的日期和时间时，这不仅仅是令人烦恼。

它会导致登录失败、引发证书错误，并搞乱计划任务。

典型症状是你修正了时间，重启后它又错了，有时会重置到一个很久以前的年份。

这个问题有一个非常常见的根本原因，尤其是在旧式台式机中。

好消息是，这通常是硬件故障排除中最容易修复的问题之一。

大多数情况下，这根本不是Windows问题。

而是主板上的一颗小电池寿命已尽。

互补金属氧化物半导体电池是主板上的一颗小型纽扣电池，它为实时时钟供电，并在计算机断电时保存固件设置。

正是它让系统在个人计算机关闭时也能记住正确的时间。

它还帮助系统记住基本输入输出系统设置，比如启动顺序和某些配置选项。

当这块电池失效时，时钟可能会重置，设置也可能恢复为默认值。

这就是为什么时间问题往往伴随着基本输入输出系统设置被重置的问题。这是一个简单的电气现实。

如果没有电池供电，时钟就不会继续走动，所以当你的个人计算机完全断电时，它就会失去时间记录。

大多数主板使用一种常见的纽扣电池，通常是CR二零三二，看起来像手表电池。

这很棒，因为它很容易找到且价格低廉。

电池位于主板上的一个小支架中，一旦你知道要找什么，通常很容易发现。

在许多情况下，你不需要特殊工具，只需小心操作即可。

因为电池类型很常见，所以故障排除很简单。

如果症状相符，更换起来很快。

这是那种罕见的、便宜的硬件修复问题。一颗小小的电池可能会引起大麻烦。

互补金属氧化物半导体电池失效的症状通常遵循一种模式。

关机后日期和时间重置，基本输入输出系统设置恢复为默认值，系统可能会显示启动警告，如校验和错误。

有些系统会要求你在启动时按某个键（比如F1）继续，因为固件检测到设置已丢失。你还可能会看到安全网站因时间不正确而失败，因为证书依赖于正确的时钟。

如果这些症状同时出现，电池就是头号嫌疑对象。

这是一个很好的故障排除案例，因为症状强烈指向一个原因。

在这里，你通常不需要复杂的诊断过程。

互补金属氧化物半导体电池的寿命不是无限的。

你的笔记提到寿命大约为三到十年，这是一个可靠的实际范围，具体取决于主板设计和使用习惯。

保持插电和通电的系统与经常断电的系统在时间保持方式上有所不同。

长期断电存放的计算机往往最先出现这个问题，因为电池必须承担所有工作。

热量和老化也会导致电池退化。

重要的一点是，这是正常的磨损，而不是用户错误。

电池是消耗品。

更换互补金属氧化物半导体电池通常很简单。

你需要关闭个人计算机电源，拔掉插头，打开机箱，找到纽扣电池，并使用小卡扣将其从支架中取出。

然后，以相同的方向插入新电池，确保其安装牢固。

更换后，时钟应停止重置，基本输入输出系统设置也应再次保持。

主要的安全习惯是先拔掉电源，并小心对待卡扣。

这不是高风险维修，但小心操作可以防止损坏支架。

一旦更换完成，你通常就大功告成了。

更换电池后，系统可能仍具有默认的基本输入输出系统设置，因为电池失效可能已经擦除了它们。

这意味着你可能需要重新进入基本输入输出系统，设置启动顺序，根据需要启用内存配置文件，并恢复任何自定义设置。

然后在操作系统中设置正确的日期和时间。

重要的一点是，更换电池可以阻止未来的重置，但它不会自动恢复你之前的自定义设置。

这就是为什么记录基本输入输出系统设置对商业系统很有用。这也解释了为什么用户有时会说电池修复后启动方式不同了。

恢复设置才算完成工作。

修复电池后，启用自动时间同步有助于长期保持时钟准确。

当Windows同步时间时，它会纠正微小的漂移，并使时钟与互联网时间服务器保持一致。

这很重要，因为在某些环境中，即使是微小的时间错误也可能导致登录问题。

自动同步还能提高系统对依赖正确时间的安全功能的可靠性。

电池在个人计算机关闭时保持时间，而同步在个人计算机开启时保持时间准确。

两者结合，使时钟保持稳定和正确。

这是一个简单的配置，可防止重复出现麻烦。

如果更换电池不能解决问题，虽然罕见，但有几种可能性。

电池支架可能已损坏或接触不良。

主板的实时时钟电路可能正在失效，这在非常陈旧或损坏的主板上可能发生。

在特殊情况下，恶意软件或损坏的系统策略可能会干扰时间设置，因此如果行为可疑，进行安全扫描是明智的。

但在正常的故障排除中，更换电池几乎每次都能解决问题。

这就是为什么它是首选修复方案，而不是最后的手段。

当常见的修复方法失败时，你开始检查物理损坏或更广泛的主板问题。

重启后重置的不准确日期和时间，几乎总是由失效的互补金属氧化物半导体电池引起的。

通常是一颗简单的纽扣电池，如CR二零三二。

更换电池通常会立即修复重置行为，然后你重新配置基本输入输出系统设置并启用自动时间同步，以获得长期的准确性。

这是一项成本低廉、快速的维修，但对可用性和安全性影响巨大。

至此，第二十三部分暂时结束。

英文原文

Hey everyone,when a computer keeps showing the wrong date and time,it's more than just annoying.

It can break logins,cause certificate errors and mess up scheduled tasks.

The classic symptom is you correct the time,reboot and it's wrong again,sometimes resetting to a much older year.

This problem has a very common root cause,especially in older desktops.

The good news is that it's usually one of the easiest fixes in hardware troubleshooting.

Most of the time,it's not a Windows problem at all.

It's a small battery on the motherboard that's reached the end of its life.

The CMOS battery is a small coin cell battery on the motherboard that powers the real-time clock and preserves firmware settings when the computer is unplugged.

It's what keeps the system remembering the correct time even when the PC is off.

It also helps the system remember BIOS settings like boot order and certain configuration options.

When this battery dies,the clock can reset and settings can return to defaults.

That's why time problems are often paired with BIOS settings caught reset problems.It's a simple electrical reality.

Without battery power,the clock doesn't keep ticking,so your PC loses track of time when it's fully powered off.

Most motherboards use a common coin cell battery,often a CR2032,which looks like a watch battery.

This is great because it's easy to find and inexpensive.

The battery sits in a small holder on the motherboard,usually easy to spot once you know what you're looking for.

You don't need special tools in many cases,just careful handling.

Because the battery type is common,troubleshooting is simple.

If symptoms match,replacement is quick.

It's one of those rare cheap fix hardware problems.A tiny battery can cause big headaches.

Dead CMOS battery symptoms often follow a pattern.

Date and time reset after shutdown,BIOS settings reset to defaults and the system may show startup warnings like checksum errors.

Some systems ask you to press a key like F1 to continue on boot because the firmware detected settings were lost.You may also see secure websites fail due to incorrect time because certificates depend on correct clocks.

If these symptoms show up together,the battery is the top suspect.

This is a great troubleshooting case because the symptom strongly points to one cause.

You don't usually need a complex diagnostic process here.

CMOS batteries don't last forever.

Your notes mention a lifespan of roughly 3 to 10 years,which is a solid practical range depending on board design and usage habits.

Systems that remain plugged in and powered can preserve time differently than systems that are unplugged frequently.

Computers stored unplugged for long periods often show this problem first because the battery has to do all the work.

Heat and age also contribute to battery degradation.

The important point is that this is normal wear,not user error.

Batteries are consumable parts.

Replacing the CMOS battery is usually straightforward.

You power off the PC,unplug it,open the case,locate the coin cell battery and release it from the holder using the small clip.

Then you insert the new battery in the same orientation,making sure it seats securely.

After replacement,the clock should stop resetting and BIOS settings should persist again.

The main safety habit is unplugging power first and being gentle with the clip.

This is not a high-risk repair,but careful handling prevents breaking the holder.

Once replaced,you are usually done.

After a battery replacement,the system may still have default BIOS settings because the battery dying likely erased them.

That means you may need to re-enter BIOS and set boot order,enable memory profiles if needed,and restore any custom settings.

Then in the operating system,you set the correct date and time.

The important point is that replacing the battery stops future resets,but it doesn't automatically restore your previous custom settings.

This is why documentation of BIOS settings can be useful for business systems.It also explains why users sometimes say it boots differently now after a battery fix.

Restoring settings completes the job.

After you fix the battery,enabling automatic time sync helps keep the clock accurate over time.

When Windows syncs time,it corrects small drift and keeps the clock aligned with internet time servers.

This matters because even a small time error can cause login issues in some environments.

Automatic sync also makes the system more reliable for security features that depend on correct time.

The battery keeps time when the PC is off and sync keeps time accurate while the PC is on.

Together,they keep the clock stable and correct.

This is a simple configuration that prevents repeat headaches.

If replacing the battery doesn't fix the issue,it's rare but there are a few possibilities.

The battery holder may be damaged or not making contact.

The motherboard's real-time clock circuitry may be failing,which can happen on very old or damaged boards.

In unusual cases,malware or corrupted system policies can interfere with time settings,so a security scan can be smart if behavior is suspicious.

But in normal troubleshooting,battery replacement fixes the problem almost every time.

That's why it's the first fix,not the last resort.

When the common fix fails,you start checking for physical damage or broader board issues.

Inaccurate date and time that resets after reboot is almost always caused by a dead CMOS battery.

Typically,a simple coin cell battery like a CR2032.

Replacing the battery usually fixes the reset behavior immediately,and then you reconfigure bio settings and enable automatic time sync for long term accuracy.

It's a cheap,quick repair with a big impact on usability and security.

And that completes section 23 for now.

213. LED 状态指示灯

大家好，欢迎进入存储和磁盘阵列故障排除部分。

我们从发光二极管状态指示灯开始，也就是那些位于计算机、驱动器托架、外部驱动器和网络附加存储盒子上的小灯。

它们不是装饰品，而是关于存储系统当前正在做什么的快速视觉线索。

有些指示灯表示活动，有些表示健康状态，还有一些是以光的形式发出的警告警报。

最棒的是，即使软件工具不可用或系统无法启动，发光二极管也能工作。

如果你学会了这些模式的含义，就能更快地诊断问题，避免猜测。

今天，我们将学习如何像技术人员一样解读这些灯光。

大多数台式机和许多笔记本电脑在前面板上都有一个驱动器活动指示灯，通常是白色或红色。

当它闪烁时，通常意味着驱动器正在读取或写入数据，这在启动、打开应用程序、保存文件或安装更新期间是正常的。

正常使用期间的偶尔闪烁是预期的，而在执行大型任务期间更频繁的闪烁也是正常的。

警告信号是当你没有进行任何高负荷操作时，它却常亮或疯狂闪烁。

这通常意味着后台有东西在猛烈读写驱动器，比如更新、索引、恶意软件，或者驱动器因反复重试而挣扎。

这本身不是完整的诊断，但它告诉了你下一步该看哪里。

一般来说，闪烁通常意味着活动。

常亮可能意味着持续活动，而熄灭可能意味着空闲，这些通常都是正常的。

但棘手的是，并非每个制造商都使用完全相同的含义。

在某些设备中，常亮可能是错误指示器而不是忙碌状态；而在某些机箱中，颜色比闪烁模式更重要。

所以，在进行故障排除时，你不能只说常亮就等于坏了，你要观察并确认该特定设备的含义。

一个好习惯是同时记录颜色和行为，比如常亮红色或闪烁琥珀色，因为组合通常很重要。

发光二极管是线索，但设备手册才是准确解读的关键。

主要的要点是将灯光模式视为你可以记录的症状。

外部硬盘驱动器和通用串行总线机箱通常有自己的指示灯，而且它们往往更直接。

一种常见的模式是：常亮蓝色或白色表示已通电并准备就绪，闪烁表示活动，红色或闪烁红色表示错误或故障。

如果你在外部驱动器机箱上看到红色，要严肃对待，但首先要从最简单的检查开始。尝试不同的通用串行总线端口，尝试不同的线缆，并确认驱动器获得了足够的电力，特别是对于较大的外部驱动器。

有时驱动器是好的，问题出在线缆或端口上。

其他时候，红色发光二极管是驱动器即将故障的早期预警。

发光二极管帮助你快速发现麻烦，但你仍需一步步确认原因。

磁盘阵列系统通常为每个驱动器配备一个托架发光二极管，这在实际故障排除中非常有用。

一种常见的模式是：绿色表示健康，闪烁绿色表示活动，琥珀色或橙色表示警告状态。

如果驱动器故障或缺失，你可能会在该托架上看到常亮琥珀色或常亮红色。

这很棒，因为它能确切地告诉你哪个物理驱动器出了问题，无需猜测。

在服务器机架中，这节省了大量时间，因为你可以立即识别出故障的托架。

磁盘阵列发光二极管基本上是一张驱动器健康的物理地图。

网络附加存储设备和服务器通常有多个类别的发光二极管：电源指示灯、网络指示灯和独立的驱动器指示灯。

这些设备通常使用颜色编码，如绿色表示正常，琥珀色表示警告，红色表示危急。

有些事情需要注意，但系统可能仍在运行。

这些指示灯旨在用于快速分诊，以便你知道这是需要观察的问题，还是需要立即修复的问题。

发光二极管不能替代管理软件，但它们能让你迅速注意到问题。驱动器活动指示灯也可以暗示性能问题。

如果驱动器指示灯持续活动且系统感觉缓慢，这表明存储是瓶颈。

这可能是繁重的合法后台任务，如更新和索引，也可能是不健康的情况，如驱动器因错误而不断重试读取。

你利用这一观察结果来决定下一步检查，比如查看操作系统中的磁盘使用情况、检查事件日志或运行驱动器健康测试。

发光二极管无法告诉你完整的故事，但它们可以揭示存储是系统中繁忙的部分。

当用户描述一切都慢，而你需要找出是哪个组件受到冲击时，这一点尤其有帮助。

如果发光二极管的行为感觉异常，你要立即调查，而不是忽略它。

如果你看到红色或琥珀色指示灯，不要恐慌，但也不要忽略它。

首先确定发光二极管属于什么：驱动器托架、网络端口、电源指示器还是常规状态灯。

接下来，检查设备文档或管理界面，因为它会将灯光转化为具体消息，如驱动器故障、磁盘阵列降级或温度警告。

然后采取正确的行动，例如重新插拔连接、更换故障驱动器、改善散热或启动重建过程。

发光二极管是第一个警报，而不是完整的诊断。

专业的响应是观察、确认并有计划地行动。

你对警告发光二极管响应得越快，就越有可能避免数据丢失。

这里有一个简单的习惯，能让你更擅长存储故障排除。

在更改任何东西之前，始终注意发光二极管的颜色和行为。

如果你先更换线缆或重启，可能会丢失那个告诉你出了什么问题的模式。

把发光二极管的状态当作犯罪现场的证据。

观察它，记录下来，然后再继续。

如果可能，拍张快速照片作为文档记录，特别是在多个托架看起来相似的服务器机房中。

当你与远程团队合作或升级至供应商支持时，这也很有帮助。

发光二极管通常是麻烦的第一个迹象，记录它们能加快诊断速度。

像这样的小习惯能让故障排除更快、更一致。

这就是发光二极管状态指示灯。

这些小灯提供了关于存储活动和健康状况的重要线索。

前面板驱动器灯告诉你系统何时在读取和写入。

外部驱动器使用颜色和闪烁模式来显示活动或故障。

而磁盘阵列和网络附加存储系统使用每个驱动器托架的发光二极管来突出显示故障或正在重建的驱动器。

214. RAID 故障症状

大家好，磁盘阵列旨在即使驱动器故障也能让系统保持运行。

但磁盘阵列并非魔法，也绝非无敌。

驱动器会故障，控制器会出错，重建需要时间，有时多次故障会接连发生。

磁盘阵列故障排除的目标是尽早识别警告信号，并在阵列从降级但仍运行转变为完全故障并停机之前做出正确响应。

我们将涵盖降级的含义、危急的含义、性能如何变化，以及一旦看到问题该怎么做。

如果你行动迅速且冷静，磁盘阵列问题通常是可控的。

如果你忽略警报，磁盘阵列问题就会变成数据丢失的故事。

降级阵列意味着其中一个驱动器不再正常工作，但磁盘阵列仍在使用冗余继续运行。

这在能容忍驱动器故障的磁盘阵列类型中很常见，比如磁盘阵列一、磁盘阵列五、磁盘阵列六和磁盘阵列十。

系统保持在线，因为阵列可以从镜像副本或奇偶校验信息中重构丢失的数据。

但降级也意味着你在没有完整安全网的情况下运行。

如果在重建之前另一个驱动器故障，你可能会丢失整个阵列。

降级并不意味着没事。

它意味着你是在透支时间。

这就是为什么必须将磁盘阵列警告视为紧急事件，即使用户还没有大声抱怨。

系统在告诉你：趁我还活着，现在就修复我。

当磁盘阵列降级时，性能通常会下降，特别是对于基于奇偶校验的阵列，如磁盘阵列五和磁盘阵列六。

这是因为系统必须不断实时计算丢失的数据，而不是从所有驱动器正常读取。

根据存储用途的不同，你可能会注意到文件访问变慢、应用程序迟缓以及启动时间变长。

这种减速不一定是第二次故障，而是在降级模式下运行的正常副作用。

在你更换故障驱动器并完成重建后，性能通常会恢复正常。

所以，性能缓慢加上磁盘阵列警告通常意味着同一件事。

冗余正在被使用，而这付出了速度的代价。

把减速当作确认阵列正在比平时更努力工作的信号。

危急或失败状态意味着阵列不再能提供冗余，或者根本无法运行。

磁盘阵列零没有冗余，因此任何单个驱动器故障都会立即导致全部数据丢失和停机。

磁盘阵列五可以承受一次驱动器故障，但第二次故障通常会将其摧毁。

磁盘阵列六可以承受两次驱动器故障，但第三次故障通常会将其摧毁。

这就是为什么危急是与降级不同级别的紧急情况。

危急意味着你可能已经处于数据丢失的境地。

在那一刻，备份才是真正的恢复计划，而不是磁盘阵列本身。

磁盘阵列非常适合正常运行时间和容错，但它与拥有备份不是一回事。

当磁盘阵列报告故障时，你的工作是识别确切是哪个物理驱动器坏了。

磁盘阵列软件通常会通过托架号、端口或插槽位置来标记它，例如三号托架或二号磁盘。

许多服务器和网络附加存储系统还会在驱动器托架上显示匹配的发光二极管指示灯，通常是琥珀色或红色。

要避免的错误是拔错了驱动器，因为从降级阵列中移除一个健康的驱动器可能会导致故障。

所以你要确认托架号，检查标签，如果可能的话，确认序列号或标识符。

不要急于这一步，因为准确性比速度更重要。

正确的识别是安全更换的基础。

有些系统支持热插拔，意味着你可以在不关闭服务器的情况下移除和更换驱动器。

这在企业服务器、许多网络附加存储设备和配置正确的磁盘阵列机箱中很常见。

其他系统需要冷插拔，意味着在移除驱动器之前必须断电，以避免损坏或检测问题。

正确的方法取决于硬件和控制器设计，而不仅仅是你感觉怎么做舒服。

如果你在不支持的系统中进行热插拔，可能会产生新问题。如果你在支持热插拔的系统中进行冷插拔，虽然较慢但通常是安全的。

如有疑问，请遵循系统文档，并将安全性和稳定性作为优先事项。

更换故障驱动器后，控制器会通过重构丢失的数据并将其写入替换驱动器来重建阵列。

这是一个繁重的过程，因为必须连续读取剩余的驱动器，以准确地重新创建丢失的数据。

重建时间可能需要数小时甚至更长，具体取决于驱动器大小和系统负载。

在重建期间，磁盘阵列仍然脆弱，因为在重建完成之前冗余度可能会降低。

把重建想象成系统正在重新保护自己，在完成之前，你的风险更高。

这就是为什么重建不是一个随意的后台事件。

它是一个高风险时期。

你的工作是照看它，监控进度，并保持环境稳定。

在重建期间，剩余的驱动器承受着巨大的压力，而这正是另一个旧驱动器可能故障的时候。

许多阵列由同时购买并以相同方式使用的驱动器构建，因此它们往往一起老化。

如果一个驱动器故障了，其他驱动器可能比你希望的更接近故障。

这就是为什么你在重建期间要避免繁重的工作负载。

不要进行巨大的文件传输，不要进行大型数据库维护，也不要进行不必要的磁盘密集型任务。

让系统尽可能安静，以便重建能安全完成。

如果重建失败或在重建期间另一个驱动器掉线，你可能会迅速从可恢复变为灾难。

重建时间是必须小心和保守的时候。

如果阵列完全故障，你有三个主要选项。

从备份恢复、尝试软件恢复或使用专业数据恢复。

备份是最干净、最安全的选项，因为它们不依赖于脆弱的故障硬件。

软件恢复有时可行，但需要技巧，如果操作不当可能会使情况恶化。

专业恢复很昂贵，但对于任务关键型数据来说可能是值得的。

关键的思维模式是：磁盘阵列不是你最后的防线。

备份才是。

磁盘阵列减少停机时间，但不能保证在所有情况下数据都能幸存。

健康的存储策略始终包括独立的备份。

这就是磁盘阵列故障症状。降级意味着丢失了一个驱动器，但阵列仍在运行，你必须在另一次故障发生之前迅速更换并重建。

在降级模式下性能通常会下降，而重建是压力很大的时期，你应该避免大量使用。

危急或失败的阵列意味着冗余已消失或阵列已停机，这正是备份最重要的时候。在更换之前务必识别出正确的故障驱动器，并了解你的硬件是否支持热插拔。

磁盘阵列有助于正常运行时间，但它不能替代备份。

接下来，我们将讨论S.M.A.R.T.故障，这是驱动器在完全故障之前开始死亡的早期预警信号。

英文原文

Hey everyone,RAID is designed to keep systems running even when drives fail.

But RAID is not magic and it's definitely not invincible.

Drives fail,controllers glitch,rebuilds take time and sometimes multiple failures happen close together.

The goal in RAID troubleshooting is to recognize warning signs early and respond correctly before the array goes from degraded but running to failed and down.

We are going to cover what degraded means,what critical means,how performance changes and what to do the moment you see trouble.

If you act quickly and calmly,RAID problems are usually manageable.

If you ignore alerts,RAID problems become data loss stories.

A degraded array means one of the drives is no longer working correctly,but the RAID is still operating using redundancy.

This is common in RAID types that tolerate drive failures,like RAID 1,RAID 5,RAID 6,and RAID 10.

The system stays online because the array can reconstruct missing data from mirrored copies or parity information.

But degraded also means you are running without your full safety net.

If another drive fails before you rebuild,you may lose the array.

Degraded is not fine.

It's you're on borrowed time.

This is why RAID warnings must be treated as urgent even if users aren't screaming yet.

The system is telling you,fix me now while I'm still alive.

When RAID is degraded,performance often drops,especially on parity-based arrays like RAID 5 and RAID 6.

That's because the system must constantly calculate missing data on the fly instead of reading it normally from all drives.

You might notice slower file access,sluggish applications and longer boot times depending on what the storage is used for.

This slowdown is not necessarily a second failure,it's a normal side effect of operating in degraded mode.

After you replace the failed drive and rebuild completes,performance typically returns to normal.

So slow performance plus a RAID warning often means the same story.

Redundancy is being used and it's costing speed.

Treat the slowdown as confirmation that the array is working harder than it should.

Critical or failed status means the array can no longer provide redundancy or it can no longer operate at all.

RAID 0 has no redundancy,so any single drive failure causes total data loss and downtime immediately.

RAID 5 can survive one drive failure but a second failure usually kills it.

RAID 6 can survive two drive failures but a third failure usually kills it.

This is why critical is a different level of emergency than degraded.

Critical is where you may already be in lost territory.

At that point,backups become the real recovery plan,not RAID itself.

RAID is great for uptime and fault tolerance,but it is not the same thing as having backups.

When RAID reports a failure,your job is to identify the exact physical drive that is bad.

RAID software will usually label it by bay number,port or slot position,such as bay 3 or disk 2.

Many servers and NAS systems also show a matching LED indicator on the drive bay,often amber or red.

The mistake to avoid is pulling the wrong drive because removing a healthy drive from a degraded array can cause failure.

So you confirm the bay number,check the label and if possible confirm serial number or identifier.

Do not rush this step because accuracy matters more than speed.

Correct identification is the foundation of a safe replacement.

Some systems support hot swapping,meaning you can remove and replace a drive without shutting down the server.

This is common in enterprise servers,many NAS devices and properly configured RAID enclosures.

Other systems require cold swapping,meaning you must power down before removing the drive to avoid damage or detection issues.

The correct method depends on the hardware and controller design,not just what you feel comfortable doing.

If you hot swap in a system that doesn't support it,you can create new problems.If you cold swap in a system that supports hot swap,it's slower but usually safe.

When in doubt,follow the system documentation and treat safety and stability as the priority.

After you replace the failed drive,the controller rebuilds the array by reconstructing missing data and writing it onto the replacement drive.

This is a heavy process because the remaining drives must be read continuously to recreate the lost data accurately.

Rebuild time can take hours or even longer depending on drive size and system load.

During rebuild,the RAID is still vulnerable because redundancy may be reduced until the rebuild completes.

Think of rebuild as the system re-securing itself and until it finishes,your risk is higher.

This is why rebuild is not a casual background event.

It's a high-risk period.

Your job is to babysit it,monitor progress and keep the environment stable.

During a rebuild,the remaining drives are under heavy stress,which is exactly when another older drive can fail.

Many arrays are built from drives purchased at the same time and used the same way,so they often age together.

If one drive failed,the others may be closer to failure than you would like.

That's why you avoid heavy workloads during rebuild.

No huge file transfers,no big database maintenance,and no unnecessary disk-intensive jobs.

Keep the system as quiet as possible so the rebuild can finish safely.

If the rebuild fails or another drive drops during rebuild,you can go from recoverable to disaster quickly.

Rebuild time is the time to be careful and conservative.

If an array fails completely,you have three main options.

Restore from backups,attempt software recovery or use professional data recovery.

Backups are the cleanest and safest option because they don't depend on fragile failing hardware.

Software recovery can sometimes work but it requires skill and can worsen the situation if done incorrectly.

Professional recovery is expensive but can be worth it for mission critical data.

The key mindset is that RAID is not your last line of defense.

Backups are.

RAID reduces downtime but it doesn't guarantee data survival in every scenario.

A healthy storage strategy always includes separate backups.

That's RAID failure symptoms.Degraded means a drive is lost but the array is still running and you must replace and rebuild quickly before another failure happens.

Performance often drops in degraded mode and rebuilds are stressful periods where you should avoid heavy usage.

Critical or failed arrays mean redundancy is gone or the array is down and that's where backups matter most.Always identify the correct failed drive before replacing it and know whether your hardware supports hot swap.

RAID helps uptime but it doesn't replace backups.

Next up we'll talk about smart failures which are early warning signals that a drive is starting to die before it fully fails.

215. S.M.A.R.T. 故障

大家好，S.M.A.R.T.是你的存储早期预警系统。

基本上，就是驱动器在告诉你：我感觉不太舒服。

与其等到驱动器完全故障并丢失数据，S.M.A.R.T.给了你提前备份和更换驱动器的机会。

这对机械硬盘和固态硬盘都很重要，因为两者都可能故障，只是方式不同。

把S.M.A.R.T.想象成健康指标。

如果数值看起来不好，你就在变成紧急情况之前采取行动。

它并不完美，但它是你防止数据丢失的最佳工具之一。

今天我们将涵盖它监控的内容，以及看到警告时该怎么做。

S.M.A.R.T.代表自我监测、分析和报告技术，它跟踪驱动器内部的健康指标。

对于机械硬盘，它可以跟踪扇区错误、启动问题和温度历史等事项。

对于固态硬盘，它跟踪与磨损相关的指标，比如驱动器寿命已使用了多少。

这些指标有助于估计驱动器是稳定的还是正在出现问题。当某些数值越过阈值时，驱动器可能会报告警告状态，如注意或损坏。

目标不是纠结于每一个数字，而是识别出趋势是否随时间变得更糟。

如果你看到恶化的模式，就计划更换。

要检查S.M.A.R.T.状态，你需要使用驱动器监控工具来读取驱动器内置的健康数据。

许多工具会用简单的术语总结它，如良好、注意或损坏，通常使用绿色、黄色和红色来表示。

这很有帮助，因为原始的S.M.A.R.T.表格起初可能令人望而生畏。最好的习惯是在遇到麻烦之前检查S.M.A.R.T.，比如在定期维护期间或当系统开始感觉变慢时。

如果你只在驱动器开始发出咔哒声后才检查S.M.A.R.T.，那就已经太晚了。

定期检查能给你争取时间的优势。

时间是冷静更换和恐慌恢复之间的区别。

对于传统机械硬盘，有些S.M.A.R.T.属性尤为重要。

重映射扇区表示驱动器发现了坏区，不得不将数据重新映射到其他地方，这表明盘片表面正在退化。

待映射扇区表明驱动器在读取某些区域时遇到困难，可能很快就会重新映射或无法读取它们。

不可纠正的错误是数据读取问题且无法修复的强烈信号。

启动重试次数可能表明驱动器启动存在机械问题。

温度也很重要，因为高温运行的驱动器磨损更快，变得不稳定。

你不需要记住每一个属性。

你只需要一旦认出坏消息即可。

如果S.M.A.R.T.工具报告注意，说明驱动器在警告你，但可能仍在工作。

你的第一个行动是立即备份重要数据，而不是观察一段时间。

一个显示注意的驱动器可能还能坚持几周或几个月，也可能明天就故障。

你无法预测确切的日子。

这就是聪明人会及早行动的地方。

现在就备份，订购替换品，并计划受控迁移。

此外，除非你已经备份，否则避免繁重的磁盘压力，如大规模文件移动、全盘扫描或修复操作。

把注意当作计划内的更换事件来处理。

如果你行动迅速，局面仍在掌控之中。

如果工具报告损坏，这意味着驱动器处于高风险状态。

此时，如果驱动器仍可读取，你要立即备份，并优先处理最重要的数据。你不要在损坏的驱动器上继续运行正常的工作负载，因为每使用一小时都会增加故障风险。

一旦数据安全，尽快更换驱动器。

损坏状态不是也许，而是驱动器正在actively故障。

目标是快速脱离危险区。

这是保存数据和丢失数据之间的区别。

S.M.A.R.T.很有帮助，但它无法预测每一次故障。

有些驱动器会因控制器故障、突发机械故障或灾难性事件而突然死亡，毫无预警。

这就是为什么你永远不要把S.M.A.R.T.作为唯一的保护措施。

即使今天每个驱动器都显示绿色健康，仍然需要备份。

S.M.A.R.T.就像烟雾探测器。

触发时很好，但你仍然需要消防出口和火灾预案。

把它视为一层防御，而不是整个策略。

如果你将S.M.A.R.T.监控与备份结合起来，就能获得更好的安全性。

固态硬盘也报告S.M.A.R.T.数据，但指标更侧重于磨损和使用情况，而非机械问题。固态硬盘跟踪写入总字节数、磨损均衡、备用块和寿命消耗。

许多固态硬盘工具会显示一个简单的已用百分比或健康百分比，代表已消耗了多少额定耐久度。

固态硬盘仍可能意外故障，但磨损指标有助于你在集群和服务器中规划更换。

关键在于，固态硬盘故障通常表现为突然的只读行为、驱动器消失或控制器故障。

监控有帮助，但备份仍然重要。

固态硬盘很快，但它们并非永生。

当出现警告信号时更换驱动器，特别是当警告计数随时间增加时。

如果重映射扇区稳步上升，这是一个你需要重视的趋势，而不是一个可以忽略的数字。

如果驱动器发出咔哒声或研磨声，无论S.M.A.R.T.状态如何，都要将其视为机械故障。

对于旧式机械硬盘，年龄可能是一个风险因素；对于固态硬盘，高磨损百分比可能预示着寿命终结规划。

主动更换是避免紧急停机时间的最佳方法之一。

紧急更换总是压力更大，成本更高。

计划内的更换能保持系统稳定，并减少意外。

这就是S.M.A.R.T.故障。

驱动器健康指标可以在驱动器完全死亡之前向你发出警告。

注意意味着立即行动：备份并计划更换；而损坏意味着紧急情况：立即备份并尽快更换。

关键的机械硬盘指标包括重映射扇区、待映射扇区、不可纠正的错误、启动问题和高温度，而固态硬盘指标更侧重于磨损和寿命。

S.M.A.R.T.有帮助，但并不完美，这就是为什么备份仍然至关重要。

将S.M.A.R.T.用作早期预警系统，而不是保证。

接下来，我们将讨论阵列丢失问题，即当你的磁盘阵列似乎消失了，尽管驱动器可能还在那里。

You don't need to memorize every attribute.

you can't predict the exact day.

You are still in control if you act quickly.

Once data is secured,replace the drive as soon as possible.

A bad status is not maybe,it's the drive is actively failing.

The goal is to exit the danger zone quickly.

This is the difference between saving data and losing data.

Smart is helpful but it doesn't predict every failure.

Monitoring helps but backups still matter.

Replace drives when warning signs appear and especially when warning counts increase over time.

If reallocated sectors are climbing steadily that's a trend you respect not a number you ignore.

If a drive is making clicking or grinding noises you treat it as mechanical failure regardless of smart status.

For older HTDs age can be a risk factor and for SSDs high wear percentages can signal end of life planning.

Emergency replacements are always more stressful and more expensive.

Planning replacements keep systems stable and reduces surprises.

Drive health indicators that can warn you before a drive dies completely.

216. 阵列丢失问题

大家好，存储方面最可怕的时刻之一，就是启动时你的磁盘阵列丢失或根本无法被识别。

数据可能还在驱动器上，但系统无法正确组装阵列，所以看起来就像一切都不见了。

好消息是，这通常是可以修复的，特别是当原因很简单时，比如线缆问题、控制器接触不良或基本输入输出系统模式更改。

坏消息是，恐慌下的操作会让情况更糟，比如初始化驱动器或在旧阵列之上创建新阵列。

目标是冷静地排查故障，并保留现有的磁盘阵列元数据。

今天我们将专注于在不破坏现有数据的情况下恢复识别。

第一步始终是物理检查。

确认每个驱动器的电源和数据连接。

线缆可能因振动、移动或意外碰撞而松动，哪怕只有一个连接缺失，也可能导致阵列显示为丢失或降级。

安全关机，打开机箱，重新插拔串行高级技术附件或串行连接小型计算机系统接口的数据线和电源线。

如果是背板系统，重新插入驱动器托盘，并确认它们咔哒一声到位。

如果只是一根线缆坏了，更换线缆就能立刻解决整个问题。

这就是为什么物理检查要先于软件更改。

许多阵列丢失的情况，仅仅是因为驱动器未连接。

接下来，检查磁盘阵列控制器是否根本能看到驱动器。

如果控制器检测不到驱动器，问题可能出在控制器卡、背板或驱动底座的供电上。

如果是附加控制器卡，将其在周边组件互联扩展插槽中重新插拔可能会有帮助，因为卡片稍微松动就会导致检测问题。你还希望在启动期间访问磁盘阵列控制器设置屏幕，看看它是否在那里列出了驱动器。

如果控制器看不到任何驱动器，你就专注于控制器和物理层问题。

如果它能看到驱动器但看不到阵列，那么问题就在于配置或元数据。

这一步能告诉你正处于哪个排查分支。

主板磁盘阵列的一个非常常见的原因是基本输入输出系统模式更改。

如果系统原本配置为磁盘阵列模式，而有人将其更改为高级主机控制器接口或其他模式，阵列可能会显示为丢失，因为磁盘阵列层不再处于活动状态。

这可能发生在基本输入输出系统重置、基本输入输出系统更新或用户调整设置之后。

解决方法通常只是将串行高级技术附件模式在基本输入输出系统中恢复为磁盘阵列模式，保存并重启。

这就是为什么随意更改基本输入输出系统存储模式很危险。

阵列并没有消失。

只是系统不再正确地解释它了。

恢复正确的模式通常能让阵列立即回来。

有些磁盘阵列控制器在连接带有现有磁盘阵列元数据的驱动器时，如果控制器不认为这些驱动器属于自己，会显示外部配置消息。

这可能发生在更换控制器、将驱动器移动到另一台服务器，或者有时在固件事件之后。

关键是导入外部配置，这样控制器就会采用现有的阵列元数据，而不是将其视为未知磁盘。

这通常是磁盘阵列控制器界面中的一个菜单选项。

危险在于导入了错误的驱动器组，所以在导入之前，你要确认手头是正确的磁盘。

如果操作正确，导入可以在不丢失数据的情况下恢复阵列。

这基本上是在告诉控制器：是的，这些驱动器属于同一个组，请使用现有的布局。

有时，描述阵列的元数据会损坏。

实际的数据块可能仍在驱动器上，但控制器无法可靠地解释如何将它们组装起来。

这可能发生在断电、控制器故障或驱动器错误之后。

在这种情况下，最严重的错误是初始化驱动器或创建新阵列，因为这会覆盖元数据，使恢复变得更加困难。

此时，你可能需要专门的恢复方法，并且应该考虑是否适合进行专业恢复。

你的首要任务是保持当前状态。

不要向驱动器写入数据，不要盲目重建，也不要重新初始化。

元数据损坏是一种情况，谨慎可以防止将可修复的局面变成灾难。

如果一个驱动器未被检测到，根据磁盘阵列类型和控制器行为，这可能导致阵列显示为丢失。

丢失的驱动器可能已损坏，可能有坏的线缆，或者存在电源问题。

你在不同的托架、使用不同的线缆或不同的端口测试该驱动器，以隔离问题是出在驱动器本身还是连接路径上。

如果驱动器已损坏，根据磁盘阵列级别，阵列可能会降级或失效。

如果在其他地方能检测到该驱动器，那么问题可能出在背板插槽或线缆路径上。

这是一种经典的隔离技术。

一次只改变一个变量，观察发生了什么变化。

你的目标是确定阵列丢失是否真的是驱动器丢失。

最危险的时刻之一，就是磁盘阵列控制器提供初始化驱动器的选项时。

初始化通常意味着擦除或覆盖元数据，这对于全新的替换驱动器来说没问题，但对于包含你阵列数据的驱动器来说却是灾难性的。

如果你初始化了错误的驱动器，可能会摧毁重建阵列所需的关键信息。

所以规则很简单。

在绝对确定某驱动器是替换驱动器而非原始阵列的一部分之前，切勿初始化任何驱动器。

如有疑问，停下来核实。

这就是为什么冷静的排查胜过快速点击。

很多磁盘阵列灾难都是由按错一个按钮引起的。

针对阵列丢失的安全策略是：停止写入，确认物理连接，确认驱动器检测，确认基本输入输出系统模式，然后才处理配置问题，比如导入外部配置。

如果仍然丢失，你就考虑元数据损坏，并决定是否升级到恢复工具或寻求专业人士帮助。

记录你所看到的一切：哪些驱动器在场、位于哪个底座、出现了哪些消息以及最近发生了什么变化。

这有助于避免重蹈覆辙，并在你需要外部帮助时提供依据。

主要目标是在恢复访问的同时保护数据完整性。

最优秀的磁盘阵列故障排除者从不匆忙。

他们保持状态，并采取深思熟虑的行动。

阵列丢失的问题感觉令人恐惧，但如果你按正确的顺序排查，它们通常是可以修复的。

从物理连接开始，确认控制器检测到了驱动器，并检查基本输入输出系统模式更改，比如磁盘阵列模式与高级主机控制器接口模式，这些可能导致阵列消失。

如果控制器报告外部配置，导入现有配置可以恢复阵列，但你必须确认是正确的驱动器。

避免初始化陷阱，因为它会破坏元数据，使恢复变得困难得多。

如果怀疑元数据损坏，请停止写入并考虑升级恢复措施。

接下来，我们将讨论可听见的警报，那些来自磁盘阵列和网络附加存储系统的哔哔声和警告，旨在让事情变得更糟之前引起你的注意。

英文原文

Hey everyone,one of the scariest storage moments is booting up and your RAID array is missing or just not recognized.

The data may still be on the drives but the system can't assemble the array correctly so it looks like everything vanished.

The good news is that this is often fixable especially when the cause is something simple like a cable,a controller seating issue or a BIOS mode change.

The bad news is that panic actions can make it worse like initializing drives or creating a new array on top of the old one.

The goal is to troubleshoot calmly and preserve existing RAID metadata.

Today we'll focus on restoring recognition without destroying what's already there.

The first step is always physical.

Confirm power and data connections for every drive.

Cables can loosen from vibration,movement or accidental bumps and one missing connection can make an array appear missing or degraded.

Power down safely,open the case and reseat SATA or SAS data cables and power cables.

If it's a backplane system,reseed the drive trace and confirm they click into place.

If a single cable is bad,swapping the cable can solve the entire problem immediately.

This is why physical checks come before software changes.

Many missing array cases are simply drive not connected.

Next,check whether the RAID controller can see the drives at all.

If the controller doesn't detect drives,the issue may be the controller card,the backplane or power delivery to the drive base.

If it's an add-in controller,reseating the controller in its PCIe slot can help because a slightly loose card can cause detection problems.You also want to access the RAID controller setup screen during boot to see if it lists drives there.

If the controller sees no drives,you focus on controller and physical layer issues.

If it sees drives but not the array,then the issue is configuration or metadata.

This step tells you which troubleshooting branch you're in.

A very common cause on motherboard RAID is BIOS mode changes.

If the system was configured for RAID mode and someone changes it to AHCI or another mode,the array can appear missing because the RAID layer is no longer active.

This can happen after a BIOS reset,BIOS update or a user tweaking settings.

The fix is often simply restoring SATA mode to RAID in BIOS,saving and rebooting.

This is why changing BIOS storage modes randomly is dangerous.

The array didn't disappear.

The system is just no longer interpreting it correctly.

Restoring the correct mode often brings the array right back.

Some RAID controllers show a foreign configuration message when drives with existing RAID metadata are connected to a controller that doesn't recognize them as its own.

This can happen after replacing a controller,moving drives to a different server or sometimes after firmware events.

The key is to import the foreign configuration so the controller adopts the existing array metadata instead of treating it like unknown disks.

This is usually a menu option in the RAID controller interface.

The danger is importing the wrong set of drives so you confirm you have the correct disks present before importing.

When done correctly,importing can restore the array without data loss.

It's basically telling the controller,yes,these drives belong together,use the existing layout.

Sometimes the metadata that describes the array gets corrupted.

The actual data blocks can still be on the drives but the controller can't reliably interpret how to assemble them.

This can happen after power loss,controller glitches or drive errors.

In this scenario,the worst mistake is initializing drives or creating a new array because that overrides metadata and makes recovery harder.

At this point,you may need specialized recovery approaches and you should consider whether professional recovery is appropriate.

Your priority becomes preserving the current state.

Don't write to the drives,don't rebuild blindly and don't re-initialize.

Metadata corruption is a scenario where caution prevents turning a fixable situation into a disaster.

If one drive isn't detected,that can cause the array to appear missing depending on RAID type and controller behavior.

The missing drive could be dead,could have a bad cable or could have power issues.

You test that drive in a different bay,different cable or different port to isolate whether it's the drive or the connection path.

If the drive is dead,the array may become degraded or fail depending on RAID level.

If the drive is detected elsewhere,then the problem may be the backplane slot or cable path.

This is a classic isolation technique.

Change one variable at a time and watch what changes.

Your goal is to identify whether missing array is really missing drive.

One of the most dangerous moments is when the RAID controller offers to initialize a drive.

Initialization usually means wiping or overwriting metadata,which is fine for a brand new replacement drive,but disastrous for a drive that contains your array data.

If you initialize the wrong drive,you can destroy the very information needed to rebuild the array.

So the rule is simple.

Never initialize any drive until you are absolutely sure it is a replacement drive and not part of the original array.

When in doubt,stop and verify.

This is where calm troubleshooting beats fast clicking.

A lot of raid disasters are caused by one wrong button.

A safe strategy for array missing is stop writing,confirm physical connections,confirm drive detection,confirm BIOS mode and only then address configuration issues like importing foreign configs.

If it's still missing,you consider metadata corruption and decide whether to escalate to recovery tools or professionals.

Document everything you see,which drives are present,which base,which messages appear and what changed recently.

This helps avoid repeating mistakes and helps if you need outside help.

The main goal is protecting data integrity while restoring access.

The best RAID troubleshooters don't rush.

They preserve state and make deliberate moves.

Array missing issues feel terrifying,but they are often fixable when you troubleshoot in the right order.

Start with physical connections,confirm the controller detects drives and check for BIOS mode changes like RAID vs.AHCI that can make arrays disappear.

If the controller reports a foreign configuration,importing the existing config can restore the array,but you must confirm the correct drives.

Avoid the initialized trap because it can destroy metadata and make recovery much harder.

If metadata corruption is suspected,stop writing and consider recovery escalation.

Next up we'll cover audible alarms,those beeps and warnings from RAID and NAS systems that are designed to get your attention before things get worse.

217. 声音警报

大家好，今天讲个简短的话题，可听见的警报。有些系统不只是显示警告灯。

它们会一直发出哔哔声，直到你注意到为止。

服务器、磁盘阵列控制器、网络附加存储设备以及一些机箱，会使用警报来提示驱动器故障、阵列降级、过热、风扇故障和电源问题。

之所以设置这些警报，是因为存储问题可能迅速演变成数据丢失，而声音比小小的发光二极管更难被忽视。

目的不是让你恐慌，也不是永远将其静音。

目的是找出触发警报的原因，并修复根本问题。

把警报想象成存储系统在说：我现在需要帮助。

如果你应对得当，警报可以防止停机时间和数据丢失。

并非所有的哔哔声都一样。

开机自检哔哔代码发生在启动过程中，通常指向中央处理器、内存或图形处理器问题，但有时当系统找不到启动驱动器或存储配置错误时，你也能听到哔哔声。

另一方面，存储警报通常在系统已经运行后持续或重复响起，旨在信号表示阵列降级或硬件故障。

这种区别很重要，因为它改变了你排查的方向。

对于开机自检相关的存储哔哔声，要检查基本输入输出系统和启动顺序问题；而对于控制器警报，则要使用磁盘阵列管理工具。还要记住，有些系统既有主板扬声器，也有磁盘阵列控制器扬声器。

如果你误判了声源，可能会去解决错误的问题。

所以，第一步是弄清楚是什么设备发出了声音。

磁盘阵列控制器警报通常由驱动器故障或阵列降级触发。

控制器发出哔哔声，是因为冗余度降低，系统现在面临更高的风险。

通常，警报会持续响起，直到你在管理实用程序或控制器界面中确认它。

正确的做法是登录磁盘阵列管理软件并阅读消息，因为它会告诉你哪个驱动器失败了，以及阵列状态如何。

在确定问题后将警报静音是可以的，但静音并不等于解决。

警报是在告诉你需要采取行动，通常是更换驱动器并重建。

磁盘阵列警报是存储领域中最明确的立即行动警告之一。

网络附加存储设备和驱动器机箱可能会因驱动器故障、磁盘阵列降级、风扇故障、电源问题或高温警告而发出哔哔声。

许多网络附加存储单元还会显示液晶显示屏消息或网页仪表盘警报，以解释警报原因。

正确的做法是检查管理界面，因为它会告诉你是存储降级问题，还是像热量这样的环境问题。

如果警报与温度有关，解决方法可能是改善气流、清理灰尘或修复故障风扇。

如果是驱动器相关的问题，解决方法是识别并更换故障驱动器，并监控重建状态。

这些警报旨在引起快速关注，因为它们通常保护着业务关键型存储。

你要把它们当作紧急维护信号来处理。

最常见的错误是将警报静音后便置之不理。

这会将一个警告变成未来的灾难，因为如果再有另一个驱动器故障，降级的阵列可能会完全失效。

正确的方法是，只有在明白警报在警告什么之后，才将噪音静音。

然后立即修复根本问题。

如果你只静音而不修复，就失去了早期预警的优势。

此外，要记录事件：何时发出警报、系统报告了什么以及采取了什么行动。

存储事件往往是更大模式的开端，比如老化的驱动器成批故障。

警报是你的朋友，但前提是你应对得当。

设置可听见警报是为了确保你迅速注意到存储问题，特别是速率降级和硬件故障。

关键在于识别哔哔声的来源，检查管理界面以获取确切原因，并修复根本问题，而不仅仅是让声音停止。

磁盘阵列控制器警报通常意味着驱动器故障或阵列降级，而网络附加存储警报还可能指示温度或风扇问题。要把警报当作紧急警告来处理，因为在存储可靠性方面，时间至关重要。

一旦处理完警报，就要转向下一个风险：机械驱动器故障噪音。

接下来，我们将重点讨论研磨声和咔哒声，这些是硬盘驱动器即将死亡的最明显迹象之一。
